4H7FrE66De.one_liner: Diversifies RLVR rollouts by sampling first tokens uniformly from the policy's top-N and splitting rollouts evenly across them.
4H7FrE66De.problem: Limited rollout diversity bottlenecks RLVR, and the sharply concentrated first-token distribution is an overlooked source of lost diversity.
4H7FrE66De.method: REFT samples first tokens uniformly from the policy's top-N candidates and allocates rollouts evenly across the sampled tokens, leaving the rest of the RLVR pipeline unchanged.
4H7FrE66De.key_idea: Force coverage of low-probability but similarly accurate first tokens through uniform top-N first-token sampling with even rollout allocation, branching reasoning paths early.
4H7FrE66De.evidence: Eight models from 0.5B to 14B across multiple architectures on mathematical reasoning and code generation under GRPO and DAPO, with comparisons against other diversification methods.
4H7FrE66De.claimed_gains: Consistently improves Pass@1, Pass@8 and Pass@64 across settings; no further numbers are visible in the abstract.
4H7FrE66De.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic that lower-ranked first tokens yield correct, distinct continuations is insightful and that the method is simple, plug-and-play and consistently better across models.
4H7FrE66De.main_concern: Comparison with other diversity-focused RLVR methods (for example DIVER) is missing, novelty is thin, and applicability to base models is untested since experiments focus on instruct models.

grVXhl52br.one_liner: Refusal fragility comes from a small gate of attention heads routing harm detection to refusal, not from detection or emission.
grVXhl52br.problem: Two explanations of fragile LLM refusal (a single residual direction or few heads versus a narrow weight-space basin) do not fit together.
grVXhl52br.method: Decomposes safety into detection of harm, routing through attention, and emission of refusal, identifies the gate heads by ablation over a candidate pool, shows standard feature attribution ranks them wrongly, and tests noise-injected fine-tuning of the gate heads to reduce dependence on them.
grVXhl52br.key_idea: Refusal depends on a thin, non-redundant set of gate attention heads connecting stable harm-detection and refusal-action features, so small perturbations there sever the connection.
grVXhl52br.evidence: Experiments across three model families using head ablation, a comparison of attribution scores against causal necessity, weight-perturbation analysis, and noise-injected fine-tuning of the gate.
grVXhl52br.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the detection, routing and action decomposition is an interesting analysis that reconciles prior safety findings and shows attribution selects the wrong heads.
grVXhl52br.main_concern: The evidence shows only that a few heads are necessary, not that they route a signal, and gate identification and presentation have gaps such as unjustified pool sizes and undefined metrics.

ClRV6QBTCx.one_liner: Learning-theory formalization of anti-distillation showing feasibility depends on agnostic PAC learning hardness and server statefulness.
ClRV6QBTCx.problem: It is unclear whether proprietary API models can provably be protected against distillation, where third parties use black-box access to build their own models.
ClRV6QBTCx.method: Formalizes distillation as a multi-round game with a taxonomy of quantifier orderings (fixed-server versus distribution-free, worst-case versus average-case), then proves positive and negative results for model classes and query distributions, linked to Gap PAC learning and LPN/planted-XOR assumptions.
ClRV6QBTCx.key_idea: Anti-distillation defenses must exploit that the attacker is computationally bounded, so provable defense or undetectable attack follows from the hardness of agnostic PAC learning for the class.
ClRV6QBTCx.evidence: Theoretical proofs only, with a positive cryptographic example and a negative example for Boolean parities and hashed parities over F_2 under uniform query distributions.
ClRV6QBTCx.claimed_gains: not stated; the result is that provable defenses exist for some model classes and query distributions while undetectable attacks exist for others.
ClRV6QBTCx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formalization is clean and rigorous, with a clear quantifier taxonomy and ties to established learning-theory and cryptographic primitives.
ClRV6QBTCx.main_concern: Results cover only finite or Boolean parity-type classes under uniform queries, leaving unclear how they transfer to LLMs, natural query distributions, and bounds that scale with the class size |H|.

NcylgTdPFB.one_liner: PrimalPFN predicts ILP solutions in context from two solved instances, pretrained on synthetic tasks without solver labels.
NcylgTdPFB.problem: Primal solution prediction for ILPs usually trains on solver-labeled instances, which needs hundreds of solver runs of up to an hour each for every problem class.
NcylgTdPFB.method: Pretrains a prior-data fitted network on synthetic tasks in which instances from standard generators are labeled by randomly sampled rules favoring feasible, high-quality assignments. At inference an exact solver labels a few context instances and the model predicts the solution the solver would find for a new instance, without retraining.
NcylgTdPFB.key_idea: Synthetic pretraining episodes label ILP instances with randomly sampled feasibility-and-quality rules, so the model learns in context to infer a labeling rule from solved instances.
NcylgTdPFB.evidence: Evaluation on three problem classes (including independent set) against PS and DiffILO baselines, with context-label interventions, prior ablations and SCIP and Gurobi solver settings.
NcylgTdPFB.claimed_gains: It needs only two solver-labeled instances per problem class covered by the pretraining prior rather than hundreds of solver runs (the abstract is cut off after this).
NcylgTdPFB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cutting solver-label cost through synthetic pretraining and in-context adaptation is useful, with competitive solution quality from two context instances and informative context-label and prior ablations.
NcylgTdPFB.main_concern: The prior is class-specific (pretraining uses generators for the three evaluated classes), so there is no evidence for unseen classes, and controls such as fixed-rule pretraining or pretraining plus few-shot fine-tuning are missing.

yFpANKjW9f.one_liner: AI teammate personalization in Overcooked: initialize from endorsements, learn a player proxy from gameplay logs, then continue task-reward RL.
yFpANKjW9f.problem: Task performance alone does not make an AI teammate a good fit for a player, and preference learning and later task optimization can interfere with each other.
yFpANKjW9f.method: Studies personalization from abundant gameplay logs and sparse noisy post-match endorsements in controlled Overcooked experiments that isolate preference initialization, training partners and reward design. The resulting recipe initializes the AI from endorsements, learns an interactive player proxy from logs, and continues task-reward RL with that proxy.
yFpANKjW9f.key_idea: Task-reward RL against a learned player proxy, starting from an endorsement-initialized policy, preserves a preferred division of labor that other training-partner distributions would replace.
yFpANKjW9f.evidence: Controlled Overcooked experiments with researcher-defined synthetic preference styles, varying preference initialization, training partners and reward design.
yFpANKjW9f.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says the procedure improves both task performance and preference satisfaction in the authors' benchmark without a preference reward, but gives no numbers.
yFpANKjW9f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing how a player acts from how they want a teammate to act is useful, and that separate experiments on initialization, partner choice and reward design are informative.
yFpANKjW9f.main_concern: Synthetic, researcher-defined preferences may not capture real player endorsements, task performance rises while preference satisfaction falls in some settings (such as Distant Tomato Style C), and the paper is hard to parse.

ay3Kkdy3oq.one_liner: Learning-augmented online scheduling with two load caps, or cost comparison against a prediction-free scheduler when rejection is allowed.
ay3Kkdy3oq.problem: Online makespan scheduling on identical machines needs algorithms that exploit predicted job-machine assignments yet keep worst-case guarantees under arbitrary predictions, with and without job rejection.
ay3Kkdy3oq.method: Each arriving job reveals its processing time and a predicted machine assignment, which may recommend rejection. Without rejection the algorithm uses two load caps, and with rejection it compares costs against a prediction-free reference scheduler, with O(m) work per job according to a reviewer.
ay3Kkdy3oq.key_idea: Constrain prediction-following with two load caps in the no-rejection setting, and with cost comparisons against a prediction-free reference scheduler when rejection is allowed.
ay3Kkdy3oq.evidence: Theoretical consistency, smoothness and robustness guarantees plus lower bounds for deterministic algorithms satisfying the same consistency requirement, followed by an empirical analysis.
ay3Kkdy3oq.claimed_gains: Both algorithms are (1+epsilon)-consistent, degrade smoothly with prediction error and retain worst-case guarantees, and the lower bounds show near-optimal robustness and smoothness.
ay3Kkdy3oq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written with simple algorithms, and value the combined consistency, robustness and smoothness guarantees together with lower bounds.
ay3Kkdy3oq.main_concern: The smoothness result is weak because the prediction error is defined relative to a fixed predicted plan, and the gap to the lower bound can be significant in some regimes.

01xQfhQPAk.one_liner: Online Label Refinement corrects RLVR training labels when a sample's predicted answers are historically stable and increasingly confident.
01xQfhQPAk.problem: RLVR degrades under noisy labels because data is wasted when the model cannot roll out the noisy label, and the policy is misguided when a wrong label is rolled out.
01xQfhQPAk.method: Online Label Refinement (OLR) performs self-consistent label correction on a sample when its predicted labels are historically stable and increasingly confident. It is motivated by the Early Correctness Coherence phenomenon, where correct-answer probability rises similarly for clean and noisy samples early in training.
01xQfhQPAk.key_idea: Replace a sample's label with the model's majority answer once that answer's frequency has been stable and rising across training rounds.
01xQfhQPAk.evidence: Six in-distribution math benchmarks and three out-of-distribution tasks under noise ratios from 0.1 to 0.9 with inactive and active noise, multiple backbones, ablations, a naturally noisy BIRD experiment and a theoretical analysis of early learning.
01xQfhQPAk.claimed_gains: Average gains of 3.6% (ID) and 3.3% (OOD) under inactive noise and 3.9% (ID) and 4.6% (OOD) under active noise.
01xQfhQPAk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important, the inactive versus active noise distinction insightful, and the method simple with little extra computation, supported by extensive experiments and ablations.
01xQfhQPAk.main_concern: Baselines are missing or mismatched (for example semi-supervised RLVR methods such as TraPO, or a simple relabel-on-zero-reward baseline), and the theory does not justify OLR's selection criterion.

Ct7Tlz9Cf1.one_liner: Proves approximation, generalization and minimax-optimality bounds for two-block neural operator Transformers on the Frechet-Holder operator class.
Ct7Tlz9Cf1.problem: Transformers perform well in operator learning, but the theory of their approximation and generalization is underdeveloped.
Ct7Tlz9Cf1.method: The paper derives uniform approximation bounds on Sobolev balls with explicit network size, non-asymptotic L2 generalization bounds under a Sobolev sub-exponential input assumption, and a matching lower bound. It extends the analysis to input and output functions observed on random grids.
Ct7Tlz9Cf1.key_idea: Approximate Frechet-Holder operators with a fixed-depth Transformer acting on coefficient sequences in an orthonormal basis (reduction to l2), and match the resulting estimation rate with a minimax lower bound.
Ct7Tlz9Cf1.evidence: Theorems on approximation, L2 generalization, a matching lower bound and random-grid error bounds, with numerical experiments on PDE solution operators showing the generalization gap shrinking with more training samples.
Ct7Tlz9Cf1.claimed_gains: Neural operator Transformers achieve minimax optimality over the Frechet-Holder class, shown by a matching lower bound; no numeric gains stated.
Ct7Tlz9Cf1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory complete and clearly written, covering approximation, generalization, minimax lower bounds and random-grid discretization effects with only two Transformer blocks.
Ct7Tlz9Cf1.main_concern: It is unclear whether practical PDE solution operators satisfy the Frechet-Holder and input assumptions, and the experiments neither verify the predicted statistical rates nor match the theorem's estimator.

YmzE4bTKxM.one_liner: GSD suppresses dominant pretrained CLIP subspace components, found by SVD, to improve generalization of AI-generated image detectors.
YmzE4bTKxM.problem: After forensic fine-tuning, pretrained semantic priors stay dominant in the representation space of vision-foundation-model detectors (termed semantic fallback), which limits generalization.
YmzE4bTKxM.method: Geometric Semantic Decoupling estimates the dominant pretrained subspace from a frozen CLIP encoder with SVD, then suppresses prior-aligned components through a geometry-constrained formulation with strength modulated across samples and layers. A mini-batch SVD approximation amortizes subspace estimation.
YmzE4bTKxM.key_idea: Softly suppress, with adaptive per-sample and per-layer strength, the dominant SVD subspace of frozen CLIP features so detectors rely less on pretrained semantic priors.
YmzE4bTKxM.evidence: Evaluated on two face-forgery protocols and synthetic-image detection datasets, with analyses of suppression strength, insertion depth, subspace dimensionality, inference protocols, and computational efficiency.
YmzE4bTKxM.claimed_gains: Average video-level AUCs of 94.5% (+2.6%) and 97.8% (+3.0%) on two face-forgery protocols, average accuracy of 97.3% (+2.1%) on synthetic-image detection, and a mini-batch SVD with over 15x lower computational overhead.
YmzE4bTKxM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the view of inherited pretrained representations interfering with forensic learning useful, backed by extensive analyses and an efficient batch-SVD.
YmzE4bTKxM.main_concern: Evidence for the causal role of semantic priors is correlational: suppressing only the first principal direction nearly matches the full method, so gains may come from generic dominant-component suppression, and batch-SVD predictions may depend on batch composition.

oqwK0wMbsT.one_liner: Places correlated experts on the same GPU and shuffles tokens toward predicted next-layer experts to cut MoE all-to-all traffic.
oqwK0wMbsT.problem: Under expert parallelism, all-to-all collectives that dispatch and combine tokens take 45% of the training step at EP32 with top-2 routing and 60% with top-6 on eight-MI300X nodes.
oqwK0wMbsT.method: Correlated expert placement colocates experts that are often selected together, paired with a dispatcher that sends each token to each GPU once. Token shuffling, applicable when sequence parallelism shards tokens across the EP group, moves each token during the reduce-scatter to the GPU predicted to hold its next-layer experts.
oqwK0wMbsT.key_idea: Exploit within-layer and cross-layer expert co-selection correlations that routers learn early in pretraining to keep more token-expert assignments on the token's own GPU.
oqwK0wMbsT.evidence: Router-correlation measurements (e.g., 0.8% of expert pairs selected together by 45% of tokens at top-2) and end-to-end pretraining step timing on MI300X nodes at EP32 with top-2 and top-6 routing, using a fused-kernel implementation.
oqwK0wMbsT.claimed_gains: Removes up to 58% of dispatched rows, reduces all-to-all by up to 2.6x, and speeds up pretraining steps by up to 1.41x with no model change.
oqwK0wMbsT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the end-to-end speedups of up to 1.41x are solid and that the routing-correlation analysis is clear and tied directly to the system design.
oqwK0wMbsT.main_concern: The closest prior work (Occult, Semantic Parallelism, NetMoE, HierMoE) overlaps with the main mechanisms but is neither cited nor compared.

XJM5zCwMcm.one_liner: Factorized spatiotemporal masked autoencoder for iEEG with temporal and spatial summary tokens trained through an information bottleneck.
XJM5zCwMcm.problem: Existing iEEG foundation models keep channel-level structure in pretraining and leave cross-channel aggregation to downstream adaptation where labeled data are limited, despite irregular electrode placement across subjects.
XJM5zCwMcm.method: A masked autoencoder keeps channel-level tokens and adds temporal summary tokens that aggregate within each channel and spatial summary tokens that aggregate across channels. An information bottleneck forces reconstruction through these summary tokens, which are then used for downstream decoding.
XJM5zCwMcm.key_idea: Force masked-patch reconstruction through temporal and spatial summary tokens via an information bottleneck so aggregation is learned in pretraining rather than downstream.
XJM5zCwMcm.evidence: Pretraining on 29 hours of iEEG, with cross-dataset evaluation on a range of iEEG decoding tasks (including Du-IN speech decoding), ablation studies, and analyses of which channels and time points the summaries aggregate.
XJM5zCwMcm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a real gap, the lack of explicit spatial and temporal aggregation in iEEG pretraining, and that experiments across varied decoding tasks and ablations support the design.
XJM5zCwMcm.main_concern: The ablations do not fully establish the information bottleneck's benefit, since gains are inconsistent across datasets, and pretraining on only 29 hours leaves the effect of scale untested.

uMm1ONrPQR.one_liner: GHGbench is an open benchmark with company and building tracks for predicting greenhouse gas emissions under fixed distribution-shift tests
uMm1ONrPQR.problem: Existing greenhouse gas prediction studies use different sources and evaluation designs, so model gains are hard to compare and performance beyond the training distribution is hard to assess.
uMm1ONrPQR.method: Releases a company track (32,830 company-year records from 12,087 companies) and a building track (491,591 harmonized building-year records from 12 public programs across 26 metropolitan areas) with a shared evaluation framework. Fixed tests cover random company records, unseen buildings, held-out regions and cities, later years, forecasting, and multimodal models using satellite-image embeddings.
uMm1ONrPQR.key_idea: Harmonize heterogeneous emissions disclosures with provenance and quality flags, and score models under fixed splits that separate the effect of input availability from distribution shift.
uMm1ONrPQR.evidence: A broad range of model families evaluated on both tracks under the fixed tests.
uMm1ONrPQR.claimed_gains: Company-track R^2 rises from about 0.3 with basic metadata to about 0.9 with company attributes, and leading models reach about 0.4 R^2 on unseen buildings when all cities are represented in training.
uMm1ONrPQR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the large harmonized dataset with provenance, quality flags, and fixed splits, and a broad evaluation protocol across entities, geographies, and time.
uMm1ONrPQR.main_concern: Headline comparisons mix metrics (pooled versus city-average R^2), and the company split puts the same firm in train and test, so models may win by recognizing the firm.

F1vSzlgZls.one_liner: Simultaneous optimistic gradient descent-ascent with independent projections at each information set converges last-iterate in behavioral-form extensive-form games
F1vSzlgZls.problem: Last-iterate guarantees for extensive-form games are mostly in sequence form, while behavioral-form guarantees often rely on regularization or payoff perturbation.
F1vSzlgZls.method: Applies simultaneous OGDA with independent Euclidean projections at each information set using ordinary counterfactual values, and proves last-iterate convergence for any fixed step size below a positive threshold in every perfect-recall two-player zero-sum EFG. A parameter-free variant halves the step size until it is small enough.
F1vSzlgZls.key_idea: Compare the behavioral-form dynamics with sequence-form dilated OGDA and control the extra correction term from ordinary counterfactual values, proving convergence without regularization or perturbation.
F1vSzlgZls.evidence: Convergence proofs for perfect-recall two-player zero-sum extensive-form games plus experiments on benchmark games that are consistent with last-iterate convergence.
F1vSzlgZls.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract gives last-iterate convergence for any fixed step size below a positive threshold, with no rate or figures)
F1vSzlgZls.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that last-iterate convergence of independent behavioral OGDA without regularization or reach-probability lower bounds is a substantive, non-trivial result with a simple update.
F1vSzlgZls.main_concern: The guarantee is asymptotic with no finite-time rate, and experimental performance is comparable to or slightly worse than baselines on benchmark games.

ImZpSvoiEO.one_liner: Sharper analysis of sub-sampling algorithms gives near-minimax regret for K-armed bandits with A optimal arms, plus a non-adaptivity lower bound
ImZpSvoiEO.problem: Prior sub-sampling algorithms for bandits with multiple optimal arms have a looser O~(sqrt(KT/A)) regret bound, and the role of knowing the number of optimal arms A is unclear.
ImZpSvoiEO.method: Provides a sharper analysis of previous sub-sampling algorithms (De Heide et al., 2021; Zhu & Nowak, 2020) and a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors. It also shows that algorithms near-optimal for one number of optimal arms must incur substantially larger regret for a smaller number.
ImZpSvoiEO.key_idea: Tighten the regret analysis of sub-sampling algorithms to a (K-A)/sqrt(KA) rate, and prove a matching lower bound and an impossibility result for adapting to unknown A.
ImZpSvoiEO.evidence: Theory only: an upper bound, a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors, and a non-adaptivity lower bound.
ImZpSvoiEO.claimed_gains: Minimax regret O~(((K-A)/sqrt(KA)) sqrt(T)), improving the previous O~(sqrt(KT/A)) and matching a lower bound up to logarithmic factors over the full range 1 <= A <= K-1.
ImZpSvoiEO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a tight minimax characterization across the full range of A, the non-adaptivity result, and a clear, well-written paper.
ImZpSvoiEO.main_concern: The improvement over prior work matters mainly when almost all arms are optimal, and the upper-bound analysis is a limited refinement of existing algorithms.

Hx3GpkaQ5T.one_liner: Multilingual long-form audio QA benchmark with 5,038 questions over 1,732 recordings in 16 languages, audited in multiple tiers.
Hx3GpkaQ5T.problem: Long-form audio performance is summarized by context length and aggregate accuracy, which hides how language, evidence, and task jointly shape difficulty.
Hx3GpkaQ5T.method: Builds open-ended questions over in-the-wild recordings with a balanced Language x Domain semantic track and a complementary acoustic track, using evidence-grounded generation, shortcut checks, and language-expert review. It then evaluates eleven audio-language models with diagnostics of language, evidence, and temporal performance.
Hx3GpkaQ5T.key_idea: Fix question counts per Language x Domain cell on native recordings, with a separate acoustic track and multi-tier auditing, so difficulty can be analyzed conditionally on language, domain, and task.
Hx3GpkaQ5T.evidence: Eleven audio-language models evaluated on 5,038 questions over 1,732 recordings (1,341 hours, 16 languages, eight domains), with targeted diagnostics; reviewers also cite 94.2% judge-human agreement.
Hx3GpkaQ5T.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports no model scores, only that language rankings change across domains and tasks and that precise clock alignment and factual grounding of acoustic events remain fragile.
Hx3GpkaQ5T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is broad (16 languages, eight domains), with a principled dual-track design on naturally occurring recordings and useful diagnostic insights beyond aggregate accuracy.
Hx3GpkaQ5T.main_concern: Novelty over existing long-audio benchmarks is not shown empirically, and cross-lingual comparability is confounded because languages use different recordings, with very small per-cell samples.

PgihJ5B0yl.one_liner: Class-wise sparse temporal pooling plus bag-constrained soft-target propagation lets MIL localize classes in time from class-set labels.
PgihJ5B0yl.problem: Bag-level accuracy in time-series multiple instance learning does not imply temporal localization, because knowing which classes occur does not determine when they occur.
PgihJ5B0yl.method: StepMIL bases each class prediction on a few timesteps selected for that class (class-wise sparse temporal pooling). It adds Local Soft-Target Propagation (LSTP), which propagates bag-constrained soft targets between neighboring timesteps weighted by source reliability and edge affinity, and is used only during training.
PgihJ5B0yl.key_idea: Select sparse evidence separately for each class, and supervise timesteps outside that evidence with soft targets propagated between neighbors under the bag-label constraint.
PgihJ5B0yl.evidence: Six datasets from human activity recognition, sleep staging and electrocardiography, with bags of up to 90,000 instances, compared against five MIL methods for bag classification.
PgihJ5B0yl.claimed_gains: Attains the highest instance macro-F1 and Cohen's kappa on every dataset and the highest bag mAP on five of the six datasets.
PgihJ5B0yl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between bag-level recognition and instance-level localization is well motivated and that StepMIL outperforms competitors in instance-level classification across six datasets.
PgihJ5B0yl.main_concern: Novelty is questioned because sparse selection of informative instances resembles attention-based MIL and top-k weakly supervised localization, and the formal proposition shows only non-identifiability, not model quality.

LFihwmgCfn.one_liner: Benchmarks commercial and open-source coding agents on DREAM computational-biology challenges against historical human team leaderboards.
LFihwmgCfn.problem: Benchmarks with pre-specified answers show whether an agent is correct but not whether it is competitive with domain experts on an open problem.
LFihwmgCfn.method: A living, extensible benchmark of AI agents on DREAM Challenges (hidden test data, expert-crafted scoring, human leaderboards) that varies the context given to agents, audits traces for leaked-data exploitation, and compares three test-time optimization methods on one task.
LFihwmgCfn.key_idea: Score agents end to end on crowdsourced challenges with hidden test data and compare them with human team leaderboards, auditing traces for leakage.
LFihwmgCfn.evidence: DREAM Challenge computational-biology tasks with repeated runs and several prompt and context settings, against historical human leaderboards.
LFihwmgCfn.claimed_gains: Under guided prompts the agents' mean score never surpasses the human best, though individual runs did on 2 tasks, and no statistically significant gains were found from more context.
LFihwmgCfn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value real computational-biology tasks with historical leaderboards, repeated runs and audits of leakage.
LFihwmgCfn.main_concern: The optimization experiment reuses the same holdout for feedback and final scoring (overfitting risk), and web search, context manipulation and task exclusions confound the human comparison.

zLbnx9Cx5b.one_liner: Identifies successor-error amplification in TD learning and suppresses successor shift while preserving TD update norm, adaptively.
zLbnx9Cx5b.problem: With function approximation, a TD update changes the successor's prediction, which also appears in the bootstrap target, so the successor's value error can amplify itself.
zLbnx9Cx5b.method: SSC-TD suppresses successor shift while preserving the norm of the TD update. The adaptive version estimates the shift's average effect on the successor's squared value error and activates suppression when the estimate indicates harm.
zLbnx9Cx5b.key_idea: Constrain the TD update to suppress its effect on the successor's prediction while keeping update norm, switched on by an estimate of harm.
zLbnx9Cx5b.evidence: A result that on deterministic chains the TD update can increase the successor's expected squared error, controlled chain experiments, and Atari experiments.
zLbnx9Cx5b.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract says only that adaptive SSC-TD lowers lifetime MSE relative to TD on a majority of Atari environments).
zLbnx9Cx5b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the amplification mechanism clearly analyzed, with a simple method and an adaptive variant motivated by when the effect is harmful.
zLbnx9Cx5b.main_concern: The contribution is overstated since the mechanism appears in Sutton and Barto and SSC-TD resembles Constrained TD, and Atari evidence uses one trajectory per game.

iHUB7Hxryt.one_liner: Training-free post-sampling correction that restores per-band power and realigns the feature-space mean of few-step diffusion samples.
iHUB7Hxryt.problem: Few-step diffusion samples deviate systematically from many-step runs through lost power across frequency bands and a feature-space mean shift.
iHUB7Hxryt.method: In a spectral-then-mean pipeline, ENCORE reuses differences between denoising outputs at consecutive steps. It first scales magnitudes to compensate per-band power loss, then realigns the sample centroid in a pre-trained feature space by ridge regression over those differences.
iHUB7Hxryt.key_idea: Use discarded consecutive denoising-output differences to fit a distribution-level spectral scaling and a ridge-regression mean shift applied after the last step.
iHUB7Hxryt.evidence: Pixel, image-latent and audio-latent diffusion models with several solvers and accelerated samplers, plus ablations and cost tables per reviews.
iHUB7Hxryt.claimed_gains: not stated (a reviewer cites Euler 4-NFE CIFAR-10 FID improving from 67.3 to 24.6).
iHUB7Hxryt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it cheap and plug-and-play with no added network evaluations, and consistently helpful across solvers and three model families.
iHUB7Hxryt.main_concern: Stage M optimizes the Inception-space mean that FID measures, so FID gains may partly reflect metric optimization and lack independent metrics.

wfYyXJq45l.one_liner: Benchmark of 270 competitive-programming problems testing LLM verdict and score prediction and synthesis of executable judge repositories.
wfYyXJq45l.problem: It is unclear whether LLMs can perform judging itself for constructive, interactive and communication problems whose correctness depends on constraints and protocols rather than output matching.
wfYyXJq45l.method: SpecialJudgeBench has 270 problems and 4,540 candidate programs (903 with numerical reference scores). It assesses verdict and score prediction, and synthesis of judge repositories from public specifications, scored on hidden candidates by verdict agreement plus build, protocol and runtime checks.
wfYyXJq45l.key_idea: Evaluate judging two ways: direct verdict and score prediction, and generation of complete runnable judge repositories checked on hidden candidate programs.
wfYyXJq45l.evidence: Seven models for verdict and score prediction and eight model-scaffold configurations for repository synthesis.
wfYyXJq45l.claimed_gains: Findings rather than gains: best verdict accuracy stays below 90% per problem type, execution completion reaches 90.9%-98.8%, and only 42.2%-55.9% of repositories judge every hidden candidate correctly.
wfYyXJq45l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark covers an underexplored capability beyond exact-output matching, with substantial data collection and multi-dimensional evaluation.
wfYyXJq45l.main_concern: The added value of full-repository synthesis over existing checker and interactor generation work (AutoCode, ScaleBox) is not empirically justified.

TtTYMFuZQv.one_liner: Distills world action model future features into a transition operator that modulates a driving planner without the model at inference.
TtTYMFuZQv.problem: Feeding world-action-model-predicted future features into a planner suffers from feature misalignment, closed-loop error accumulation and high runtime cost.
TtTYMFuZQv.method: A compact transition operator learns to transform current scene features toward future WAM representations and modulates the planner through a FiLM-style mechanism while planning stays anchored to fresh observations; a rule-supervised scorer trained with a metric simulator guides transition learning.
TtTYMFuZQv.key_idea: Learn a transition operator from current scene features to the pretrained world model's future representations at training time, and apply it as FiLM modulation of the planner.
TtTYMFuZQv.evidence: NAVSIM-v2 navhard benchmark and zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM, with a DrivoR base planner and Wan2.2 teacher per the reviews.
TtTYMFuZQv.claimed_gains: On NAVSIM-v2 navhard the baseline EPDMS improves by 13.7% (from 48.3 to 54.9), and zero-shot closed-loop on HUGSIM gains 25.4% in a metric cut off in the abstract.
TtTYMFuZQv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is practical, since the large video teacher is used only at training time and the planner stays lightweight, with strong results on NAVSIM and HUGSIM.
TtTYMFuZQv.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate transferred world-model dynamics from the added modulator architecture, and the claims of ego-motion disentanglement and observation-preserving modulation are not supported.

TLuhtJ2fA1.one_liner: Derives a closed-form, image-dependent calibration map correcting probability distortion from compound cross-entropy plus soft Dice segmentation losses.
TLuhtJ2fA1.problem: Segmentation networks trained with compound losses such as cross-entropy plus soft Dice output distorted posteriors, which hurts uses like radiotherapy planning that need calibrated probability maps.
TLuhtJ2fA1.method: By balancing the opposing loss gradients at a stationary point they derive a calibration map parameterized by the image's foreground fraction and attained Dice, and they propose a foreground-conditioned isotonic regression for fitting on held-out data.
TLuhtJ2fA1.key_idea: Balance the cross-entropy and soft-Dice gradients at a stationary point to obtain a closed-form map from foreground fraction and attained Dice to the true posterior.
TLuhtJ2fA1.evidence: A proof that no beta, Platt or temperature map can represent the derived map, controlled synthetic experiments, and experiments on five medical segmentation tasks (primarily one fold) per the reviews.
TLuhtJ2fA1.claimed_gains: Correcting with the derived map alone consistently reduces NLL and ECE versus raw outputs without held-out labels or retraining; no specific numbers are stated.
TLuhtJ2fA1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis gives an interpretable explanation of why compound losses distort probabilities, and the label-free post-hoc correction is practically useful.
TLuhtJ2fA1.main_concern: The derivation relies on stationarity and on approximating region-level Dice gradients with image-level statistics, and its validity for real trained networks and other losses is unclear.

lNC9BOoAzT.one_liner: Single-image compositional 3D scene generation that jointly generates environment and objects in a shared frame, then refines each object.
lNC9BOoAzT.problem: Methods that represent scenes only as collections of objects lack geometric context from the environment for placing objects.
lNC9BOoAzT.method: Scene-Frame Generation jointly generates separate environment and object components in a shared coordinate frame, Object-Centric Refinement refines each object in a local frame with scene context, and Object-to-Scene Distillation transfers pretrained object-generation priors using automatically composed and rendered synthetic scenes.
lNC9BOoAzT.key_idea: Model the environment as an explicit component generated jointly with objects, then distill pretrained object-generation priors into scene generation through automatically composed synthetic scenes.
lNC9BOoAzT.evidence: Indoor and outdoor benchmarks, with training on 125K synthetic scenes and comparisons to a MIDI dataset and TRELLIS.2 per the reviews.
lNC9BOoAzT.claimed_gains: Improved scene-level geometric accuracy over the evaluated baselines; no numbers are stated.
lNC9BOoAzT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling the environment jointly with objects is well motivated and gives a clear, simple end-to-end pipeline that balances scene-level coherence and object-level detail.
lNC9BOoAzT.main_concern: Evaluation and positioning are unclear: CD and F-score do not directly measure object-environment relationships, dataset-size matching is uncertain, and the distinction from PartCrafter is not developed.

ZlgDCbUTRP.one_liner: Video-diffusion-based framework that fits material-dependent physical parameters per object and semantic component for simulatable 3D assets.
ZlgDCbUTRP.problem: Existing physical 3D generation gives limited control over material behavior and cannot estimate physical properties from complex object and part interactions.
ZlgDCbUTRP.method: PhysFit fits physical properties using material-conditioned video diffusion dynamics as references, with windowed fitting and Hallucinated Forcing to separate VDM-hallucinated motion from material responses. PhysComp decomposes interactions into objects and semantic components whose parameters are optimized independently and composed for joint simulation.
ZlgDCbUTRP.key_idea: Use material-conditioned video diffusion outputs as fitting targets, with windowed fitting and a Hallucinated Forcing term to filter nonphysical motion before per-component parameter optimization.
ZlgDCbUTRP.evidence: Experiments on PhysAssets and Google Scanned Objects compare against existing methods using CLIP similarity and physical controllability scores.
ZlgDCbUTRP.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims the best CLIP and physical controllability scores on both datasets, with no numbers visible).
ZlgDCbUTRP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the combination of material-conditioned video priors, windowed fitting and component-level simulation gives a useful route to controllable physical reconstruction, with materials and component motion preserved.
ZlgDCbUTRP.main_concern: Evaluation relies on CLIP and VLM-rated controllability rather than measuring physical-parameter error, and component separability and Hallucinated Forcing lack quantitative ablation.

GTJ8Ug8ddb.one_liner: Mechanistic analysis showing a linear name-origin direction drives recall heads to fabricate birthplaces for invented people and misrecall real ones.
GTJ8Ug8ddb.problem: It is unclear what computes the confident but fabricated facts models give about nonexistent people, and whether that computation also harms recall for real people.
GTJ8Ug8ddb.method: On 402 invented names absent from pretraining corpora, they trace fabricated birth cities to a linear origin direction at the name tokens, test it by adding mean differences between traditions, and use path patching to locate late recall heads. They then compare recall for real people whose birthplace contradicts their name against fame-matched people.
GTJ8Ug8ddb.key_idea: A linear origin direction at name tokens is read by late recall heads that map a name's tradition to demonyms, countries and cities.
GTJ8Ug8ddb.evidence: 402 invented names certified absent from three pretraining corpora, Wikidata and Wikipedia, five open instruction-tuned models, activation and path patching, steering vectors, and 38 famous people for Gemma-2-2B.
GTJ8Ug8ddb.claimed_gains: Models name a city of the name's tradition 0.99 to 1.00 of the time (0.88 to 0.99 strict); adding a donor-tradition mean direction yields a donor-tradition city for 0.51 to 0.83 of fresh names; contradicting-origin real people are recalled at a quarter to a half of the fame-matched rate.
GTJ8Ug8ddb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the synthetic-name design with corpus-absence checks is careful and the finding that fabrication follows name origin and hurts real people is well supported.
GTJ8Ug8ddb.main_concern: The claimed shared recall mechanism is not uniquely established, since the same heads write capital-city answers, effects are weak in some models, and the direction may only encode familiar name pieces.

L4JDIRcSCf.one_liner: Trains informal-reasoning LLMs on teacher proofs revised using verified Lean proofs, so no Lean is needed at inference.
L4JDIRcSCf.problem: Informal outcome-level supervision gives little guidance on rigorous proof structure, while calling Lean at inference incurs recurring formalization costs.
L4JDIRcSCf.method: Lean-grounded Learning has a teacher first write an informal proof, then revise it using a verified Lean proof. A student is then trained by SFT on these Lean-grounded revisions.
L4JDIRcSCf.key_idea: Use verified Lean proofs as training-time privileged information to revise informal teacher proofs, then distill the revisions into a student via SFT.
L4JDIRcSCf.evidence: Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Base and Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct across AIME24, ProofNet, MATH, AMC and Olympiad Math, with controlled supervision comparisons.
L4JDIRcSCf.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-30B-A3B, AIME24 accuracy rises from 45.0 to 55.0 and ProofNet from 72.1 to 80.9 over the natural-language privileged-information baseline; with 30K examples Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Base surpasses Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct on MATH, AMC and Olympiad Math.
L4JDIRcSCf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, the method is simple, and the controlled comparisons (same problems, teacher and SFT setup) support the gains from Lean grounding.
L4JDIRcSCf.main_concern: A key control is missing: the same teacher writing a natural-language proof directly from the problem and Lean proof, without the initial draft, so the value of draft-then-revise is not established.

tHX0Ublg85.one_liner: Black-box prompt learning that co-evolves a router and specialized prompts across heterogeneous task streams.
tHX0Ublg85.problem: Existing prompt learning needs model internals or targets a single dataset, whereas deployed black-box LLMs face heterogeneous query streams that cause cross-dataset interference.
tHX0Ublg85.method: EEVEE adds a router that partitions incoming inputs into task clusters and assigns each to a suitable prompt configuration. The router and prompts are optimized with a co-evolution strategy that interleaves router and prompt learning phases.
tHX0Ublg85.key_idea: Alternate router learning and prompt learning so cluster assignments and cluster-specialized prompts develop together under a black-box LLM.
tHX0Ublg85.evidence: Experiments across multiple datasets with Qwen3-4B-Instruct and DeepSeek-V3.2, compared against GEPA and ACE, plus routing controls and run-variability analyses in the appendix per reviewers.
tHX0Ublg85.claimed_gains: Improves average multi-benchmark scores by 10.38 and 24.32 points over Qwen3-4B-Instruct and DeepSeek-V3.2, and surpasses GEPA and ACE by up to 37.2% and 48.2%.
tHX0Ublg85.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-dataset interference is shown concretely and the routing controls (random, mixed prompt, dataset-ID classifier) support that the learned partition does more than detect benchmark format.
tHX0Ublg85.main_concern: The gain from the co-evolution schedule is not cleanly isolated, since the classifier-plus-GEPA comparison uses different repetition protocols and evaluation covers only static single-turn benchmarks.

SvwubZNI7u.one_liner: Plug-and-play repair of feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting that weights diffusion pseudo-targets by reprojection-based confidence maps.
SvwubZNI7u.problem: Feedforward 3DGS struggles on trajectory-based sparse-view driving scenes, and existing diffusion repair mainly targets optimization-based 3DGS near observed viewpoints.
SvwubZNI7u.method: Starting from a pretrained feedforward model, ConFixGS generates diffusion-enhanced local pseudo-targets and cross-checks them by reprojection against support views. The resulting dense confidence maps guide a lightweight refinement that keeps reliable details and suppresses hallucinated evidence.
SvwubZNI7u.key_idea: Validate diffusion-enhanced pseudo-targets by reprojection cross-checking against support views, and use the resulting confidence maps to weight refinement.
SvwubZNI7u.evidence: Novel view synthesis experiments on Waymo, nuScenes and KITTI with feedforward backbones such as DepthSplat and WorldMirror, with ablations and runtime analysis.
SvwubZNI7u.claimed_gains: PSNR gains of up to 3.68 dB and FID reduced by nearly half on Waymo, nuScenes and KITTI novel view synthesis.
SvwubZNI7u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the confidence-weighted refinement is intuitive, model-agnostic across backbones, and gives consistent improvements over initial reconstructions on several datasets.
SvwubZNI7u.main_concern: SSIM is lower than Difix3D (0.7193 versus 0.7817) without explanation, and reviewers question the confidence smoothing heuristic and whether the contribution is over-claimed relative to existing diffusion repair.

Pj5GxJZUU7.one_liner: Self-supervised goal-conditioned RL that infers waypoints in closed form by spherical interpolation of hyperspherical contrastive representations.
Pj5GxJZUU7.problem: Long-horizon goal-conditioned RL from scratch, with no data, rewards, demonstrations or pretrained models, needs planning that adapts to goal difficulty without a separate high-level policy or graph search.
Pj5GxJZUU7.method: C-Slerp learns contrastive representations on a hypersphere and composes them repeatedly to infer intermediate waypoints by spherical linear interpolation. The representation geometry also sets the number of waypoints for each goal-reaching problem.
Pj5GxJZUU7.key_idea: Place contrastive representations on a hypersphere so waypoints come from spherical linear interpolation and the waypoint count is set by alignment scores.
Pj5GxJZUU7.evidence: Experiments on long-horizon navigation and robotic manipulation, including towers of up to eight cubes, with ablations on fixed versus adaptive waypoint counts and the rotation matrix.
Pj5GxJZUU7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports no numbers; it states success on tasks where strong baselines fail to achieve a single success and that fixed waypoint counts substantially degrade performance).
Pj5GxJZUU7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that closed-form waypoint inference with no extra high-level policy, and adapting the number of waypoints to task difficulty, is a simple and well-motivated idea with strong results on hard sparse-reward tasks.
Pj5GxJZUU7.main_concern: Modeling assumptions are not validated: the orthogonal matrix limits temporal transitions, waypoints are treated as Markov-independent, and predicted waypoint counts are not shown to match true task horizon.

cIlGZca87F.one_liner: Steers frozen diffusion or flow policies with RL over a learned mean shift of prior noise, bounded in typical-shell widths.
cIlGZca87F.problem: Frozen generative policies act well only on noise typical of their Gaussian prior, yet existing steering methods bound noise in raw units retuned per task and need a critic distilled through the frozen policy.
cIlGZca87F.method: Typical DSRL makes the latent policy the prior shifted by a learned mean, so its KL divergence from the prior is exact, and bounds it in widths of the prior's typical shell with one budget across dimensions. The critic sees only typical noise, so no distillation is needed.
cIlGZca87F.key_idea: Shift the Gaussian prior by a learned mean, bound the exact KL in typical-shell widths, and so keep the latent noise typical for the frozen policy.
cIlGZca87F.evidence: Eleven robomimic, Adroit and Gym tasks with one budget, compared on performance versus training time; a noise probe in Sec. 3.1 shows frozen policies degrade on atypical noise.
cIlGZca87F.claimed_gains: With one budget on eleven tasks, Typical DSRL is Pareto-optimal in performance against training time, and baselines that come close train two to twenty-four times longer; deploying the latent mean outperforms sampling on every task.
cIlGZca87F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the noise probe is a useful diagnosis and the method is concise, with exact KL computation, no critic distillation and thorough experiments across eleven tasks.
cIlGZca87F.main_concern: Gains are not clearly due to typicality, since Typical DSRL is deployed with the mean latent while baselines use stochastic policies, and it trails LP-DS-SAC on door, hammer and relocate under stochastic evaluation.

RYcgKdEbb2.one_liner: Forecasts with exogenous variables by inferring, in context, how the target responds to conditions from observed look-back transitions.
RYcgKdEbb2.problem: Prevailing methods encode look-back and future exogenous inputs together and leave the pairing of conditions with target responses to implicit learning.
RYcgKdEbb2.method: InRelCast treats each observed transition in the look-back window as an answered example and each future transition as a new case, and infers the relation for future transitions in context. Reviews describe pseudo-query and reconstruction objectives and conditional parameter modulation.
RYcgKdEbb2.key_idea: Treat look-back condition-response transitions as in-context demonstrations from which a relation is inferred and used to modulate the forecast for future exogenous conditions.
RYcgKdEbb2.evidence: Per the TL;DR, in-domain and zero-shot transfer experiments against baselines for forecasting with exogenous variables; details are cut off in the abstract.
RYcgKdEbb2.claimed_gains: not stated (the TL;DR claims outperformance over baselines in-domain and in zero-shot transfer, with no numbers).
RYcgKdEbb2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing forecasting with exogenous variables as in-context relation learning is well motivated and gives a coherent design with pseudo-query supervision.
RYcgKdEbb2.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate learning from historical demonstrations versus ordinary conditional prediction, and the novelty over prior in-context forecasting such as Chronos-2 and COSMIC is questioned.

CYTPQwpCZi.one_liner: Flow-matching posterior over plausible execution rules lets a world model pick risk-constrained plans and decide when to gather information.
CYTPQwpCZi.problem: Identical tool interfaces and similar observations can hide different execution rules, so a plan safe in one deployment may cause irreversible errors in another.
CYTPQwpCZi.method: VERSA learns a joint rule posterior with conditional flow matching and a rule-conditioned transition model that predicts plan outcomes. It selects a plan under a risk constraint and decides whether acquiring more information is worth it before execution.
CYTPQwpCZi.key_idea: Represent hidden rules as a version space with a learned flow-matching posterior, and pick plans under a risk constraint instead of identifying the exact deployment.
CYTPQwpCZi.evidence: Theoretical upper bounds on execution risk and value of information, plus experiments on retail and airline workflows against ReAct, WebDreamer and RAP, with ablations.
CYTPQwpCZi.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims superior task performance and execution safety in hidden-rule environments, with no numbers).
CYTPQwpCZi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling hidden execution rules for safe tool use is well motivated and that VERSA combines rule posterior, outcome prediction and risk-aware decisions in a coherent framework with extensive ablations.
CYTPQwpCZi.main_concern: The flow-matching posterior is not shown to beat simpler enumeration or classification (airline gain of 0.12 points with intervals including zero) despite heavy inference cost, and recent uncertainty-aware baselines are missing.

DNqLcirNz5.one_liner: Agent benchmark built by using agent skills as blueprints to retrieve artifacts, synthesize sandboxed tasks, and generate fine-grained rubrics.
DNqLcirNz5.problem: Expert-curated agent benchmarks have procedural depth but narrow domain coverage, while crowdsourced ones span domains but lack execution rigor.
DNqLcirNz5.method: SkillForgeBench runs three stages: skill-guided resource and artifact retrieval, skill-driven task synthesis that partitions artifact roles and packages sandboxed scenarios, and conversion of skill requirements into completion and process rubrics for strict requirement-level scoring.
DNqLcirNz5.key_idea: Use agent skill specifications as shared procedural anchors across artifact retrieval, task synthesis and rubric design to scale tasks with deep procedural structure.
DNqLcirNz5.evidence: 842 sandboxed tasks across five professional domains evaluated on eight mainstream agents, with a human audit of 100 tasks and with-versus-without-skill comparisons per reviews.
DNqLcirNz5.claimed_gains: 842 sandboxed tasks across five professional domains reveal a steep capability hierarchy among eight agents, led by Opus 4.8 at 40.9% strict completion.
DNqLcirNz5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 842 executable tasks with real artifacts and combined process-level and outcome-level rubrics are a valuable, well-grounded benchmark resource.
DNqLcirNz5.main_concern: Scoring relies almost entirely on LLM judges whose reliability is not validated against human or rule-based checks, the judge model is unspecified, and per-domain results are not reported.

4ap8KVtAYQ.one_liner: Pixel diffusion transformer without timestep input, trained on spatially-varying noise, that infers per-patch noise levels and denoises patch by patch.
4ap8KVtAYQ.problem: Diffusion models are trained with one noise level per image, and prior spatially-varying denoising needs an input noise map giving the noise level at every pixel.
4ap8KVtAYQ.method: They remove the timestep input of a pixel diffusion transformer and train it on spatially-varying noise; the model predicts the clean image, and the size of the residual after subtracting it from the input gives each patch's noise level. Finetuning adds this ability to pretrained models, including a text-to-image model.
4ap8KVtAYQ.key_idea: Drop the timestep input and read per-patch noise levels from the residual between the input and the predicted clean image.
4ap8KVtAYQ.evidence: Demonstrations of removing strong spatially-varying noise, filling noise-covered regions, outpainting and local editing without masks or noise maps, and finetuning of pretrained models including a text-to-image model.
4ap8KVtAYQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims the finetuned model remains a generator with almost no loss in quality, with no numbers).
4ap8KVtAYQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives a new capability without a noise map, unifying restoration, hole filling, outpainting and editing, with useful analysis separating local noise estimation from local denoising.
4ap8KVtAYQ.main_concern: Residuals mix true noise with model reconstruction error, which hurts performance at low noise levels, and baselines are evaluated outside their training noise ranges.

mdkl5aEJRT.one_liner: Derives step-level confidence from Mixture-of-Experts routing statistics to drive targeted revision and to distill a process reward model.
mdkl5aEJRT.problem: Process reward models need reliable step labels, which currently come from human annotation, rollout-based estimation or auxiliary verification.
mdkl5aEJRT.method: They build routing confidence from overall routing mass, head routing mass and within-step routing variation. RoCo-Rethink regenerates the trajectory after the least confident step, and RoCo-PRM uses a strong MoE to annotate steps with routing-derived scores and distills them into a standalone PRM.
mdkl5aEJRT.key_idea: Treat expert-routing statistics inside an MoE as an intrinsic step-confidence signal for process supervision without human labels or verification rollouts.
mdkl5aEJRT.evidence: Experiments across multiple MoE architectures and diverse reasoning tasks, compared with logit-confidence, LECO and random rethink and with MC-PRM and CPMI-PRM baselines.
mdkl5aEJRT.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims RoCo-Rethink and RoCo-PRM consistently outperform strong baselines and that RoCo-PRM transfers across architectures and tasks, with no numbers).
mdkl5aEJRT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the routing signal is simple, needs no extra verification rollouts, and is tested across several model families with reasonably controlled comparisons.
mdkl5aEJRT.main_concern: Routing statistics correlate only weakly with verifier step quality (Spearman about 0.05 to 0.25), and length or position confounds and direct PRM validation are not addressed.

ApZbWICzRo.one_liner: Explains federated on-policy distillation's learning-rate sensitivity as aggregation-rollout feedback and fixes it with teacher-guided adaptive update scaling.
ApZbWICzRo.problem: Collaboration gains in federated on-policy distillation are obscured because FedAvg can match local training at a small learning rate yet gain clearly at a larger one.
ApZbWICzRo.method: Theory in a solvable model shows aggregation-induced optimization lag delays access to useful teacher supervision for the student's own rollouts. FedTOPS reuses teacher feedback on current trajectories to adapt the FedAvg update magnitude under clientwise predictive-change constraints.
ApZbWICzRo.key_idea: Because the student generates its own training rollouts, aggregation lag slows later supervision, so FedTOPS scales the aggregated update using teacher feedback on current trajectories.
ApZbWICzRo.evidence: A solvable-model theory with a rollout-source swapping intervention, and experiments on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks compared with FedAvg and validation-tuned fixed scaling.
ApZbWICzRo.claimed_gains: Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, FedTOPS improves macro Avg@8 over FedAvg by 7.33 to 14.26 percentage points.
ApZbWICzRo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the learner-and-generator framing is insightful, the theory isolates the feedback mechanism, and the method is simple and cheap (8 to 15% overhead per one review).
ApZbWICzRo.main_concern: Experiments do not rule out the simpler explanation that the effective step size is too small at 1x learning rate, and the advantage over simple server-step adjustments is not established.

dgkarYpfIC.one_liner: Benchmark of interventions that measures which evidence route audio-visual deepfake detectors use, showing training data can redirect it.
dgkarYpfIC.problem: Audio-visual deepfake detectors score near-perfect in-domain but fail unpredictably under distribution shift, and accuracy alone does not reveal which evidence they rely on.
dgkarYpfIC.method: AVRouteBench first applies an intervention-based signature (leading silence, speaker identity, modality skew, generator overfit) to narrow candidate routes, then confirms candidates with direct interventions such as breaking the audio-visual pairing while keeping each stream intact.
dgkarYpfIC.key_idea: Measure a detector's evidence route by intervening on candidate cues and breaking audio-visual pairing, treating the route as a property of the trained instance.
dgkarYpfIC.evidence: A fixed AV-HuBERT backbone with a logistic head under varied training mixtures, matched sweeps, a same-source intervention, a published detector trained on two sources, and 19 detector instances evaluated mainly on FakeAVCeleb.
dgkarYpfIC.claimed_gains: Changing only the training mixture moves fake-video/real-audio AUC from 0.495 to 0.980 with one frozen AV-HuBERT backbone and one logistic head.
dgkarYpfIC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-architecture mixture sweep is compelling and the evidence-route analysis with targeted interventions goes beyond accuracy-based evaluation.
dgkarYpfIC.main_concern: The interventions do not uniquely identify a detector's route, since the signature covers only four cue axes, confirmation thresholds are descriptive, and many of the 19 detectors share backbones.

n6BdPjyxUp.one_liner: Equivariant residue-level model that combines local geometry with AlphaFold2 pairwise features to predict cryptic binding pockets from one structure.
n6BdPjyxUp.problem: Cryptic pockets are transient binding sites invisible in static structures and cannot be found by local concavity alone.
n6BdPjyxUp.method: PocketMon is a context-conditioned equivariant residue field that integrates SE(3)-equivariant geometric modeling with general pairwise residue priors for whole-protein residue-level prediction. The authors also curate and standardize three cryptic-pocket benchmarks.
n6BdPjyxUp.key_idea: Treat cryptic pocket discovery as local-global inference, fusing equivariant local residue geometry with pairwise residue priors to predict hidden binding sites.
n6BdPjyxUp.evidence: Three curated cryptic-pocket benchmarks including PocketMiner and CryptoBank, the AF2BIND binding-site benchmark, ablations, and a human proteome-scale detection application.
n6BdPjyxUp.claimed_gains: Up to 14.83% absolute PR-AUC improvement on PocketMiner over competitive baselines.
n6BdPjyxUp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining local geometry with global residue-pair context is well motivated, with consistent gains across several datasets and supporting ablations.
n6BdPjyxUp.main_concern: The benefit of the geometric architecture is not separated from pretrained AlphaFold2 pair features, with no pair-feature-only baseline and only a small gain on AF2BIND (67.77 to 68.63 PR-AUC).

HAGfaHSbW0.one_liner: Compiles stack-dependent token validity into finite signatures so grammar-constrained decoding masks tokens by precomputed table lookup.
HAGfaHSbW0.problem: Context-free grammars make token validity depend on an unbounded parser stack, which makes online masking in grammar-constrained decoding expensive.
HAGfaHSbW0.method: InstaGrammar compiles stack-dependent compatibility for a fixed grammar and vocabulary into finite response signatures. A first-pop decomposition makes them compositional: a push follows a compiled transition and a pop restores the saved signature, so masking combines precomputed rows.
HAGfaHSbW0.key_idea: Use a first-pop decomposition so each push updates a compiled stack signature in one transition and each pop restores the saved one, replacing stack simulation with lookups.
HAGfaHSbW0.evidence: Per-token matcher cost on MaskBench against XGrammar and llguidance, preprocessing cost, and end-to-end vLLM serving throughput on schemas with heavy online cost.
HAGfaHSbW0.claimed_gains: On MaskBench mean per-token matcher cost is 7.4 microseconds (1.9 with reuse), with P99 of 11 microseconds under reuse versus 422 for llguidance and 1,278 for XGrammar; vLLM throughput is 5.9 times XGrammar's and 2.1 times llguidance's, at a median 0.24 s preprocessing per schema.
HAGfaHSbW0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the first-pop decomposition gives a principled, theoretically supported construction and that matcher latency and serving throughput improve, especially on schemas with expensive online masking.
HAGfaHSbW0.main_concern: The closest prior work, PSC, is not compared directly, and the broader suite shows 2,073 validation mismatches versus 1,664 for XGrammar and 22 for llguidance without attribution.

ClZNdSlbUO.one_liner: Latent diffusion over irregular trajectories that embeds spatial displacement and time gaps between observations as offset features.
ClZNdSlbUO.problem: Irregularly sampled trajectories couple displacements with unequal time intervals, so adjacent sequence tokens do not correspond to comparable physical transitions.
ClZNdSlbUO.method: GeoDiffusion applies spatio-temporal offset encoding that jointly embeds displacement and time interval between consecutive observations, and learnable latent queries aggregate position and offset features so a denoising network reconstructs latents carrying locations and transition scales.
ClZNdSlbUO.key_idea: Embed the spatial displacement and time gap between consecutive observations as an offset feature and compress trajectories into latent slots via learnable queries for diffusion.
ClZNdSlbUO.evidence: Experiments on five maritime and urban trajectory datasets for prediction and imputation, with Jaccard, POR, DTW and ADE measurements.
ClZNdSlbUO.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims favorable aggregate prediction and imputation performance across evaluated settings, with exceptions in individual comparisons, and gives no numbers).
ClZNdSlbUO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and that one framework supporting prediction, imputation and endpoint-conditioned planning with offset features is a sensible design for irregular observations.
ClZNdSlbUO.main_concern: The offset encoding is seen as limited novelty, key inference steps for unknown future displacements are undefined, and main text and appendix are inconsistent (clean-latent versus noise prediction).

323rMmFiY8.one_liner: Deepfake detection MLLM that grounds its first judgment in the best intermediate layer, then reflects via contrastive teacher self-distillation.
323rMmFiY8.problem: Deepfake detection accuracy degrades across successive language-model layers in MLLMs, so detection ability in intermediate visual representations is lost in the final prediction.
323rMmFiY8.method: SeeTR grounds an initial judgment in the most discriminative intermediate representation, then builds reflective reasoning to keep or revise it. CT-OPSD refines this on the model's own rollouts using token-level disagreement between teacher contexts conditioned on the true label and its opposite.
323rMmFiY8.key_idea: Make the first judgment from the best intermediate layer, then train keep-or-revise reflection with on-policy distillation weighted by disagreement between label-conditioned and opposite-label teachers.
323rMmFiY8.evidence: Layer-wise probing on InternVL3, Qwen3-VL and LLaVA, SFT comparisons, and training and evaluation of SeeTR on InternVL3 against baselines including AIGC detectors.
323rMmFiY8.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract reports no numbers).
323rMmFiY8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the layer-wise probing showing stronger intermediate-layer detection across several backbones is a useful finding that motivates the initial-judgment design.
323rMmFiY8.main_concern: Reflection is asymmetric, correcting 1,918 of 4,949 missed fakes but only 25 of 1,777 false fakes, suggesting a bias toward predicting fake, and full training is shown only on InternVL3.

RkTzi4e9Jd.one_liner: Links large spectral norms to a lazy regime that hurts generalization in continual learning, and controls them with spectral parameterizations.
RkTzi4e9Jd.problem: Loss of generalization in continual learning, where a network still fits training data but generalizes worse, lacks a mechanistic explanation.
RkTzi4e9Jd.method: They propose the spectral lazy regime, signaled by large increases in the spectral norm of parameter matrices, and connect large spectral norms to lazy (kernel) training theoretically. They constrain the spectral norm of weight matrices and propose two new parameterizations for finer control.
RkTzi4e9Jd.key_idea: Large spectral norms push training into a lazy regime that inhibits representation learning, so bounding the spectral norm of weights avoids loss of generalization.
RkTzi4e9Jd.evidence: Theory linking large spectral norms to the lazy regime, and experiments with spectral-norm and other norm constraints, radius sensitivity and rescaling studies, and a per-task reset baseline.
RkTzi4e9Jd.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports no numbers; it claims that constraining the spectral norm avoids loss of generalization).
RkTzi4e9Jd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper cleanly separates loss of generalization from loss of trainability and that the radius sensitivity and rescaling experiments are informative.
RkTzi4e9Jd.main_concern: Novelty is questioned since prior work already bounds the spectral norm to preserve plasticity, and the theory does not prove that lazy training causes poor generalization or spectral growth.

fS0g9cK70J.one_liner: Federated multi-objective LLM alignment where each client resolves objective conflicts locally with a regularized MGDA subproblem and sends one update.
fS0g9cK70J.problem: Server-side conflict resolution needs per-objective gradients from every client, while independent client-side resolution yields inconsistent objective weights, called multi-objective disagreement drift.
fS0g9cK70J.method: FIRM regularizes each client's multiple-gradient descent subproblem so its objective weights are less sensitive to perturbations in estimated gradients, and communicates one model update per client. A finite-time bound on the Pareto-stationarity gap separates standard client drift from disagreement induced by client-side resolution.
fS0g9cK70J.key_idea: Regularize each client's MGDA weight subproblem so locally computed objective weights stay stable under gradient noise, drift and heterogeneity.
fS0g9cK70J.evidence: A finite-time Pareto-stationarity bound for a federated multi-objective actor-critic abstraction, plus experiments with PPO and LoRA on LLM alignment, with communication and scalability studies per reviews.
fS0g9cK70J.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract reports no numbers).
fS0g9cK70J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying disagreement drift as a distinct error source from client drift is valuable and that the theory separates its contribution to convergence.
fS0g9cK70J.main_concern: The convergence analysis assumes a linear critic, full participation and uniform aggregation, unlike the practical PPO-with-LoRA setup, and regularized MGDA has been studied before.

SzFsrRf7RJ.one_liner: Face recognition on identity-distilled diffusion latents from unconditioned inversion, with mirrored guidance and quantization, bounding visual disclosure.
SzFsrRf7RJ.problem: Existing face-protection methods are validated mainly empirically, leaving visual information disclosure beyond identity unquantified.
SzFsrRf7RJ.method: InvFace inverts an identity-conditioned diffusion model without the identity condition to get noise-like but recognition-usable latents, then applies mirrored classifier-free guidance to strengthen identity and block recovery, and quantization to make the representation finite-valued.
SzFsrRf7RJ.key_idea: Decompose protection into stepwise transitions (identity-distilling inversion, mirrored guidance, quantization) whose accumulated within-identity variance yields information-theoretic bounds on leakage.
SzFsrRf7RJ.evidence: Recognition utility and reconstruction-attack experiments against prior protection methods, ablations across representation states, and information-theoretic bounds.
SzFsrRf7RJ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims InvFace matches leading prior works in recognition utility with stronger resistance to multiple reconstruction attacks, with no numbers).
SzFsrRf7RJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using identity-conditioned diffusion inversion with mirrored guidance is a well-motivated alternative to feature pruning or learned obfuscation, supported by ablations and a new semantic reconstruction attack.
SzFsrRf7RJ.main_concern: The practical benefit of stepwise privacy quantification is not shown, since a comparable bound might follow from terminal within-identity variance, and optimization-based white-box attacks are not tested.

zASLvxeJX7.one_liner: Multi-task gradient balancing that rotates task gradients toward a consensus direction while penalizing deviation from the original gradients.
zASLvxeJX7.problem: Gradient manipulation methods over-prioritize geometric alignment, which changes task gradients heavily and dilutes task-specific information.
zASLvxeJX7.method: RGB adjusts task gradients by rotation toward a consensus direction, reducing global conflict while penalizing excessive deviation from the original task-gradient directions.
zASLvxeJX7.key_idea: Rotate each task gradient only partway toward a consensus direction, with a fidelity penalty trading conflict reduction against deviation from the original gradient.
zASLvxeJX7.evidence: MTL benchmarks with 3 to 40 tasks (NYUv2, Cityscapes, CelebA, QM9 per reviews), and ablations on the degree of rotation.
zASLvxeJX7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims competitive results across benchmarks ranging from 3 to 40 tasks, with no performance numbers).
zASLvxeJX7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the alignment-versus-fidelity framing is clear and the method gives competitive results across the evaluated multi-task benchmarks.
zASLvxeJX7.main_concern: The theory is seen as overshooting what is proved, results depend on per-dataset alpha-step tuning, and scalability and runtime cost with many tasks are not established.

x1NH6UPJie.one_liner: Anchor-regularized FTRL repeatedly solves a game regularized toward an anchor strategy, giving faster last-iterate rates under stochastic and bandit feedback.
x1NH6UPJie.problem: Uncoupled learning in two-player zero-sum matrix games with stochastic feedback has slow last-iterate rates, notably Otilde(t^-1/4) under bandit feedback.
x1NH6UPJie.method: AR-FTRL repeatedly solves the game regularized toward an anchor strategy profile and updates the anchor to each solution. The analysis uses metric subregularity of the bilinear structure so the regularized equilibrium contracts toward the Nash set at each anchor update.
x1NH6UPJie.key_idea: Re-anchor the regularizer at each solution so the regularized equilibrium contracts toward the Nash set by a constant factor per anchor update.
x1NH6UPJie.evidence: Theoretical guarantees for noisy-gradient feedback and for bandit feedback under a unique fully mixed Nash equilibrium; no experiments are mentioned.
x1NH6UPJie.claimed_gains: The last-strategy L2 gap converges at rate Otilde(T^-1/2) at anchor updates, faster than the Otilde(t^-1/4) of every-round guarantees under bandit feedback.
x1NH6UPJie.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and improves the bandit-feedback last-iterate rate to Otilde(T^-1/2) while handling an importance-weighted estimator with unbounded variance.
x1NH6UPJie.main_concern: The rate holds only at anchor updates, depends on a problem-dependent subregularity constant and a unique fully mixed equilibrium, and may not be comparable to every-round guarantees or checkpoint-averaged baselines.

XfFQngfAoh.one_liner: External associative memory for LLM systems that stores immutable episodes and binds recurring concepts to them for cue-driven recall.
XfFQngfAoh.problem: New and old evidence compete within finite retrieval and context budgets, so an LLM system that keeps every document can still lose the ability to use earlier knowledge.
XfFQngfAoh.method: Memini keeps each observation as an immutable source episode, with query-independent updates that bind recurring concepts to episodes and accumulate co-observations across them. At query time partial cues follow bounded associative routes to recover source episodes, alone or combined with dense retrieval.
XfFQngfAoh.key_idea: Bind recurring concepts to immutable source episodes through accumulated co-observations, and recover episodes along bounded associative routes from partial cues.
XfFQngfAoh.evidence: Streams built from MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA measuring acquisition, retention and cross-arrival use of evidence, against HippoRAG2 and dense retrieval, with a concept-shuffling ablation.
XfFQngfAoh.claimed_gains: With matched models, hybrid readout reduces mean answer-F1 forgetting by 44 to 64% relative to HippoRAG2's released incremental path, and improves cross-arrival answer F1 by 1.44 to 7.71 points over dense retrieval alone.
XfFQngfAoh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the protocol separating acquisition, retention and cross-arrival recombination is careful and that the shuffling control shows the stored organization matters beyond keeping the source archive.
XfFQngfAoh.main_concern: The continual-learning framing is seen as overstated, the HippoRAG2 comparison is confounded by writer model strength (GPT-5.4 versus 4o-mini), and gains over dense retrieval are small or not significant.

zPOL1SdLC9.one_liner: Selects Cauchy, tanh-derived and Gaussian features from a dictionary using PDE residuals, then freezes and refits them for PINNs.
zPOL1SdLC9.problem: Finite-size physics-informed networks must represent distinct spatial structures, such as rational-wave poles, that a single activation family handles poorly.
zPOL1SdLC9.method: CAPINN uses PDE residuals to jointly select feature families, locations and scales from a supplied Cauchy, tanh-derived and Gaussian dictionary, freezes the selected geometry, jointly refits coefficients, and reconstructs bases across time intervals without interior solution labels, with GPU-parallel candidate evaluation.
zPOL1SdLC9.key_idea: Greedy, residual-guided selection of heterogeneous basis functions from a dictionary, so the chosen Cauchy components match the solution's analytic pole structure.
zPOL1SdLC9.evidence: One- and two-dimensional PDEs and structured 5D to 100D radial benchmarks, with ablations removing Cauchy features and comparing fixed or random construction against residual-guided construction.
zPOL1SdLC9.claimed_gains: Relative L2 errors below 1e-6 on Benjamin-Ono and Peregrine rational waves, and 0.023% vector-velocity error on 2D sine-lid cavity flow versus 0.152% for parameter-matched Physics-Informed Gaussians.
zPOL1SdLC9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that matching feature form to solution structure is well motivated and that the representation ablations and negative controls convincingly support the residual-driven construction.
zPOL1SdLC9.main_concern: The comparison confounds representation with tuning and sampling, since CAPINN is tuned per problem against untuned single-seed baselines and adaptive collocation methods are missing, and the benchmark roster favors Cauchy structure.

dgirdRlD7Y.one_liner: Test-time prompt-tuning regularizer pushing apart only class features whose cosine exceeds the attainable bound for N classes in D dimensions.
dgirdRlD7Y.problem: Entropy-minimizing test-time prompt tuning of CLIP makes the model over-confident and collapses when the prompt is carried along a test stream, because it pulls together competing classes.
