dgirdRlD7Y.method: AGI-TPT adds a regularizer that pushes apart only class-feature pairs whose cosine exceeds c-star(N,D), the smallest largest-cosine that N unit vectors in D dimensions can attain, and applies no force below it. The level is computed from N and D rather than tuned.
dgirdRlD7Y.key_idea: Penalize only class-feature pairs whose cosine exceeds the geometrically attainable bound for N classes in D dimensions, computed rather than tuned.
dgirdRlD7Y.evidence: Theory for freely optimizable class vectors (zeroes of the loss are maximally separated configurations), single-step strength-matched comparisons, and online adaptation experiments across multiple CLIP backbones with ablations and label-shift tests.
dgirdRlD7Y.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract gives no headline accuracy or calibration numbers; it notes only that at a single step a random reversal of TPT's step of the same strength comes within 0.13 ECE of it).
dgirdRlD7Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating single-step strength effects from sustained class-geometry effects is a useful insight, backed by matched-strength controls and online experiments.
dgirdRlD7Y.main_concern: The guarantees concern freely optimizable class vectors rather than shared prompts, and one-step ECE of AGI-TPT and strength-adjusted O-TPT is similar (1.81% versus 1.86%), leaving the independent benefit of the geometry less clear.

jUNY4Kw6Wr.one_liner: Attributes multi-agent failures by scoring steps with a temporal graph encoder, then an LLM predicts the error-source set.
jUNY4Kw6Wr.problem: Existing failure attribution identifies a single responsible agent or step, overlooking multiple intertwined error sources in one failed multi-agent execution.
jUNY4Kw6Wr.method: GAMA represents each execution as a temporal graph with dependency and same-agent relations, and a graph encoder combines upstream dependencies and downstream consequences into source-error scores. These scores guide an LLM to predict the final attribution set, evaluated on the new Whos & Whens benchmark.
jUNY4Kw6Wr.key_idea: Use graph-encoder source-error scores over a temporal dependency graph to guide an LLM in separating originating errors from propagated ones.
jUNY4Kw6Wr.evidence: The new Whos & Whens benchmark with step-level multi-source annotations built by context-dependent error injection, plus single-source benchmarks, across three LLM backbones and ablations.
jUNY4Kw6Wr.claimed_gains: On Whos & Whens, GAMA improves exact match by 7.58% over the best baseline across three LLM backbones.
jUNY4Kw6Wr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-source formulation distinguishing source from propagated errors is well motivated and that gains hold across LLM backbones and benchmarks.
jUNY4Kw6Wr.main_concern: Design choices (GNN, LLM scorer, dependency-edge extraction) are not justified against simpler alternatives, and there is no per-domain, per-source-count or out-of-distribution evaluation.

bFpC2Q9vIb.one_liner: Certifies minimal sets of reward and value predictions that preserve a world-model planner's decision by re-executing the planner natively.
bFpC2Q9vIb.problem: Explanations scored on recorded planner computation ignore how search adapts to replaced predictions, and a single passing set leaves minimum size, alternatives and reliability unresolved.
bFpC2Q9vIb.method: FutureCert intervenes on recorded and newly visited prediction read sites during native re-execution, uses exact auditing to recover minimum size, all minimum certificates and their core, and budgeted search and constrained repair to return verified sets. Independent calibration gives cross-stream reliability with a finite-sample guarantee.
bFpC2Q9vIb.key_idea: Test sufficiency of predicted rewards and values by re-running the planner with interventions at both recorded and newly visited read sites, not on frozen search trees.
bFpC2Q9vIb.evidence: Four planners and six tasks, including TD-MPC2, comparing native re-execution with frozen-tree explanations, exact audits, and Beam-4 variants under a query cap.
bFpC2Q9vIb.claimed_gains: Native re-execution rejects 16.5% of explanations selected on frozen search trees and 78.9% on TD-MPC2; at a 384-query cap default FutureCert recovers the exact minimum size on 93.0% of TD-MPC2 decisions versus 86.5% for Beam-4.
bFpC2Q9vIb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, since explanations evaluated on frozen computation may not survive re-planning, and that the experiments and counterexample support this.
bFpC2Q9vIb.main_concern: Novelty and significance are questioned because the ingredients are established, and certificates depend on audit setting while exact audits are limited to small evidence spaces (about H up to 12).

Ds2rDCUAHc.one_liner: Anomaly detector that calibrates scores across normal-support bins so weakly supported normal data stops receiving inflated anomaly scores.
Ds2rDCUAHc.problem: Normal-only multivariate time-series detectors cover normal behaviors unevenly, so weakly supported normal observations get higher raw scores and cause false-positive disparities under a shared threshold.
Ds2rDCUAHc.method: RestoreAD uses Row-Uniform regularization to discourage concentrated normal-to-normal relations, retrieves normal references for both scoring and support estimation, and applies Cross-Support Normality Calibration (CSNC). CSNC aligns training-score medians across support bins while preserving within-bin rankings.
Ds2rDCUAHc.key_idea: Estimate how well each normal observation is supported by normal references and align training-score medians across support bins without changing within-bin rankings.
Ds2rDCUAHc.evidence: The official TSB-AD-M Eval split against recent baselines, diagnostic analyses of score dependence on support, and a controlled study with symmetric normal regimes and unequal training support.
Ds2rDCUAHc.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims the highest mean on each reported metric among compared baselines on the TSB-AD-M Eval split, with no numbers).
Ds2rDCUAHc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that normal support imbalance and false-positive disparity are practically relevant problems that go beyond aggregate detection metrics, and that CSNC has a theoretical analysis.
Ds2rDCUAHc.main_concern: Channel-independent scoring may miss joint cross-channel anomalies, the practical effect of reduced disparity is unclear, and one reviewer could not tell which problem is solved or why other support or shift corrections were not compared.

SKFWafMK6K.one_liner: Learns piecewise-smooth coefficient images by gradient descent on a difference-of-squares factorization of local image differences.
SKFWafMK6K.problem: Explicit penalties such as total variation need a nonsmooth fit for every tuning value, so implicit regularization could be a cheaper route to piecewise-smooth image coefficients.
SKFWafMK6K.method: The coefficient image is split into a polynomial background and a component reconstructed from local differences of a chosen order, with a difference-of-squares factorization encouraging sparse differences and a quadratic consistency term. Gradient descent from small balanced initialization with backtracking and validation-based early stopping fits the factors.
SKFWafMK6K.key_idea: Gradient descent from small balanced initialization on squared-factor difference coordinates implicitly yields sparse local differences without an explicit variation penalty.
SKFWafMK6K.evidence: Finite-step prediction and coefficient-error bounds under correlated sub-Gaussian designs, an n^-1/2 prediction rate under bounded variation, and synthetic, real-image-based and real image dataset experiments against TV, CP, ridge and elastic net.
SKFWafMK6K.claimed_gains: not stated (the TL;DR claims lower computational cost than TV; the abstract states an n^-1/2 prediction rate up to logarithmic and geometric factors and gives no empirical numbers).
SKFWafMK6K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical analysis is strong, including finite-step bounds without restricted-eigenvalue assumptions, and that the method is competitive with TV in accuracy and cost.
SKFWafMK6K.main_concern: Related implicit-regularization methods such as Split LBI are not compared, real-image evaluation is thin (one real dataset per one review), and novelty over difference-based representations is questioned.

BRz6kEJFs7.one_liner: Sentence-centric chest X-ray vision-language pretraining that expands positive pairs by LLM abstract-level mapping and mitigates false negatives.
BRz6kEJFs7.problem: Radiology reports are long and dense, positive-pair diversity in sentence-level pretraining is limited, and clinically equivalent sentences recurring across patients create false negatives in contrastive learning.
BRz6kEJFs7.method: SentZero uses LLM-based abstract-level sentence structuring and mapping to widen positive pairs, adds a loss term for false negatives, and applies sentence-conditioned residual modulation of visual embeddings so visual features adapt to each input sentence.
BRz6kEJFs7.key_idea: Map finding sentences to abstract forms to enlarge positive pairs, add a false-negative loss term, and modulate visual embeddings residually by sentence.
BRz6kEJFs7.evidence: Zero-shot classification and grounding on seven benchmarks against eight baselines including RadZero, CoNNs and GLINT, with component ablations and a false-negative comparison.
BRz6kEJFs7.claimed_gains: not stated (the TL;DR claims leading zero-shot multi-task performance and the abstract claims improved zero-shot generalization over prior multi-task zero-shot methods, with no numbers).
BRz6kEJFs7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SentZero leads most reported zero-shot comparisons, including a large localization gain, and that the false-negative motivation and abstract-level mapping are clear.
BRz6kEJFs7.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed, since the no-component baseline already beats RadZero by 1 to 5 points and the false-negative component's own benefit is unclear without a same-supervision control.

LcIkFCDnoc.one_liner: Adds human-hand eigenvector perturbations to independent joint noise to correlate exploration in dexterous manipulation RL and trajectory optimization.
LcIkFCDnoc.problem: Exploration by independent joint perturbations rarely finds coordinated multi-joint behaviors, and reduced human-derived action spaces limit expressivity or add redundant dimensions.
LcIkFCDnoc.method: EigenDEXplore adds perturbations along human-derived eigenvectors to independent joint-space noise, producing correlated exploration while leaving the action space unchanged. They compare action dimensionality, exploration strategy and human data sources across manipulation settings.
LcIkFCDnoc.key_idea: Use human hand-coordination eigenvectors to shape exploration noise only, keeping the full joint action space intact.
LcIkFCDnoc.evidence: Experiments across multiple dexterous hands covering grasping, in-hand reorientation and contact-rich manipulation, in RL and sampling-based trajectory optimization, with real-world evaluation per reviews.
LcIkFCDnoc.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims consistent outperformance of joint-space and learned action-space baselines across multiple dexterous hands, with no numbers).
LcIkFCDnoc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, plug-and-play for existing RL and trajectory optimization pipelines, and supported by experiments across hands and tasks.
LcIkFCDnoc.main_concern: The advantage over Eigen-Residual is unclear with overlapping confidence intervals, novelty over PCA-based action priors is limited, and exploration-baseline comparisons are insufficient.

ylk9tGGim0.one_liner: Quantizes the LM-head to about 2 bits on the NPU, then refines top candidates on the CPU using existing embeddings.
ylk9tGGim0.problem: Large vocabularies make the LM-head costly to store and execute on mobile NPUs, and existing methods either limit compression or add heavy CPU overhead.
ylk9tGGim0.method: Q2F runs an NPU-compatible ultra-low-bit LM-head to generate candidates, relying on low-bit predictions retaining promising candidates, then refines them on the CPU using existing embeddings. It supports greedy and stochastic decoding at 2.2 bits per LM-head weight.
ylk9tGGim0.key_idea: Treat the quantized LM-head as a candidate generator whose top-K recall is high, and rerank those candidates with full-precision embeddings already in memory.
ylk9tGGim0.evidence: Four-task accuracy across three models with FP16 decoders, and on-device measurements on Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Llama3.2-1B with a 4-bit decoder.
ylk9tGGim0.claimed_gains: Four-task average accuracy stays within 0.32 percentage points of FP16 baselines at 2.2 bits per LM-head weight; on Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 it cuts LM-head weight storage by 73% over INT8 and raises end-to-end throughput by 19.6% for Llama3.2-1B.
ylk9tGGim0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the candidate-generation-plus-selective-recovery formulation is simple and hardware-aware, supported by top-K recall analysis and real-device evaluation.
ylk9tGGim0.main_concern: The near-FP16 quality claim lacks seeds or variability for stochastic decoding, and hardware evidence covers only one 1B model on one chipset.

uzaCZM59TP.one_liner: Open-world detector using a dynamic graph over class prototypes to pick local hard negatives and organize multi-component foreground modeling.
uzaCZM59TP.problem: Open-world detectors treat known-class discrimination and foreground (objectness) modeling separately, leaving the connection between the two objectives underexplored.
uzaCZM59TP.method: PROW maintains a dynamic graph over class prototypes updated from matched positive queries; locally confusable prototypes become negatives for class discrimination, and the graph groups prototypes into neighborhood-conditioned foreground components, with each query using the most compatible component for objectness. Later tasks use confidence-filtered pseudo-labels and replay.
uzaCZM59TP.key_idea: Reuse one prototype-neighborhood graph both to choose hard negatives for class discrimination and to define multiple foreground components for objectness.
uzaCZM59TP.evidence: Experiments on the M-OWODB and S-OWODB open-world detection benchmarks with ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity and pseudo-label and replay analyses; the visible abstract gives no numbers.
uzaCZM59TP.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract reports no numbers; reviews describe competitive results, particularly in unknown recall and known-unknown confusion).
uzaCZM59TP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared prototype-neighborhood formulation gives a coherent link between known-class detection and unknown discovery, with competitive results and useful ablations.
uzaCZM59TP.main_concern: Foreground-component construction is under-analyzed (number, size and stability not reported, heuristic threshold), and some baseline numbers may come from an older evaluation setting, leaving U-Recall comparisons unclear.

c3pGZZ4j9n.one_liner: Ridge-leverage peeling algorithm for column subset selection with outliers that cuts the number of selected columns to O(k/eps^2).
c3pGZZ4j9n.problem: The existing bicriteria algorithm for column subset selection with outliers needs a column count depending on d, and naive importance sampling is dominated by high-leverage outliers.
c3pGZZ4j9n.method: The method iteratively removes columns by ridge-leverage peeling, avoiding separation of inlier and outlier scores while controlling the number of discarded inliers. It returns a (1+eps)-approximation using O(k/eps^2) columns while discarding at most (1+eps)m columns.
c3pGZZ4j9n.key_idea: Peel columns iteratively by ridge leverage score without identifying outliers, so importance sampling is not dominated by outlier high-leverage directions.
c3pGZZ4j9n.evidence: Theoretical analysis comparing three algorithms in a table of column and outlier bounds; reviews note there are no numerical experiments.
c3pGZZ4j9n.claimed_gains: A (1+eps)-approximation with O(k/eps^2) columns while discarding at most (1+eps)m columns, improving the previous O((k/eps^6)(log(d/m)+1/eps)) column bound.
c3pGZZ4j9n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the improved column complexity, removing dependence on d, is a theoretically meaningful result in an important problem and the paper is well written.
c3pGZZ4j9n.main_concern: All guarantees are bicriteria with no lower bound showing the relaxation is necessary, there are no experiments, and reviewers found constant inconsistencies between algorithms and proofs.

DFA3HJZMaC.one_liner: Transformer for forecasting with exogenous variables using per-token parameters and separate attention routing for endogenous and exogenous streams.
DFA3HJZMaC.problem: Joint models of endogenous and exogenous variables apply the same transformations to differently-roled tokens and use one attention distribution per head that entangles temporal modeling with exogenous information acquisition.
DFA3HJZMaC.method: MixRoute makes representation and information flow type-aware for endogenous patches, exogenous variables and learnable global tokens. Under Mixed Parameterization endogenous patches share parameters while each exogenous and global token has private ones, and Adaptive Information Routing uses separate queries for an intrinsic stream over the endogenous series and an exogenous stream.
DFA3HJZMaC.key_idea: Give each exogenous and global token private parameters and route information through separate query streams for endogenous history and exogenous inputs.
DFA3HJZMaC.evidence: Experiments across multiple real-world datasets with and without future exogenous values, component ablations, and parameter-capacity controls per reviews.
DFA3HJZMaC.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract reports no numbers; reviews describe consistent improvements across multiple datasets).
DFA3HJZMaC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation around homogeneous parameter sharing and entangled attention is clear and that the design is well presented, with consistent gains across datasets and ablations.
DFA3HJZMaC.main_concern: Novelty over TimeXer and OneTrans is questioned, gains may reflect added capacity or unmatched tuning, and baseline results are reused from DAG without run-to-run uncertainty.

7oN5evwNFO.one_liner: Learns a coupled K/V correction trained on receiver behavior to translate one model's KV cache for another without prefill.
7oN5evwNFO.problem: Switching models breaks KV-cache reuse and forces the receiver to prefill again, and reconstruction fidelity of translated caches turns out to be a poor proxy for receiver utility.
7oN5evwNFO.method: CacheLink learns a coupled K/V correction supervised through the receiver's behavior directly, rather than through K/V reconstruction error, to turn a sender cache into a receiver-compatible state.
7oN5evwNFO.key_idea: Train the translated K/V cache with a receiver-side functional objective, correcting K and V jointly because their query-dependent attention importance is coupled.
7oN5evwNFO.evidence: Four independently trained sender-receiver pairs and seven evaluation panels, matched diagnostics comparing K/V error with receiver attention and next-token behavior, and a Ridge transport baseline.
7oN5evwNFO.claimed_gains: CacheLink improves the equal-weight mean over all methods for every pair, changes K/V squared error by less than 0.4% in matched diagnostics, and reduces handoff latency by up to 7.27 times versus receiver re-prefill at 32K context.
7oN5evwNFO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis showing that near-identical KV reconstruction errors yield very different receiver behavior is well done, and that CacheLink outperforms Ridge on almost all benchmarks across four model pairs.
7oN5evwNFO.main_concern: The coupled K/V correction is not sufficiently justified against simpler alternatives such as independent residuals or a joint MLP, and quality gaps remain on some long-context tasks.

gSPRBHuGCc.one_liner: Training-free frame selector that scores frames by option-contrastive relevance and allocates the frame budget across temporal segments.
gSPRBHuGCc.problem: Question relevance alone does not show whether a frame supports one candidate answer over the others, which matters for frame selection in multiple-choice long-video QA under a small budget.
gSPRBHuGCc.method: With a frozen image-text encoder, FULCRUM scores each frame against each question-option pair and combines the strongest match with its margin over the mean match across options. Scores guide budget allocation across temporal segments, with a coverage floor and diversity-aware selection to reduce redundancy.
gSPRBHuGCc.key_idea: Score each frame by its best question-option match plus its margin over the mean option match, and allocate frames across segments in proportion to that evidence.
gSPRBHuGCc.evidence: LongVideoBench and Video-MME with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA-Video-7B at 4, 8, 16 and 32 frames, against uniform sampling and reimplementations of ten selectors.
gSPRBHuGCc.claimed_gains: Outperforms uniform sampling and ten published selectors at all budgets of 4, 8, 16 and 32 frames; with eight frames on LongVideoBench it improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B accuracy from 44.2% to 62.5%.
gSPRBHuGCc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gains are consistent across two benchmarks, two answering models and all frame budgets, with a closed-form justification and useful ablations.
gSPRBHuGCc.main_concern: Novelty over option-guided selectors such as QAaF is limited and QAaF is not compared, and the method is restricted to multiple-choice questions with unquantified extra encoder cost.

3ST1VLm85N.one_liner: Multi-task massively parallel RL where policies execute cross-task action chunks in spare environments, chosen by the true task's Q value.
3ST1VLm85N.problem: In massively parallel on-policy RL, performance saturates with environment count because extra environments produce redundant trajectories from similar actions sampled around the policy mean.
3ST1VLm85N.method: SWAP uses the behavioral diversity of multi-task learning: in a designated subset of parallel environments per task, policies replan by sampling action chunks from all task policies and executing the chunk that maximizes Q under the true task. Pathwise policy gradients through the critic absorb this off-policy exploration without importance sampling.
3ST1VLm85N.key_idea: Replan with action chunks sampled from every task's policy and execute the one with the highest true-task Q value, using spare rollout capacity for coherent exploration.
3ST1VLm85N.evidence: Multi-task RL experiments on the MT50 benchmark with five seeds and confidence intervals, compared against methods such as PPO and CPO at several rollout horizons.
3ST1VLm85N.claimed_gains: not stated (the TL;DR and visible abstract describe resolving saturation and give no numbers).
3ST1VLm85N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the saturation problem and the idea of using excess environment capacity for switched multi-task actions are clearly motivated, with strong results at longer rollout horizons.
3ST1VLm85N.main_concern: Experiments fix the environment count and so do not show that SWAP reduces saturation as parallel environments grow, comparisons to stronger baselines are missing, and evaluation covers little domain diversity.

KPbaPyGjdt.one_liner: Applies inverse-moment conditioning on activity and error factors to direct feedback alignment, tested with preregistered controls.
KPbaPyGjdt.problem: In direct feedback alignment, unequal scales across activity or error directions can distort the local update even when random feedback provides useful credit.
KPbaPyGjdt.method: nDFA applies inverse-moment conditioning to either side of the DFA update: an activity factor shared with the Fast First-Order Optimizer (FOOF) and an error factor built from local DFA errors. A linear analysis describes how activity conditioning changes spectral learning rates and early-stopping risk.
KPbaPyGjdt.key_idea: Precondition DFA updates by inverse second moments of layer activity, and optionally of local errors, to equalize learning rates across directions.
KPbaPyGjdt.evidence: Aligned linear analysis, synthetic experiments, CIFAR-10 experiments at matched training time with paired seeds and Holm correction, 48-seed follow-ups, and Transformer language models.
KPbaPyGjdt.claimed_gains: With output-error feedback, both factors lower DFA test perplexity 2.8- to 3.7-fold at matched training time on Transformer language models.
KPbaPyGjdt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is unusually rigorous, with frozen protocols, paired seeds, multiple-comparison correction and honest reporting of negative results.
KPbaPyGjdt.main_concern: Activity conditioning is largely adapted from FOOF and KFAC, the theory gives no DFA-specific mechanism, and similar gains under backpropagation suggest general preconditioning rather than a DFA effect.

n9A1jfCUVR.one_liner: Trains an LLM questioner by preference optimization to ask for unstated and sequentially revealed information, scored by dependency graphs.
n9A1jfCUVR.problem: Proactive-agent work mostly studies when an agent should act, not what information it should pursue beyond what the user asked.
n9A1jfCUVR.method: They define horizontal proactivity (unstated needs the context already identifies) and vertical proactivity (needs only earlier evidence reveals), scored from transcripts using a need graph from a benchmark's decomposition. Q&D trains a questioner to prefer the question whose continuation retrieves more required evidence, with no reward model or judge.
n9A1jfCUVR.key_idea: Train the questioner with preferences defined by how much required evidence each question's continuation retrieves, measured against a need dependency graph.
n9A1jfCUVR.evidence: Held-out splits of three multi-hop QA benchmarks at equal retrieval spend, controls for question volume and length, and transfer to an interactive customer-service agent with a simulated customer.
n9A1jfCUVR.claimed_gains: At equal retrieval spend the trained questioner improves both forms of proactivity over the same prompted model and outperforms a prompted model 15 times larger on two of three benchmarks, with gains persisting after controlling for question volume and length.
n9A1jfCUVR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the need-graph formulation gives a judge-free, grounded way to measure proactive search and that retrieval gains hold under equal-spend and length controls.
n9A1jfCUVR.main_concern: The metrics do not clearly separate proactivity from evidence recall (only 20 of 1,040 probed dependency edges validated), QA gains are modest, and stopping behavior is imperfect.

AM6wNOiBLG.one_liner: Regularizes composite query-key and value-output attention operators on stored PCA supports during LoRA for replay-free continual ASR.
AM6wNOiBLG.problem: Adapting speech recognizers to new domains degrades earlier ones when past utterances are unavailable, and constraining shared representations can block useful adaptation.
AM6wNOiBLG.method: After each task PAF summarizes attention inputs by means and principal component bases, then on those affine supports regularizes a score operator (query and key projections) and a transport operator (value and output projections). Transport references are reconstructed from the merged model and stored low-rank update history, so no past examples or teacher are needed.
AM6wNOiBLG.key_idea: Preserve the composite attention functions, not individual projection weights, on stored low-dimensional input supports, allowing coordinated projection changes that leave the operators unchanged.
AM6wNOiBLG.evidence: Theoretical propositions under bounded-support assumptions and experiments on multiple domain sequences and ASR settings against baselines including GainLoRA.
AM6wNOiBLG.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract reports no numbers).
AM6wNOiBLG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving attention functions rather than constraining LoRA update subspaces is well motivated and gives a practical replay-free, teacher-free method with consistent improvements across domain sequences.
AM6wNOiBLG.main_concern: The theoretical guarantees assume identical attention inputs inside the stored supports, which do not hold in practice (PCA supports explain about 46% of energy at m=16), and the advantage over the strongest baselines is not shown robust.

ZohsxjfLKQ.one_liner: Adds a lightweight joint decoder to diffusion language models that generates dependent tokens in parallel groups within each step.
ZohsxjfLKQ.problem: Discrete diffusion language models sample tokens independently within a step, so accurate individual predictions can combine inconsistently and fixing this costs extra Transformer passes.
ZohsxjfLKQ.method: SPDLMs reuse a single Transformer evaluation of the noisy sequence per step, and a lightweight decoder generates dependent tokens in parallel groups, confining sequential computation to that decoder. A read/write mechanism updates one additional KV pair per token.
ZohsxjfLKQ.key_idea: Replace the product distribution over tokens within a step with a structured joint distribution sampled by a small decoder that reuses one backbone pass.
ZohsxjfLKQ.evidence: Controlled pretraining and adaptation of existing diffusion language models, including TinyStories experiments and larger-model experiments such as Sumi-7B on GSM8K.
ZohsxjfLKQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract and TL;DR claim improved few-step generation and quality-latency trade-offs with minimal overhead, with no numbers).
ZohsxjfLKQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is compact and simple, models within-step dependencies without extra backbone evaluations, and gives a useful quality-latency trade-off.
ZohsxjfLKQ.main_concern: Lightweight dependency-modeling heads already exist and several are not compared experimentally, and evaluation relies heavily on TinyStories and GSM8K with limited larger-scale settings.

qlG7rCOie2.one_liner: Intervention study of when vision-language models need direct image access during answer generation, using attention knockout and state replacement.
qlG7rCOie2.problem: It is unclear when a VLM needs direct access to image tokens while generating an answer rather than relying on information already in context.
qlG7rCOie2.method: They intervene on direct image access while retaining previously computed states, across real-image and synthetic tasks, and vary whether required attributes are supplied as text or stated by the model itself. They also compare conditions with identical generated prefixes but different earlier image access.
qlG7rCOie2.key_idea: Sever or replace direct image-side access during generation while keeping earlier computed states, to measure dependence as a function of available text and prior image access.
qlG7rCOie2.evidence: Real-image and synthetic tasks on Qwen2.5-VL-32B and InternVL3-14B, with attention knockout and image-side state replacement interventions.
qlG7rCOie2.claimed_gains: not stated (this is an analysis paper; the abstract reports no numbers).
qlG7rCOie2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and that the systematic analysis with several complementary interventions yields insightful findings, such as dependence differing with prior image access even for identical text.
qlG7rCOie2.main_concern: Attention knockout does not remove visual information already stored in earlier hidden states, so the work does not identify what is retained internally, and some findings are seen as expected.

wcPaLT8GKW.one_liner: Combines fMRI brain foundation model attention with effective-connectivity estimation to recover directed brain connections.
wcPaLT8GKW.problem: Brain foundation models predict clinical and demographic traits well, but what their self-attention represents about brain connectivity is a black box.
wcPaLT8GKW.method: They train a canonical brain foundation model with bias-free learnable embedding tokens on large-scale lifespan fMRI, analyze its spatiotemporal self-attention as direct connectivity, and in AXON integrate attention weights with an established effective-connectivity method to resolve connection directionality. AXON-derived connectivity is then used for downstream prediction.
wcPaLT8GKW.key_idea: Use pooled self-attention weights from a brain foundation model to guide an effective-connectivity estimator, giving directed networks per subject.
wcPaLT8GKW.evidence: Mouse and macaque tract-tracing connectomes, human-brain simulations built from empirical structural data, lifespan cohorts, and a downstream benchmark with 14 brain foundation model variants and other baselines per reviews.
wcPaLT8GKW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims accurate directionality recovery in mouse, macaque and simulated human networks, with no numbers).
wcPaLT8GKW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the validation is extensive across species and ground truths and that the analyses of what attention encodes, including ablations, add value beyond prediction accuracy.
wcPaLT8GKW.main_concern: Pooled attention is largely subject-invariant (r = 0.71 to 0.96 with the BOLD input ablated), so gains may reflect population-level information rather than attention, and encoder selection and data splits raise leakage questions.

As7cX3Irw8.one_liner: Controlled synthetic and real-world diagnostic study of how time series foundation models use cross-channel and covariate information.
As7cX3Irw8.problem: It is unclear whether multivariate time series foundation model forecasts reliably reflect the predictive value of related series and covariates.
As7cX3Irw8.method: They run controlled synthetic experiments with known cross-channel relationships and real forecasting tasks, examining temporal relationships, dependence structures, known-future conditioning and covariate reliability, and compare against statistical baselines fitted to the same contexts.
As7cX3Irw8.key_idea: Use synthetic data with known generating processes, oracles and fitted statistical baselines to separate unavailable information from information available but underused.
As7cX3Irw8.evidence: Controlled synthetic experiments, real-world forecasting tasks, and comparisons of three recent foundation models against statistical baselines and oracle references.
As7cX3Irw8.claimed_gains: not stated (this is a diagnostic study; it reports that conditioning on a model's own median covariate forecasts raises quantile loss and lowers interval coverage, and that propagating covariate uncertainty recovers much but not all of the loss).
As7cX3Irw8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic design with known generating processes, oracle references and statistical baselines is clean and separates underuse of information from its absence.
As7cX3Irw8.main_concern: The yardstick is questionable, since fitted baselines match the synthetic process class (home-field advantage), synthetic processes are simple linear Gaussian, and covariate-reliability experiments have no comparison method.

fyI3wb0Fnh.one_liner: Steers pretrained diffusion and flow models at sampling time with structure-dependent projections for stereochemistry, validity and crystal symmetry.
fyI3wb0Fnh.problem: Atomistic diffusion and flow models struggle to satisfy structural geometry, stereochemistry and crystallographic symmetry, and corrections must preserve geometry already captured by the pretrained model.
fyI3wb0Fnh.method: During sampling AtomSteer corrects intermediate structure predictions with bounded local projections, graph-rigid stereochemical transformations and projections over periodic symmetries, accepting only updates that improve constraint satisfaction while limiting changes to the rest of the structure.
fyI3wb0Fnh.key_idea: Apply constraint-specific projections to intermediate predictions at test time, accepting an update only if it improves constraint satisfaction with limited change elsewhere.
fyI3wb0Fnh.evidence: Three pretrained backbones (ET-Flow, Boltz-2, FlowMM) across conformer generation, protein-ligand complex prediction, and crystal generation and structure prediction, including EZBench and MP-20.
fyI3wb0Fnh.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract reports qualitative gains in molecular validity, E/Z stereochemical accuracy and crystal symmetry, with no numbers).
fyI3wb0Fnh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is practical, needs no retraining, uses well-motivated structure-dependent projections, and gives consistent improvements across backbones.
fyI3wb0Fnh.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate intermediate projection from applying the same projections only to final structures, computational cost is not reported, and novelty relative to PCFM is unclear.

tVyajwkJj9.one_liner: Predicts child-anchor features from ancestors using hyperbolic relations, so each anchor stores only low-dimensional variables and a bounded residual.
tVyajwkJj9.problem: Multiscale 3D Gaussian Splatting methods store independent high-dimensional features per anchor, causing large storage costs in large-scale scenes.
tVyajwkJj9.method: HHC-GS uses hyperbolic relations to modulate ancestor-conditioned feature prediction, restricts feature-generation dependencies to ancestor paths for local map loading, and jointly optimizes multiple hierarchy prefixes with frozen-teacher supervision to keep quality under different budgets.
tVyajwkJj9.key_idea: Generate each non-root anchor's features from its ancestors with hyperbolic-distance weighting, storing only low-dimensional structure and a bounded residual.
tVyajwkJj9.evidence: Experiments on MatrixCity, BungeeNeRF and UrbanScene3D against Octree-GS, with ablations including independent-feature, low-dimensional-only and Euclidean-context variants.
tVyajwkJj9.claimed_gains: Compared with Octree-GS, HHC-GS achieves comparable or better reconstruction quality while reducing model size by more than 85% on all three datasets.
tVyajwkJj9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the ancestor-conditioned feature prediction cuts storage substantially while keeping competitive rendering quality, with targeted ablations and clear motivation.
tVyajwkJj9.main_concern: The source of the storage savings is unclear, since the Independent Feature variant is already far smaller than Octree-GS (167.3 versus 623.6 MB), and hyperbolic distance and the hierarchy regularizer are not separately ablated.

ehwhVLrb0f.one_liner: Identity-preserving expert swap plus cross-fitting tests whether token-level best-expert headroom in sparse MoEs is real.
ehwhVLrb0f.problem: Counterfactual routing experiments in MoEs report apparent headroom that depends on how an expert is substituted and on whether the best expert is scored on the same data used to select it.
ehwhVLrb0f.method: They introduce an identity-preserving swap that exchanges expert roles while keeping the native routed-weight multiset, so expert identity is not confounded with routing-weight geometry. They evaluate with cross-fitting (select experts on one part of a continuation, score on another) and a matched-noise reference.
ehwhVLrb0f.key_idea: Swap expert identities while preserving the routed-weight multiset, and select experts on one interleaved half of a continuation but score them on the other.
ehwhVLrb0f.evidence: 7 MoE architectures and 202 matched cells, plus exhaustive-pool studies including a Qwen3 layer with 128 routed experts and a 256-expert model.
ehwhVLrb0f.claimed_gains: Forcing reports more same-sample headroom than the swap in 199 of 202 cells with a primary forcing-to-swap ratio of 5.48, while cross-fitted selection yields no detectably positive pooled gain.
ehwhVLrb0f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the swap is a useful control that separates expert identity from routing-weight side effects and that the paper addresses an important MoE interpretability issue with good related-work coverage.
ehwhVLrb0f.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the cross-fit halves are exchangeable (which the matched-noise null assumes), and note dense writing and some conclusions stronger than the evidence given limited detection power.

Kq4bf4cxTj.one_liner: Training-free defense that restores weakened refusal signals in Jacobian-lens space during prefill attacks, anchored to the pre-attack safety state.
Kq4bf4cxTj.problem: Prefill jailbreaks make safety-aligned language models continue an unsafe assistant prefix even when they would refuse the same request under normal decoding.
Kq4bf4cxTj.method: They use the Jacobian lens to track vocabulary-grounded harmfulness and refusal signals and observe refusal-state erosion along the prefill. J-Anchor uses the model's pre-attack safety state as a request-specific anchor and selectively restores weakened refusal in J-space during prefilling and decoding.
Kq4bf4cxTj.key_idea: Anchor to the pre-attack refusal state and restore the eroded component inside the J-lens refusal subspace, scaling the intervention by the current refusal deficit.
Kq4bf4cxTj.evidence: Fixed-prefill and deep-prefill attack evaluations across model families, with ablations comparing J-space refusal restoration against generic activation perturbations, plus benign-behavior and reasoning checks.
Kq4bf4cxTj.claimed_gains: Fixed-prefill attack success falls from 54-89% to at most 1.0%, and deep-prefill attack success from 83-94% to at most 2.5%.
Kq4bf4cxTj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the defense is effective against prefill attacks and that combining a pre-attack anchor with feedback on the current refusal deficit is a useful design.
Kq4bf4cxTj.main_concern: Evaluation covers only fixed and deep prefill attacks (no adaptive, multi-turn or other jailbreak settings), and the refusal-erosion mechanism has limited quantitative validation.

nMbXfqBef1.one_liner: Sends all prompt chunks through one layer group first, finishing low-rank KV factors earlier and cutting peak prefill memory.
nMbXfqBef1.problem: In xKV-style cross-layer low-rank KV compression under chunk-major chunked prefill, each factor depends on all prompt tokens, so factor completion is tied to the final chunk and dense K/V from multiple groups overlap near the prompt end.
nMbXfqBef1.method: SeamKV sends all prompt chunks through one factor-producing layer group before advancing deeper, accumulates factor statistics during forward execution, and completes remaining prompt-global products over bounded source blocks. It then replaces dense K/V with the finished factor once the group has produced all required rows and its last prefill use has passed.
nMbXfqBef1.key_idea: Producer-oriented execution order: finish each layer group over the whole prompt, accumulating factor statistics on the fly, so dense K/V can be replaced by factors early.
nMbXfqBef1.evidence: Matched chunk-major controls at 32K-128K context, a second factor geometry, and serving tests at N=1/2/4 concurrency, on an 8B model on 4090 GPUs.
nMbXfqBef1.claimed_gains: Per-GPU peak memory drops 9.5-20.8% across 32K-128K versus a matched chunk-major control, cache-ready time is lower at every tested length, and peak live dense groups at 128K falls from 8 to 1.
nMbXfqBef1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clearly stated, the memory savings are meaningful, and the matched-control decomposition shows where the savings come from.
nMbXfqBef1.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over Layered Prefill, the memory-latency trade-off (one-shot xKV is faster at mid lengths), and the missing throughput and concurrency evidence beyond a single hardware setup.

JXDQsImGbl.one_liner: Interleaves LLM formulation reasoning with targeted tool calls that turn instance data into evidence for optimization modeling.
JXDQsImGbl.problem: LLM optimization modeling treats instance data as values to bind to a formulation inferred from text, ignoring structural and numerical properties of the data that affect correctness and solver efficiency.
JXDQsImGbl.method: InForm progressively acquires instance evidence by calling formulation-oriented tools before each formulation decision is finalized, rather than analyzing the whole instance upfront. An experience-retrieval component supplies reusable guidance for turning recurring evidence patterns into local formulation decisions.
JXDQsImGbl.key_idea: Interleave formulation reasoning with targeted tool calls that convert raw instance data into mathematically meaningful evidence before each decision, aided by retrieved experience.
JXDQsImGbl.evidence: Four large-scale OR benchmarks including MIPLIB-NL, with component ablations, shared-backbone agent comparisons, and inference-cost measurements.
JXDQsImGbl.claimed_gains: 84.1% average formulation accuracy, 6.8 percentage points above the strongest baseline and 31.5 percentage points over the base LLM on MIPLIB-NL, plus 1.07x to 2.18x solver-time improvements on commonly correct instances.
JXDQsImGbl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the tool design practical, with ablations on progressive tool use, specialized tools, and memory supporting each component.
JXDQsImGbl.main_concern: Online memory is built from verified test-set trajectories in a fixed order, so memory gains may reflect benchmark-specific learning, and cost-matched baselines and repeated-run variability are missing.

S6jBIulhDf.one_liner: Federated RAG conformal prediction fixing the honest-node group across calibration and prediction to resist Byzantine nodes.
S6jBIulhDf.problem: Existing methods assume every node is honest or protect only the calibration step, while Byzantine nodes may misreport both during calibration and when answering new questions.
S6jBIulhDf.method: The hub has all nodes score the same calibration questions and keeps a candidate answer only if some plausible group of honest nodes, the same group in both steps, would admit it. This gives a fixed-membership conformal rule with a provable hierarchy of prediction sets.
S6jBIulhDf.key_idea: Exploit that the honest nodes are identical in calibration and prediction by scoring shared calibration questions and keeping an answer only if one fixed plausible honest group supports it.
S6jBIulhDf.evidence: Theory plus real-world multiple-choice QA experiments (GPT-2 scorer on four benchmarks and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct on OpenBookQA, per reviews) varying attacks, corruption budgets, dependence and quantization.
S6jBIulhDf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the fixed-honest-set insight clear and the problem of Byzantine nodes in both phases practically relevant, with a precise inference rule and theory.
S6jBIulhDf.main_concern: Main experiments use GPT-2 at near-chance accuracy (24.10%-28.12%), and prediction sets stay near 3.6 of four options, so practical usefulness is weakly demonstrated.

AIy7MvmZLA.one_liner: Adds one interaction exponent coupling model size and data to the Chinchilla scaling law.
AIy7MvmZLA.problem: The standard Chinchilla form assumes model size and data affect loss independently, so it mis-estimates loss at data-scarce and overtraining extremes.
AIy7MvmZLA.method: The Skaling law extends Chinchilla with a single interaction exponent between model capacity and data, fitted on two large training grids, and is paired with a sparse low-compute grid strategy.
AIy7MvmZLA.key_idea: Couple parameters and tokens in the loss surface through one interaction exponent, keeping an analytical compute-allocation rule.
AIy7MvmZLA.evidence: Two large training grids for interpolation and extrapolation, including sparse-grid fits and an L-shape sampling scheme, compared with Chinchilla and Farseer.
AIy7MvmZLA.claimed_gains: One extra parameter reduces MAPE by roughly 2-3x on interpolation and extrapolation and by up to an order of magnitude on sparse grids; a sparse low-compute grid matches or exceeds Chinchilla on the full grid with up to 10x less compute.
AIy7MvmZLA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the experiments extensive across model and data sizes, the L-shape sampling scheme useful, and the single-parameter coupling simple and interpretable.
AIy7MvmZLA.main_concern: The functional form is not new (a prior work used the same formulation), and the advantage over Chinchilla and Farseer depends on the fitting procedure.

SpPCdHXxJQ.one_liner: A multi-view SFT plus reinforcement-learning pipeline with reward models removes unwanted lighting from generated 3D asset textures.
SpPCdHXxJQ.problem: Unwanted highlights in generated 3D textures reduce realism and editability, and 3D delighting lacks dedicated evaluation systems or optimization paradigms.
SpPCdHXxJQ.method: They build lighting datasets and three structurally distinct evaluation models as a benchmark, then use an adaptive decoupled multi-objective SFT and RL joint architecture in which SFT injects basic delighting capability and RL further improves it.
SpPCdHXxJQ.key_idea: Train delighting with RL against reward models that separately score lighting removal and content consistency, after SFT provides basic capability.
SpPCdHXxJQ.evidence: New lighting datasets and evaluation models; reviews cite comparisons with Paint3D and Hunyuan3D, ablations, multiview visualizations, and a human study.
SpPCdHXxJQ.claimed_gains: Improves delighting performance by 18.7% while reducing FID by 55.0%.
SpPCdHXxJQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is practically useful, separating shadow removal from appearance preservation is well motivated, and the RL design improves on SFT with supporting ablations.
SpPCdHXxJQ.main_concern: Technical novelty beyond integrating SFT, Flow-GRPO, and reward modeling is unclear, and related work such as PBR texture generation (MaterialMVP, Material Anything) and external baselines are missing.

CnIYCwzOpD.one_liner: Federated LoRA fine-tuning with random orthogonal projection compression and LoRA-aware error feedback for bidirectional communication savings.
CnIYCwzOpD.problem: Federated LoRA fine-tuning has bidirectional communication bottlenecks, and existing fixes either restrict trainable LoRA factors, hurting performance, or compress updates in ways that need dense downlink or server-side recompression.
CnIYCwzOpD.method: A random orthogonal projection (ROP) compressor is linear, so the server aggregates compressed LoRA updates directly. Because standard error feedback may impair optimization with ROP, LA-EF uses shared LoRA geometry to regulate historical compression residuals.
CnIYCwzOpD.key_idea: A shared linear random orthogonal projection compresses both LoRA factors, and error-feedback residuals are filtered through LoRA-factor geometry.
CnIYCwzOpD.evidence: A proof of the same O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence order as full-precision FedAvg, plus experiments on multiple datasets and LLMs (three seeds and 10 clients in the main runs per reviews).
CnIYCwzOpD.claimed_gains: Reduces total communication cost by up to 96.9% relative to full-precision FedAvg while achieving competitive performance (abstract is cut off after "competitive").
CnIYCwzOpD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design targets a concrete limitation, since sparsified updates densify after aggregation, and that shared linear projections give compact bidirectional aggregation with both factors trainable.
CnIYCwzOpD.main_concern: Novelty is limited because linear shared-seed compression and error feedback are established (closest prior work uncited), and the benefit of LA-EF over simple residual damping is not isolated.

s8HWNwp6Mf.one_liner: Trains a dense retriever and pointwise LLM reranker on examiner claim citations for patent prior-art search over seven million patents.
s8HWNwp6Mf.problem: Patent prior-art search must match claims to earlier patents in different terminology, and high recall at deep cutoffs can coexist with poor coverage among the earliest results.
s8HWNwp6Mf.method: The retriever learns from cited positives with lexical hard negatives and cross-device negatives, and the pointwise LM reranker uses claim-conditioned excerpts to predict structured citation-alignment labels and scores. They also build PAR4PC-Retrieve, linking PANORAMA queries and citation targets to a frozen corpus of over seven million U.S. patents.
s8HWNwp6Mf.key_idea: Adapt retrieval and reranking separately using claim-level examiner citations, with BM25 hard negatives and cross-device in-batch negatives for the retriever.
s8HWNwp6Mf.evidence: PAR4PC-Retrieve (7M+ U.S. patents), a same-encoder comparison, a comparison with task-adapted Qwen3-Reranker-8B, ablations, and a 50-case blinded human study per reviews.
s8HWNwp6Mf.claimed_gains: Supervised retrieval improves Recall@5000 by 8.71 percentage points over the same unadapted encoder; reranking improves Recall@20 by 14.40 points over the retriever's ordering and 8.56 points over task-adapted Qwen3-Reranker-8B.
s8HWNwp6Mf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the realistic-scale benchmark is a useful resource, separating retrieval from reranking is sound, and the gains over baselines are substantial and well documented.
s8HWNwp6Mf.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (established contrastive retrieval, hard negatives, LoRA, pointwise ranking), and temporal filtering, patent-family leakage, and latency are unresolved.

INySVzMlx4.one_liner: Post-hoc landmark graph composes local distance predictions to improve long-range minimum action distance estimates without retraining.
INySVzMlx4.problem: Learned Minimum Action Distance estimates can be locally accurate yet unreliable over long horizons.
INySVzMlx4.method: Hierarchical distance decomposition composes local predictions of an existing learned distance model through a sparse graph of landmark states, and applies to any such model without retraining. The theory bounds the resulting estimation errors and shows order preservation for sufficiently separated state pairs.
INySVzMlx4.key_idea: Reuse only the base model's trusted short-range predictions and compose them through a sparse graph of landmark states to estimate long-range distances.
INySVzMlx4.evidence: PointMaze and AntMaze experiments in OGBench measuring Spearman correlation with grid-geodesic distance and downstream planning success, plus error-bound theory.
INySVzMlx4.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says long-range estimation accuracy and downstream planning improve, without numbers)
INySVzMlx4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple, training-free, broadly applicable method with honest theory, clear writing, and gains that carry over to planning and control.
INySVzMlx4.main_concern: The method depends on local accuracy and dataset coverage of the base model with no practical check, and experiments are limited to PointMaze and AntMaze with a proxy distance metric.

ebKF3mNzwV.one_liner: Chest X-ray VQA model trained with radiologist eye gaze as an RL reward, outputting organ box, gaze points, and answer.
ebKF3mNzwV.problem: SFT and RL objectives supervise only generated text, not where the model looks, so a model can answer correctly while attending to clinically irrelevant regions.
ebKF3mNzwV.method: CheXGaze generates an organ bounding box, gaze points, and an answer, following the radiologists' global-to-focal reading process. Gaze is used as an RL reward rather than an imitation target, with a population-prior correction and alternating SFT and GRPO per reviews.
ebKF3mNzwV.key_idea: Reward predicted gaze points by the fraction of radiologist fixation mass they cover, corrected for a population spatial prior, instead of imitating gaze.
ebKF3mNzwV.evidence: MIMIC-CXR-VQA and the CXR subsets of SLAKE and VQA-RAD, ablations of output components and training strategies, and an attention analysis against radiologist gaze.
ebKF3mNzwV.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports effectiveness on three datasets and closer attention alignment with radiologists' gaze, without numbers)
ebKF3mNzwV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that gaze-as-reward with an anti-shortcut population-prior correction is well motivated for sparse, noisy gaze data and gives encouraging transfer results.
ebKF3mNzwV.main_concern: Gains are modest with no significance testing, and the gaze reward's specific contribution and the faithfulness of generated gaze to the answer are not isolated.

z0nQAdCOH0.one_liner: Evaluates open-ended mathematical exploration in LLMs using equational-theory tasks that measure future utility and idea diversity.
z0nQAdCOH0.problem: Open-ended exploration, theory building and asking new research questions are under-studied capabilities of language models compared with problem solving.
z0nQAdCOH0.method: It builds problem-solving tasks inside generated equational theories that stay hard for frontier models without tools, measures future utility as the improvement from providing an exploration document, and measures idea diversity through a limited automated-reasoning query interface that enables unambiguous comparison of ideas across runs.
z0nQAdCOH0.key_idea: Score exploration by how much an exploration document improves later problem solving and by the diversity of distinct automated-reasoning queries across runs.
z0nQAdCOH0.evidence: Reviewers report 21 theories for the utility exam and five for the diversity experiment, filtered from 1,953 candidate theories to 373, evaluated on frontier reasoning models.
z0nQAdCOH0.claimed_gains: Observes notable but uneven benefits from exploration across models and theories; no numbers stated.
z0nQAdCOH0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets an under-explored aspect of mathematical reasoning and that automated generation and verification of unfamiliar theories gives a useful, reproducible evaluation framework.
z0nQAdCOH0.main_concern: No control isolates exploration from extra information or compute (such as matched summaries or equal-length guided preparation), and coverage is small (21 and 5 theories).

uX65exPmqe.one_liner: Interactive person re-identification combining query-adaptive low-rank alignment anchors with a reflective questioner that refines follow-up questions.
uX65exPmqe.problem: As queries move from sparse attributes to fine-grained cues, a fixed cross-modal alignment may not suit every query state, and plausible follow-up questions may be redundant, visually unsupported or uninformative.
uX65exPmqe.method: On retrieval, PAIReID learns lightweight low-rank alignment anchors from progressive query states and composes them by current query semantics without round identities. On interaction, a State-Aware Reflective Questioner tracks appearance coverage and selectively refines unsuitable questions without task-specific fine-tuning.
uX65exPmqe.key_idea: Low-rank alignment anchors are dynamically composed by current query semantics, while a questioner tracks appearance coverage to reject and refine uninformative follow-up questions.
uX65exPmqe.evidence: Experiments on Interactive-PEDES, with Qwen-2.5-VL used as a prompt-based questioner per reviews.
uX65exPmqe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the two challenges are well motivated and that addressing both retrieval adaptation and question selection in one framework is a meaningful direction.
uX65exPmqe.main_concern: Limited novelty and weak ablation evidence: the framework combines LoRA, mixture-of-experts-style routing and prompting, and experiments do not show query-dependent alignment beats pooled adapter training or uniform anchor mixing.

6gJELX705a.one_liner: Perturbs text embeddings early in diffusion denoising and restores them under classifier guidance to make natural adversarial images transfer.
6gJELX705a.problem: Natural adversarial examples must work across different classifiers without losing image quality, but a fixed text condition may restrict adversarial search to a subset of a class's visual variations.
6gJELX705a.method: TPA temporarily perturbs text embeddings during early denoising and progressively restores the original condition while guiding sampling with classifier gradients, changing both the denoising trajectory and the intermediate images on which adversarial guidance acts. Reviewers note the perturbation follows CADS-style embedding noise with annealing and moment rescaling.
6gJELX705a.key_idea: Add annealed noise to the text-conditioning embedding in early denoising steps so the sampler explores more class variations under classifier-gradient guidance.
6gJELX705a.evidence: ImageNet-1K across surrogate-victim classifier pairs including adversarially trained models, compared with NatADiff and another baseline using image-quality metrics, FID to ImageNet-A, matched ablations, and a small human study.
6gJELX705a.claimed_gains: Higher black-box attack success than existing natural adversarial generation methods across all evaluated surrogate-victim pairs, better learned image-quality metrics than NatADiff on most, and lower FID to ImageNet-A than both baselines; no numbers stated.
6gJELX705a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree early text-embedding perturbation is a simple, training-free way to improve transferability, with consistent gains over baselines supported by matched ablations.
6gJELX705a.main_concern: The core intervention is adopted from CADS and the other components resemble existing designs, so the contribution is mainly a combination, and the mechanism and class fidelity of generated images are not established.

G9XcJvABUT.one_liner: Shared spectral-energy descriptors and graph-filter experts transfer anomaly patterns to unseen graphs.
G9XcJvABUT.problem: Graph-specific anomaly detectors lack a common representation space for transferring anomaly knowledge across domains.
G9XcJvABUT.method: SV-GAD builds a graph vocabulary from spectral-energy statistics describing node-signal variation relative to graph structure. A mixture of graph-filter experts models different spectral behaviors to support cross-graph anomaly detection.
G9XcJvABUT.key_idea: Represent nodes through shared spectral-energy measurements and route them among graph-filter experts specializing in different spectral behaviors.
G9XcJvABUT.evidence: Zero-shot evaluations cover diverse anomaly-detection benchmarks, including citation networks and T-Social, with routing and architectural ablations.
G9XcJvABUT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find spectral representations promising for cross-graph feature mismatch and recognize competitive zero-shot results.
G9XcJvABUT.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the spectral vocabulary's contribution from projected features, dimensionality reduction, and preprocessing.

FYIUdWxibK.one_liner: Text-aligned semantic profiles rank CLIP attention heads for sparse task-specific fine-tuning.
FYIUdWxibK.problem: Existing CLIP adaptation methods do not explicitly identify which internal visual-transformer units matter most for a target task.
FYIUdWxibK.method: SAHR constructs text-aligned profiles of attention-head semantics and compares them with task-aware descriptions. It ranks head-task correspondence and updates only a sparse set of top-ranked heads.
FYIUdWxibK.key_idea: Match attention-head semantic profiles to task descriptions and fine-tune only the highest-ranked heads.
FYIUdWxibK.evidence: Evaluations include 11 few-shot classification benchmarks, Flickr30K and MSCOCO retrieval, OOD robustness, multiple CLIP backbones, and component ablations.
FYIUdWxibK.claimed_gains: In the 16-shot setting, SAHR achieves 83.1% average accuracy on 11 benchmarks with 1.18M parameters.
FYIUdWxibK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate converting head-level semantic interpretation into selective adaptation and evaluating it across diverse downstream tasks.
FYIUdWxibK.main_concern: The method's distinction from existing head interpretation and selective adaptation techniques remains insufficiently established.

egAVxGaAb8.one_liner: Experimental discrepancies revise physical mechanisms and equations while retained exploration procedures guide later modeling attempts.
egAVxGaAb8.problem: Existing AI systems struggle to autonomously choose physical-model structures, couplings, and mechanisms from experimental evidence.
egAVxGaAb8.method: EvoSim revises mechanisms and equations in response to experimental discrepancies and checks physical plausibility on held-out data. It uses exploration traces to update knowledge, skills, and multi-agent coordination procedures for subsequent modeling.
egAVxGaAb8.key_idea: Use measurement-model discrepancies to revise equations and retain validated exploration procedures for future physical-model construction.
egAVxGaAb8.evidence: Two industrial battery tasks evaluate lithium-metal-plating onset and dynamic driving-condition voltage predictions, with repeated matched trials assessing retained procedures.
egAVxGaAb8.claimed_gains: EvoSim reports 1.79% state-of-charge mean absolute error for plating onset, 7.62 mV voltage root mean square error, and approximately 36% fewer model and physics errors relative to baseline.
egAVxGaAb8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value solver-based physical modeling checked against real measurements and evidence that retained procedures reduce subsequent modeling failures.
egAVxGaAb8.main_concern: Comparisons do not establish an advantage over strong procedural-memory or experience-distillation baselines.

v5cC1gtXWU.one_liner: Paired passage deletion measures which answerless bridges individual language models need for correct multi-hop answers.
v5cC1gtXWU.problem: Model-agnostic relevance labels cannot capture whether a particular reader depends on a passage that does not contain the answer.
v5cC1gtXWU.method: The study deletes either a bridge passage or a control from the same context and records whether only bridge removal breaks a correct answer. It compares model-specific necessity with lexical, dense, cross-encoder, and ContextCite scores.
v5cC1gtXWU.key_idea: Define passage necessity per model by comparing answer failures after bridge deletion against same-context control deletion.
v5cC1gtXWU.evidence: Experiments cover eleven open-weight models on HotpotQA and MuSiQue, with additional DROP arithmetic and synthetic-prompt tests.
v5cC1gtXWU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled deletion intervention and broad evidence that passage necessity varies across models.
v5cC1gtXWU.main_concern: Short four-passage contexts and eligibility conditioned on successful answering limit relevance to realistic retrieval settings with missing or redundant evidence.

3IOp4jQTYc.one_liner: Spherical Laplacian-pyramid diffusion couples coarse and fine climate bands through exact projections and band-specific noise schedules.
3IOp4jQTYc.problem: Independently trained coarse generation and super-resolution stages lack exact multiresolution composition, while weather channels have different scale-dependent variability.
3IOp4jQTYc.method: SPyD decomposes a spherical climate field into a coarse band and orthogonal finer bands with separate noise schedules. Coupled probability-flow ODEs use a shared denoising formulation instantiated by separately trained conditional band models, with conditioning as an exact state projection.
3IOp4jQTYc.key_idea: Diffuse orthogonal spherical pyramid bands with band-specific schedules while conditioning fine bands on exact projections of the evolving state.
3IOp4jQTYc.evidence: Evaluations compare SPyD with cBottle-SR across 12 atmospheric variables using CRPS, RMSE, precipitation extremes, spectra, and ensemble calibration on a HEALPix construction.
3IOp4jQTYc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the spherical multiresolution formulation and strong single-stage results across climate variables and precipitation metrics.
3IOp4jQTYc.main_concern: The multistage model underperforms the single-stage version on important metrics, limiting the practical benefit of exact multiresolution composition.

WFLS89sCe2.one_liner: Stateful device agents switch execution modalities while a global orchestrator revises plans and device assignments after failures.
WFLS89sCe2.problem: Cross-device agents can repeatedly fail when they cannot distinguish modality-specific problems from task infeasibility on a device.
WFLS89sCe2.method: OctoNest combines iterative device-local subtask refinement and modality control with global feedback-driven planning and reassignment. CAPEBench introduces controlled perturbations to evaluate these recovery decisions.
WFLS89sCe2.key_idea: Separate local modality recovery from global device reassignment and update both using execution feedback.
WFLS89sCe2.evidence: CAPEBench contains 158 instances from 23 seed tasks, with matched-modality baseline comparisons, ablations, four-backbone tests, and external CRAB tasks.
WFLS89sCe2.claimed_gains: OctoNest improves Perfect Pass over the strongest baseline by 18.35 percentage points and reduces token cost per perfect pass by 39.8%.
WFLS89sCe2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical separation of local and global recovery and the observed improvements with comparable execution capabilities.
WFLS89sCe2.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the role structure contributes beyond existing hierarchical agents and additional model or inference resources.

EsS6ecnNnV.one_liner: Linear privacy probes identify restricted spans whose cached positions generated tokens cannot attend to.
EsS6ecnNnV.problem: Agents with personal information must decide which spans are appropriate to disclose for the current task.
EsS6ecnNnV.method: The work models contextual privacy as a linear component of span representations and trains layer-specific probes. Probe-guided attention masking blocks generated tokens from attending to restricted cached positions without changing the base model.
EsS6ecnNnV.key_idea: Classify context-dependent restricted spans with linear probes and mask their cached positions during generation.
EsS6ecnNnV.evidence: Five-model experiments evaluate probe accuracy, 226 context-flip pairs, disclosure completeness, and generated-token counts on a structured synthetic benchmark.
EsS6ecnNnV.claimed_gains: Probes average 90.5% accuracy and shift correctly on 96.2% of 226 context-flip pairs, while masking yields 32.3% Completeness versus 24.7% for CI-CoT and averages 178 generated tokens versus 475.
EsS6ecnNnV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard span-level contextual privacy as useful and the probing-plus-masking approach as lightweight.
EsS6ecnNnV.main_concern: Reviewers find that isolated, structured probe inputs provide limited evidence for intrinsic privacy awareness or reliable behavior in realistic full prompts.

rZFAAb8lVK.one_liner: Replacing harmful fine-tuning answers with corrections reduces emergent misalignment more than deleting the same selected rows.
rZFAAb8lVK.problem: Deleting harmful demonstrations may inadequately mitigate broad misalignment induced by narrow poisoned fine-tuning data.
rZFAAb8lVK.method: The study preselects poison rows and compares deletion with corrected answers to the same prompts under paired training settings. It tests correction doses, paraphrase controls, other models, and corrective training of already-poisoned models.
rZFAAb8lVK.key_idea: Retain selected poisoned prompts but replace harmful answers with corrective supervision instead of removing the rows.
rZFAAb8lVK.evidence: Experiments fine-tune Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on bad medical advice mixed with benign chat and extend to another base model and financial-advice misalignment.
rZFAAb8lVK.claimed_gains: Correcting a quarter of poison rows cuts the emergent-misalignment rate by about a third, whereas deleting the same rows has little measurable effect.
rZFAAb8lVK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical correction-versus-deletion question and the controlled experiments with paired seeds and multiple judges.
rZFAAb8lVK.main_concern: Reviewers find the fixed 56-question evaluation insufficient to establish broad, persistent mitigation under poisoning-context triggers.

CzDLiwNxO8.one_liner: A Gaussian process predicts candidate expansion gains, and joint Thompson sampling allocates agents' next experiments.
CzDLiwNxO8.problem: Rule-based candidate selection does not explicitly estimate the improvement and uncertainty associated with the next expansion.
CzDLiwNxO8.method: BayesianAgent learns expansion gains with a Gaussian process that shares evidence across related candidates. Joint Thompson sampling selects which executable solution the agent should improve next.
CzDLiwNxO8.key_idea: Share expansion-gain evidence through a Gaussian-process posterior and jointly sample candidate values to allocate further experiments.
CzDLiwNxO8.evidence: Evaluations compare budgeted agentic search on 15 AlphaEvolve mathematical optimization tasks and 22 MLE-bench Lite tasks, including ablations and prediction diagnostics.
CzDLiwNxO8.claimed_gains: BayesianAgent achieves AlphaEvolve average rank 1.96 over three seeds and MLE-bench Lite mean gold and medal rates of 43.94 and 69.70.
CzDLiwNxO8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing expansion potential from current quality and the broad evaluation of a coherent allocation model.
CzDLiwNxO8.main_concern: Reviewers identify provider and CPU changes across AlphaEvolve runs that confound attribution of gains to the selection strategy.

8cx83uuOS9.one_liner: Iterative disassembly exposes occluded LEGO parts, producing atom-level annotations for an end-to-end semantic segmentor.
8cx83uuOS9.problem: Brick-level semantics become ambiguous when a LEGO brick spans parts, while occlusion complicates semantic segmentation.
8cx83uuOS9.method: LEGO-SAM atomizes assemblies and combines 2D multimodal visual evidence with 3D segmentation priors. Chain-of-Disassembly removes consistently segmented parts across views and generates labels to train LEGO-SAM-Flash with residual adapters and an atom-level head.
8cx83uuOS9.key_idea: Iteratively remove multi-view-consistent segmented parts from atomized assemblies to reveal hidden structure and generate training annotations.
8cx83uuOS9.evidence: The data engine produces 1.86M atoms and 67K semantic parts, while LEGO-SAM-Bench supplies 347K atoms and 6.4K parts for quantitative evaluation and ablations.
8cx83uuOS9.claimed_gains: The abstract reports outperforming the strongest baseline by 31.18%.
8cx83uuOS9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value atom-level LEGO segmentation and its relevance to part retrieval and assembly-aware applications.
8cx83uuOS9.main_concern: Reviewers question baseline fairness because generic 3D segmentors lack clearly matched LEGO-specific adaptation or training.

IfEfBuYZJs.one_liner: Construction layouts anchor a program canvas before bidirectional diffusion fills CadQuery implementations.
IfEfBuYZJs.problem: Token-order generation and undifferentiated program denoising poorly coordinate CAD decisions spanning distant code regions.
IfEfBuYZJs.method: CADiff predicts interface-level construction structure and implementation-span capacities, renders an anchored program canvas, and denoises remaining code bidirectionally. CADConstruct supplies dimension-grounded requirements, executable programs, and explicit construction structure.
IfEfBuYZJs.key_idea: Resolve shared interfaces and implementation-span capacities first, then condition bidirectional code denoising on those fixed anchors.
IfEfBuYZJs.evidence: CADConstruct evaluations cover easy, medium, and hard programs using executability, feature recovery, and geometric fidelity, with ablations and ExeCAD transfer.
IfEfBuYZJs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the scaffold-first organization well motivated and the performance improvements across difficulty levels encouraging.
IfEfBuYZJs.main_concern: Reviewers agree that the experiments do not isolate denoising-view contributions from ordinary fine-tuning and scaffold conditioning.

wYJDFWQr4m.one_liner: Matching bounds quantify the extra prediction-set size required to enforce cumulative miscoverage budgets at every round.
wYJDFWQr4m.problem: Marginal or long-run conformal coverage can permit temporary violations of a cumulative error budget.
wYJDFWQr4m.method: The analysis characterizes minimum cumulative excess set size under hard online coverage constraints and regularity conditions on the coverage-size frontier. It provides matching lower bounds and algorithms using past scores without a known score distribution.
wYJDFWQr4m.key_idea: Compare hard-budget online prediction sets with the population-optimal set to bound unavoidable cumulative excess size under different evaluation-time criteria.
wYJDFWQr4m.evidence: Theoretical results cover i.i.d. data, oracle score knowledge, and empirical threshold estimation, with matching bounds under stated assumptions.
wYJDFWQr4m.claimed_gains: Minimum excess-size costs are Θ(log T) at a fixed time known in advance, Θ(T^{1/3}) for the largest expected cost over fixed times, and Θ(√T) for expected hindsight worst realized cost.
wYJDFWQr4m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize rigorous matching bounds and useful characterization of the efficiency cost of hard coverage constraints.
wYJDFWQr4m.main_concern: Reviewers agree that strong frontier and score assumptions limit the connection between the theoretical rates and practical conformal models.

xRCuxcIta9.one_liner: Restricting diffusion-classifier evidence to selected noise bands avoids fragile low-noise terms under domain shift.
xRCuxcIta9.problem: Exact-likelihood weighting can amplify misleading low-noise class evidence and reduce diffusion-classifier robustness under domain shift.
xRCuxcIta9.method: The study decomposes class-conditional negative log-likelihood across noise levels and compares scoring rules on identical denoising errors. It restricts the evidence integral to a noise band chosen without test-domain access or retraining.
xRCuxcIta9.key_idea: Exclude fragile low-noise evidence by restricting the class-score integral to a selected diffusion noise band.
xRCuxcIta9.evidence: Controlled scoring comparisons cover all six Rotated MNIST folds and CIFAR-10-C corruptions, with CIFAR-10.1 as a boundary case.
xRCuxcIta9.claimed_gains: On CIFAR-10-C noise corruptions, exact likelihood performs at chance while uniform-timestep scoring reaches 36%, and band-restricted scoring exceeds both on those corruptions and all six Rotated MNIST folds.
xRCuxcIta9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the noise-level diagnosis and controlled evidence that reweighting improves the tested diffusion classifiers.
xRCuxcIta9.main_concern: Reviewers find the small MNIST and CIFAR models too narrow to support broader claims about generative-classifier robustness.

O6rZzDmQbo.one_liner: Room-view-object memory supports hierarchical visual retrieval and activates exploration at the level where evidence appears.
O6rZzDmQbo.problem: Scene graphs discard visual detail, while class-based image retrieval inherits detection errors and separates evidence retrieval from exploration.
O6rZzDmQbo.method: HiREx organizes co-visible views, semantic room anchors, and object crops into one visual memory. Task retrieval narrows evidence through these layers and triggers corresponding exploration options.
O6rZzDmQbo.key_idea: Use the layer that supplies task evidence to choose the level of subsequent exploration within a shared visual-memory hierarchy.
O6rZzDmQbo.evidence: Question-answering and goal-navigation benchmarks compare baselines and ablate memory, hierarchical retrieval, and exploration components.
