O6rZzDmQbo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using a shared hierarchical representation to retrieve evidence and decide where to gather further observations.
O6rZzDmQbo.main_concern: Insufficient differentiation and comparison with closely related visual-memory and retrieval systems make the contribution hard to assess.

TYSv9rIhiQ.one_liner: Functionally equivalent website variants isolate how implementation changes alter web-agent success and rankings.
TYSv9rIhiQ.problem: Existing web-agent benchmarks do not test whether task-solving ability survives alternative implementations of the same functionality.
TYSv9rIhiQ.method: WebVariants shares tasks and backend verification across multiple implementations of each website. It evaluates observation modalities, successful termination, and training across variants.
TYSv9rIhiQ.key_idea: Hold task functionality and verification fixed while changing website structure, text, and visual interfaces.
TYSv9rIhiQ.evidence: The benchmark covers nine websites, five implementations each, 228 shared tasks, and 1,140 task-environment instances across text, screenshot, and multimodal agents.
TYSv9rIhiQ.claimed_gains: Up to 50% of pairwise agent rankings reverse across implementations.
TYSv9rIhiQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlled evaluation of website-implementation sensitivity across agent types.
TYSv9rIhiQ.main_concern: The small website/task set and narrow constructed variants limit generalization to naturally diverse implementations.

zQJREErz9F.one_liner: Encoder-specific gradient gates learn where multimodal alignment updates enter heterogeneous encoders without changing the forward objective.
zQJREErz9F.problem: A scalar alignment weight cannot generally allocate alignment influence differently across modalities with unequal information quality.
zQJREErz9F.method: The paper introduces encoder-specific admission variables that scale shared alignment gradients while preserving the forward loss. A lightweight training-time controller maps task–alignment gradient interactions to admission levels and learns from training progress.
zQJREErz9F.key_idea: Gate alignment gradients separately for each encoder through admission variables while leaving the numerical forward objective unchanged.
zQJREErz9F.evidence: Theory distinguishes isotropic from asymmetric admission, and multi-seed experiments study heterogeneous sensing and ViT-B/16 RGB–event and RGB–sonar retrieval across three datasets.
zQJREErz9F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find encoder-specific backward allocation a clear, interpretable optimization perspective with a simple implementation.
zQJREErz9F.main_concern: The experiments do not convincingly establish the learned controller's advantage over scalar tuning or simpler allocation rules.

K6NFBKjxUN.one_liner: Sense-discriminative subspaces and selective model editing condition backdoor activation on particular meanings of polysemous words.
K6NFBKjxUN.problem: Contextual word meaning can trigger malicious LLM behavior without explicit lexical triggers, but this risk remains underexplored.
K6NFBKjxUN.method: SAB combines sense discrimination with selective model editing to isolate a discriminative sense subspace. Separate editing channels inject target behavior while preserving benign responses to other senses.
K6NFBKjxUN.key_idea: Project word-sense representations into a discriminative subspace and separate malicious injection from benign preservation through selective editing channels.
K6NFBKjxUN.evidence: Experiments on four public benchmarks and CW20 assess target-sense attack success and false triggering on non-target senses.
K6NFBKjxUN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find word-sense-specific backdoors an interesting fine-grained threat and recognize the motivation for selective editing.
K6NFBKjxUN.main_concern: The contribution is insufficiently distinguished from prior semantic and implicit-trigger backdoor attacks.

RzaonjomRu.one_liner: A diffusion generator co-trains with a forecaster to adapt synthetic time-series samples to downstream learning needs.
RzaonjomRu.problem: Small time-series datasets limit forecasting, while conventional augmentation may fail to generate useful training examples.
RzaonjomRu.method: DAD4TS jointly trains a diffusion-based generator and forecasting model, updating the generator according to generated-data usefulness. Mathematical transformations project time series into latent space instead of a conventional VAE.
RzaonjomRu.key_idea: Update synthetic-data generation alongside the forecaster using the generated samples' usefulness for prediction.
RzaonjomRu.evidence: Qualitative and quantitative experiments compare eight methods on six real-world datasets and six time-series forecasting models.
RzaonjomRu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider task-oriented augmentation under data scarcity practical and recognize broad dataset and model coverage.
RzaonjomRu.main_concern: Insufficient component ablations leave unclear whether diffusion, adaptive updates, and other modules are necessary for the gains.

rnW279hYev.one_liner: Teacher solutions seed reusable student prompts, refined and selected through label-free teacher–student answer agreement.
rnW279hYev.problem: Prompt distillation without labels can select shared teacher–student mistakes because teacher solutions are unverified.
rnW279hYev.method: K2P synthesizes prompts from teacher solutions and refines them using paired teacher and student responses. Agreement guides search, retained candidate archives, and selection on separate selection questions; deployment uses the frozen student and chosen prompt.
rnW279hYev.key_idea: Construct and refine reusable prompts from teacher responses, retaining candidates for answer-agreement-based selection without ground-truth labels.
rnW279hYev.evidence: Three-seed comparisons cover four tasks and two students, with label-free and supervised baselines, refinement ablations, archive diagnostics, and conditional accuracy theory.
rnW279hYev.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value improving frozen students without labels and recognize strong results against label-free prompt-optimization baselines.
rnW279hYev.main_concern: Nearly error-free teachers fail to stress the imperfect-reference problem that motivates the label-free method.

RlNz9XOG1a.one_liner: Post-episode reflection revises external language rules while GRPO trains agents to use the evolving state.
RlNz9XOG1a.problem: Reinforcement learning often stores acquired task knowledge implicitly rather than as inspectable and reusable rules.
RlNz9XOG1a.method: ELSA maintains an external language state that conditions action selection and language-based value and world-model reasoning within each episode. Between episodes, reflection updates the state and GRPO trains the policy from sparse outcomes.
RlNz9XOG1a.key_idea: Alternate reflection-based updates of explicit language state with policy optimization that learns to use that state.
RlNz9XOG1a.evidence: Four symbolic text-observable environments test unknown-rule interaction against prompting and policy-training controls, with state-intervention and refinement ablations.
RlNz9XOG1a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize effective interaction-based learning and controls showing the value of external state and its refinement.
RlNz9XOG1a.main_concern: Missing comparisons with related reflection-memory and policy-learning combinations leave ELSA's additional contribution unclear.

gtpwYkRqV6.one_liner: Paired harness swaps and unchanged reruns separate coding-agent cost differences from model-specific accuracy effects and sampling noise.
gtpwYkRqV6.problem: Reported harness gains often lack a rerun baseline showing whether accuracy changes exceed ordinary execution variability.
gtpwYkRqV6.method: The study holds models and tasks fixed while swapping production harnesses and rerunning unchanged configurations. Paired outcome analyses and token-cost decomposition assess model-dependent harness effects.
gtpwYkRqV6.key_idea: Compare task-outcome changes from harness swaps against changes from rerunning the same model–harness configuration.
gtpwYkRqV6.evidence: Seven models run through Claude Code, mini-SWE-agent, and OpenCode on SWE-bench Verified and two other benchmarks, with paired tests and cost analysis.
gtpwYkRqV6.claimed_gains: Where bounded, harness differences are 2 to 5 points; OpenCode trails by 8 to 9 points on one model and leads by 14 on another, while cost differences range from under 10% to 3 to 4 times.
gtpwYkRqV6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical harness question and the careful decomposition of token costs.
gtpwYkRqV6.main_concern: Too few replications and limited statistical power prevent broad conclusions that harnesses have little effect on accuracy.

VQTNpZC8sO.one_liner: Distills client-specific prediction corrections into shared specialty adapters and routes their responses within personalized federated models.
VQTNpZC8sO.problem: Personalized federated models retain client-specific class weaknesses because locally acquired strengths remain difficult to transfer across clients.
VQTNpZC8sO.method: FedConsult identifies specialties from differences between global and personalized predictions, then distills similar correction patterns into adapters in a shared feature space. Recipient clients combine adapter responses through response-aware sparse routing.
VQTNpZC8sO.key_idea: Cluster global-to-personalized prediction corrections into specialty adapters and route their responses through each recipient's personalized prediction pathway.
VQTNpZC8sO.evidence: Experiments on natural and medical image classification benchmarks assess overall accuracy and client-specific weak-class accuracy.
VQTNpZC8sO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value transferring complementary client capabilities through lightweight adapters compatible with personalized prediction pathways.
VQTNpZC8sO.main_concern: Comparisons omit directly relevant multi-expert methods, leaving the advantage over existing expert-sharing frameworks unclear.

tY7H9zoVkl.one_liner: Combines GRPO with bounded teacher guidance restricted to failed trajectories and scaled by group difficulty.
tY7H9zoVkl.problem: Token-local distillation ignores trajectory correctness, while group-relative reinforcement learning supplies coarse credit and no signal for all-failure groups.
tY7H9zoVkl.method: DiffGate adds selective teacher supervision to GRPO using verifier outcomes to select failed trajectories. It weights this guidance by group difficulty and smoothly bounds teacher-student discrepancies.
tY7H9zoVkl.key_idea: Apply difficulty-weighted, smoothly bounded teacher updates only to verifier-rejected trajectories alongside GRPO.
tY7H9zoVkl.evidence: Reviewers describe experiments across student model sizes on mathematical reasoning and code generation, with baseline comparisons and ablations.
tY7H9zoVkl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combination understandable and reasonably motivated, with teacher guidance supplying signals when student rollouts fail.
tY7H9zoVkl.main_concern: Reviewers question the technical contribution beyond existing OPD-GRPO combinations and the evidence that its added gating and bounding are necessary.

Q5eTfJJwnQ.one_liner: Decomposes hidden coding tasks across pull requests to study when gradual attacks evade diff-based monitors.
Q5eTfJJwnQ.problem: It remains unclear when distributing malicious work across pull requests makes attacks harder for code monitors to detect.
Q5eTfJJwnQ.method: The study defines decomposability criteria and builds side tasks for comparing gradual attacks with their best single-PR placement. Controlled monitor inputs and activation probes examine factors behind detection differences.
Q5eTfJJwnQ.key_idea: Split a hidden side task into individually less suspicious pull-request components and compare monitoring against the best single-request placement.
Q5eTfJJwnQ.evidence: The evaluation covers more than 11,000 trajectories from four attacker models and eight monitor models on cache-poisoning and credential-exfiltration tasks.
Q5eTfJJwnQ.claimed_gains: Qwen3.8-27B's gradual cache-poisoning attacks show significant evasion advantages in 41 of 252 comparisons after Holm correction, with none in the other direction.
Q5eTfJJwnQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the careful evaluation against the best single-PR placement, including detection calibration and controls.
Q5eTfJJwnQ.main_concern: Task restrictions may make single-PR attacks conspicuously out of scope, confounding the measured advantage of distributing attacks.

JhKbGJ5VSq.one_liner: Re-equilibrates persistent sphere packings and rebuilds tetrahedral connectivity to preserve interior-node identities during large shape changes.
JhKbGJ5VSq.problem: Fixed-connectivity meshes degrade during large deformations, while fresh remeshing loses interior-node correspondence needed for computational design.
JhKbGJ5VSq.method: JamTet combines octree-based sphere packing with constrained Delaunay tetrahedralization and re-equilibrates the same spheres as shapes change. A differentiable JAX simulator connects these meshes to soft-robot morphology optimization.
JhKbGJ5VSq.key_idea: Carry interior-node identities on persistent spheres while rebuilding mesh boundaries and connectivity after each shape change.
JhKbGJ5VSq.evidence: Static meshing comparisons, sphere-to-bunny morphing, and soft-robot design experiments assess element quality, inversions, and swimming fitness.
JhKbGJ5VSq.claimed_gains: Interior-node gradients improve swimming fitness by 0.73–1.07 over a matched surface-only variant, while voxelized versions yield 32–63% lower fitness.
JhKbGJ5VSq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical sphere-packing mechanism and its preservation of interior-node identities during deformation.
JhKbGJ5VSq.main_concern: Quantitative morphing evidence covers only one shape pair, leaving behavior on thin features, concave shapes, and broader deformations uncertain.

lC1U96Au7V.one_liner: Compiles separately editable transition contributions into a fixed-shape memory field that modulates a frozen language agent.
lC1U96Au7V.problem: Language-agent memories struggle to combine record-level editability with compact access that avoids textual retrieval and replay.
lC1U96Au7V.method: RCMF assigns each decision transition an identifiable parametric contribution and aggregates contributions into a field queried by the current state. Additive insertion or removal edits individual records without retraining the frozen model or recompiling other records.
lC1U96Au7V.key_idea: Sum independently attributable transition-memory contributions into a fixed-shape field, enabling additive record edits and state-conditioned reads.
lC1U96Au7V.evidence: Experiments on AppWorld, ALFWorld, and WebShop compare task performance against multiple memory baselines.
lC1U96Au7V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that the additive construction combines identifiable, editable records with memory-count-independent runtime reads.
lC1U96Au7V.main_concern: Missing raw-text replay comparisons using the same Selector leave the advantage of parametric access over equivalent textual memory unclear.

6NRajskPa3.one_liner: Synthesizes paper-grounded reproduction examples and checklist rewards to train a compact paper-to-code model through supervised learning and reinforcement learning.
6NRajskPa3.problem: Paper-repository pairs do not supply the intermediate supervision and implementation-fidelity feedback needed to learn faithful paper reproduction.
6NRajskPa3.method: ReSpec filters paper-repository pairs for implementation fidelity and generates examples for six reproduction subtasks. Paper-grounded checklists provide process rewards for plan construction and file-level code writing during task-decomposed reinforcement learning after supervised fine-tuning.
6NRajskPa3.key_idea: Convert paper specifications into synthetic intermediate targets and checklist-based rewards for separate planning and code-writing tasks.
6NRajskPa3.evidence: The data engine uses 6,172 paper-repository pairs, 430,428 supervised examples, and 76,448 reinforcement-learning samples, with evaluation on PaperBench Code-Dev.
6NRajskPa3.claimed_gains: ReSpec scores 65.6% vs. 65.4% for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B using one-sixth as many active parameters (0.5B vs. 3B), with matched two-pass refinement yielding 70.6% and 69.9%.
6NRajskPa3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large automatically constructed process-supervision dataset and the observed improvement from reinforcement learning.
6NRajskPa3.main_concern: Reviewers note that the advantage over Qwen3.5-35B-A3B is small when inference scaffolds match, weakening the headline comparison.

Hzn5u3JP0l.one_liner: Benchmarks specification, annotation, and proof generation for fixed C programs using reference artifacts and machine-checked semantic comparisons.
Hzn5u3JP0l.problem: Existing verification benchmarks often let models generate the code they verify or supply specifications, obscuring capabilities on fixed algorithmic programs.
Hzn5u3JP0l.method: PV-Bench supplies expert-reviewed specifications and QCP verification artifacts for fixed C programs, then evaluates specification generation, annotation generation, and residual Rocq proof completion independently. Proofs and refutations compare candidate specifications with reference contracts, with human review for undecided cases.
Hzn5u3JP0l.key_idea: Hold C implementations fixed and isolate specification, annotation, and proof generation using reference artifacts and machine-checked contract equivalence.
Hzn5u3JP0l.evidence: The benchmark contains 233 programs, including 147 accepted Codeforces solutions rated from 800 to 2800, plus algorithms, data structures, and library routines.
Hzn5u3JP0l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of evaluating fixed C programs that combine algorithmic reasoning with explicit memory manipulation.
Hzn5u3JP0l.main_concern: The fidelity of reference specifications needs stronger justification because implementation-specific requirements could reject valid alternative contracts.

VwrRD81GLa.one_liner: Decomposes shared output error to explain hidden-unit saturation and learning stalls in direct feedback alignment.
VwrRD81GLa.problem: Direct feedback alignment can stall near class-frequency prediction even when hidden features still encode class information.
VwrRD81GLa.method: The paper derives a mean-covariance decomposition and an approximate model of shared-error-driven saturation. Selective removal and feedback-routing controls test the mechanism, while centering interventions separate shared from input-dependent teaching signals.
VwrRD81GLa.key_idea: Separate common output error from input-dependent feedback to expose and control hidden mean drift, saturation, and suppressed feature amplitude.
VwrRD81GLa.evidence: Reduced-model predictions and controlled experiments examine tanh networks, persistent sign feedback under SGD and Adam, and a normalized Transformer.
VwrRD81GLa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mechanistic decomposition and quantitative account connecting shared error to saturation and learning behavior.
VwrRD81GLa.main_concern: Reviewers question practical significance because the strongest evidence concerns specialized fixed-feedback settings and adaptive optimization shortens the stalls.

mIhPdwPhK8.one_liner: VTU routes query-relevant coarse image regions into fine-grained tokens inserted before the segmentation token.
mIhPdwPhK8.problem: Spatially compressed visual tokens discard local detail needed for precise segmentation of boundaries and complex objects.
mIhPdwPhK8.method: VTU first processes coarse visual tokens for global image-query understanding, then uses a lightweight router to select regions for fine-grained token insertion before the segmentation token. Mixed-region router supervision and simple-sample skipping control which additional tokens are introduced.
mIhPdwPhK8.key_idea: Query-guided routing inserts selected fine-grained visual features into the language-model sequence immediately before segmentation-token generation.
mIhPdwPhK8.evidence: InternVL3 2B and 8B experiments cover referring, generalized referring, reasoning, and semantic segmentation, with ablations of routing, supervision, and token selection.
mIhPdwPhK8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the local-detail motivation and routing design coherent and acknowledge strong results across segmentation tasks.
mIhPdwPhK8.main_concern: The contribution of fine-grained detail is not fully isolated from input formatting, model capacity, or unmatched training and token budgets.

XEG92F8KVG.one_liner: Analyzes how sparse autoencoders tile character-count manifolds and tests latent clustering to uncover modular hex-count representations.
XEG92F8KVG.problem: Automated methods that cluster sparse autoencoder latents to discover multidimensional feature manifolds remain poorly validated on how cleanly they recover underlying activation geometry.
XEG92F8KVG.method: The authors conduct a mechanistic case study of character-count representations in language models, characterizing how sparse autoencoders tile the manifold and testing whether SAE latent clustering recovers clean raw-activation subspaces. Applying lessons from this diagnostic, they probe hexadecimal string distributions to identify and intervene on modular character-count representations.
XEG92F8KVG.key_idea: Audit SAE latent-clustering manifold discovery against known character-count tiling geometry and probe activation subspaces on hexadecimal strings for modular counting structures.
XEG92F8KVG.evidence: Evaluated via SAE tiling diagnostics, latent clustering subspace noise analyses, and activation probing and steering on prose and hexadecimal character-counting tasks in language models.
XEG92F8KVG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the deep case study provides a useful reality check on automated SAE latent clustering and uncovers modular (mod 8, 4, 2) character-counting structures.
XEG92F8KVG.main_concern: Reviewers note that the empirical scope is restricted solely to character counting without testing other manifolds, and that key quantitative and steering results are relegated to the appendix.

WGcEYbY800.one_liner: Supervises layout, object, and view latent tokens with VGGT 3D features during SFT and masked-span GRPO.
WGcEYbY800.problem: Textual chain-of-thought does not constrain spatial hidden states in multi-view VLMs, while single-level 3D latent reasoning lacks multi-granular scene, object, and view structure.
WGcEYbY800.method: H3D-LVR structures a VLM's reasoning trace around three generated latent spans—scene layout, key objects, and input views—supervised during SFT via feature reconstruction against VGGT-derived 3D features under teacher forcing. Answer-level GRPO with hidden-state replay and full-span loss masking further refines reasoning without corrupting latent semantics, requiring only images and prompts at inference.
WGcEYbY800.key_idea: Supervise interleaved layout, object, and view latent spans with VGGT 3D features during SFT, then refine answers via GRPO with hidden-state replay and span masking.
WGcEYbY800.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen2.5-VL-7B across multi-view spatial reasoning benchmarks including MindCube-Tiny, SPAR-Bench, and out-of-domain MMSI without 3D tools at inference.
WGcEYbY800.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that supervising multi-granular 3D latent spans only during training keeps inference lightweight and produces large in-domain accuracy gains on MindCube-Tiny and SPAR.
WGcEYbY800.main_concern: Reviewers uniformly cite the absence of a matched text-only CoT SFT baseline trained on the same Gemini-generated reasoning data without latent tokens to isolate hierarchical latent supervision.

scT7T8JiAM.one_liner: Subtracts token-level score shifts induced by random reference messages during hindsight self-distillation from user feedback.
scT7T8JiAM.problem: Self-distillation methods that re-score a model's prior response conditioned on the next user message suffer from large, response-dependent score shifts induced even by empty templates or unrelated messages.
scT7T8JiAM.method: The authors show that message-independent background shifts enter hindsight token scores additively and therefore cancel under contrast. Contrastive Self-Distillation (CoSD) contrasts token-level score changes under the actual follow-up user message against average scores under a few randomly sampled reference messages from other interactions.
scT7T8JiAM.key_idea: Cancel response-dependent background score shifts in feedback-conditioned self-distillation by contrasting real follow-up message token scores against randomly sampled reference messages.
scT7T8JiAM.evidence: Supported by an additive background cancellation analysis, empty and random-feedback diagnostics, and on-policy and off-policy experiments across multiple LLM families and two real-world interaction datasets.
scT7T8JiAM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that empty and unrelated follow-up messages demonstrably confound SDPO score shifts and that contrasting against random reference messages is a simple, reward-model-free fix.
scT7T8JiAM.main_concern: Reviewers point to a sign mismatch between the Bayesian hindsight theory and instruction-prefixed prompts, sensitivity to reference-message distribution mismatches, and missing comparison against contrastive self-distillation (CREDIT).

GIfar6q7aw.one_liner: Triggers memory-guided reflection via a hidden-state hesitation probe and internalizes adaptations through hindsight on-policy self-distillation.
GIfar6q7aw.problem: Memory-augmented LLM agents rely on hallucination-prone self-evaluation to decide when to reflect and keep learned experience external to model weights, causing repeated retrieval overhead.
GIfar6q7aw.method: Thinking Mode-Aware (TMA) memory trains a linear discriminant probe on hidden states of confident versus hesitant CoT segments to compute a hesitation score that selectively triggers trajectory-memory reflection. An on-policy self-distillation stage then uses a hindsight-conditioned teacher with successful trajectories and reflections to supervise the student on its own rollouts.
GIfar6q7aw.key_idea: Trigger memory-backed reflection using a linear discriminant hesitation probe on CoT hidden states and distill hindsight-guided reflections into policy parameters on student rollouts.
GIfar6q7aw.evidence: Evaluated on interactive agent tasks including ALFWorld and WebShop with ablations comparing LDA hesitation triggering against periodic triggering and LLM self-evaluation.
GIfar6q7aw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that probing CoT hidden states to detect hesitation triggers reflection without extra LLM calls and outperforms periodic or self-evaluated triggering on ALFWorld.
GIfar6q7aw.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about generalization and statistical robustness given the small (~491-493 sample) poorly documented probe training set, single-run evaluations, and incomplete OPSD results on WebShop.

81Baa0RYLy.one_liner: Maps teacher hidden states into student-usable representations via downstream-trained projectors before on-policy hidden-state distillation.
81Baa0RYLy.problem: On-policy output distillation leaves intermediate student computation unsupervised, while naive hidden-state matching fails when geometrically aligned teacher states are unusable by downstream student layers.
81Baa0RYLy.method: On-Policy Mechanism Distillation (OPMD) first builds a student-compatible teacher by training projectors so transformed teacher representations function directly inside the frozen student's downstream computation. In a second stage, the student internalizes these compatible intermediate states along its own on-policy rollouts.
81Baa0RYLy.key_idea: Construct student-compatible intermediate targets by training teacher-to-student projectors through frozen downstream student layers, then distill those targets along on-policy student trajectories.
81Baa0RYLy.evidence: Evaluated across three single-teacher settings (including RL-Math to Qwen3-1.7B on AMC, AIME24, and AIME25), multi-teacher distillation, and cross-family SFT, alongside weight-patching analyses.
81Baa0RYLy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that operationalizing compatibility via usability in the student's downstream layers rather than geometric MSE is well motivated and yields consistent mathematical reasoning gains.
81Baa0RYLy.main_concern: Reviewers note that Stage II is never compared against output-only on-policy distillation from the constructed intermediate teacher, leaving hidden-state supervision confounded with teacher-assistant bridging.

mKxwjnvMVf.one_liner: Shrinks per-class training pools to show the easy-versus-coverage coreset crossover stabilizes in samples per class, not fraction.
mKxwjnvMVf.problem: Evaluating coreset selection at fixed dataset fractions obscures regime comparisons because the crossover budget between easy-sample selection and coverage-based selection shifts across dataset sizes.
mKxwjnvMVf.method: The authors measure the crossover budget m0 between an easy-sample learnability selector (LFrac) and a coverage selector (Herding) while systematically shrinking per-class pool sizes by up to 8.4x and varying selectors, learners, optimizer steps, and effective image resolution. This nested pool-shrinking protocol tests whether m0 scales with dataset fraction or stays invariant in absolute samples per class.
mKxwjnvMVf.key_idea: Measure the easy-sample-to-coverage crossover budget across nested per-class pool reductions to test invariance in absolute samples per class versus dataset fraction.
mKxwjnvMVf.evidence: Evaluated across four datasets including ImageNet-1k, ImageNet-100, and CIFAR-100 under nested pool shrinking, two easy-sample selectors, two coverage anchors, two convolutional learners, equalized steps, and 49x pixel-count reduction.
mKxwjnvMVf.claimed_gains: Shrinking ImageNet-100's per-class pool by 8.4x keeps m0 between 65 and 80 samples per class while its fraction drifts by roughly 10x, and reducing effective pixel count by 49x lowers full-data accuracy by 7.4 points while moving m0 only from about 66 to 80.
mKxwjnvMVf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that questioning fixed-fraction coreset reporting is worthwhile and that the nested pool-shrinking experiment cleanly falsifies fraction-indexed scaling of the crossover boundary.
mKxwjnvMVf.main_concern: Reviewers note sensitivity of m0 to the feature-extractor instrument (shifting nearly 2x on CIFAR-100), missing recent budget-adaptive coreset baselines, and unclear motivation for the image-downsampling intervention.

P6e88OmcB9.one_liner: Represents PDE solution operators as continuous fields of task-adaptive Gaussian radial basis functions with parent-child sharing.
P6e88OmcB9.problem: Conventional physics-informed operator networks rely on abstract latent basis representations that lack explicit, interpretable, task-dependent spatial geometry.
P6e88OmcB9.method: KAPI-ONet encodes functional inputs with a Gaussian-splat functional autoencoder (GSFAE) and predicts PDE solutions as continuous fields of task-adaptive Gaussian radial basis functions parameterized by centers, scales, orientations, and coefficients. A hierarchical parent-child construction shares geometric transformations across child kernels while keeping coefficients independent to reduce output parameter complexity.
P6e88OmcB9.key_idea: Parameterize physics-informed PDE solution operators as continuous task-adaptive Gaussian RBF fields compressed via parent-child shared geometric transformations and a Gaussian-splat input encoder.
P6e88OmcB9.evidence: Supported by approximation and geometric-sharing error analyses alongside experiments on forward and inverse PDEs, parametric flows, and weakly supervised biomedical problems.
P6e88OmcB9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit task-conditioned Gaussian kernel geometry with hierarchical parent-child sharing provides a compact, inspectable alternative to standard latent operator bases across diverse PDE tasks.
P6e88OmcB9.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations against globally shared kernel geometry with task-only coefficients, potential OOD bottlenecks from freezing GSFAE on fine-scale fields, and evaluation mainly on smooth 1D and 2D problems.

tuVoXYPM4s.one_liner: Compiles an internal tool-source detector and residual-stream behavioral correction into two existing SwiGLU neurons against prompt injection.
tuVoXYPM4s.problem: Language models internally represent whether instructions originate from untrusted tool outputs yet still execute injected instructions due to a source-behavior dissociation.
tuVoXYPM4s.method: After identifying that tool-originating instructions remain linearly separable in hidden states, the method compiles a localized defense directly into two existing SwiGLU neurons without adding parameters or external modules. An internal tool-content signal gates when the edit activates, while a learned residual-stream vector writes a behavioral correction to restore benign execution under attack.
tuVoXYPM4s.key_idea: Repurpose two existing SwiGLU neurons to gate on internal tool-source representations and write a learned residual-stream behavioral correction under prompt injection.
tuVoXYPM4s.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen models from 4B to 27B (primarily Qwen3.6-27B) on AgentDojo indirect prompt injection and benign utility benchmarks.
tuVoXYPM4s.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.6-27B, the method reduces AgentDojo attack success from 28.9% to 0.9% while maintaining clean utility at 90.7%.
tuVoXYPM4s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying the source-behavior gap motivates a minimal, parameter-free two-neuron edit that substantially lowers indirect prompt injection success with minimal utility drift.
tuVoXYPM4s.main_concern: Reviewers cite weak baseline comparisons omitting established prompt-injection defenses (such as Meta SecAlign, ASIDE, or PromptGuard), Qwen and SwiGLU-only evaluation, and vulnerability to white-box adaptive attacks.

J1n76ATXpB.one_liner: Replays fixed browser actions to return visual and structural diffs for multi-agent software repair and self-distillation.
J1n76ATXpB.problem: Software engineering LLM agents struggle with UI and layout bugs due to weak visual grounding, lack of execution-based visual verification, and scarce multimodal training data.
J1n76ATXpB.method: DuoAgent coordinates an orchestrator, a reproducer that builds a browser sandbox and fixed defect-triggering action sequence, a solver proposing patches, and a verifier that replays the actions to return visual and structural trace diagnoses. It pairs this harness with synthetic sandbox perturbation from 100 seeds and diagnosis-conditioned on-policy self-distillation (DuoOPSD).
J1n76ATXpB.key_idea: Ground repository-level UI bug repair in deterministic browser-action replay that returns visual and structural trace diffs for iterative solving and on-policy self-distillation.
J1n76ATXpB.evidence: Evaluated on a multimodal browser software engineering benchmark across multiple agent harnesses (including Codex and Claude Fable 5.1) and open models (Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-4-E4B) trained with DuoOPSD.
J1n76ATXpB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that converting visual bug reports into deterministic browser sandboxes with replayed action traces provides automated execution-grounded verification and enables effective self-distillation.
J1n76ATXpB.main_concern: Reviewers note missing component ablations of the DuoAgent harness itself (replay, visual versus structural diagnosis, and learned skills), unmeasured verifier accuracy against hidden tests, and single-benchmark evaluation.

VFwbVsF2lE.one_liner: Tests majority-voted LLM safety panels under shared misleading peer messages and restores accuracy using pre-message independent votes.
VFwbVsF2lE.problem: Combining LLM safety judges via majority voting assumes error reduction, but exposing panel members to a shared misleading peer message beforehand can trigger conformity that amplifies errors.
VFwbVsF2lE.method: Holding six open-weight LLM reviewers and the majority-voting rule fixed across six safety datasets, the authors compare panel false-alarm rates when reviewers vote independently versus after seeing a shared misleading peer message. They model error aggregation via individual flip rates and test hybrid panels that retain a subset of pre-message independent votes.
VFwbVsF2lE.key_idea: Expose fixed LLM moderation panels to a shared misleading peer judgment before voting and replace half the votes with pre-message judgments.
VFwbVsF2lE.evidence: Evaluated across six open-weight LLMs and six safety moderation datasets alongside Poisson-binomial independence calculations and vote-threshold analyses.
VFwbVsF2lE.claimed_gains: Under silent peers, the panel's false-alarm rate on benign items is 42.0% versus the 55.7% reviewer average, whereas under wrong peers reviewers falsely flag 86.5% on average, the panel flags 100% of benign items, and keeping three of six pre-message votes restores the panel's advantage.
VFwbVsF2lE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled message-swap experiment cleanly demonstrates how conformity flips majority voting from error correction to error amplification, backed by exact Poisson-binomial validation.
VFwbVsF2lE.main_concern: Reviewers note that comparing silent against wrong peers conflates label presence with label incorrectness, assumes all reviewers simultaneously see the same wrong signal, and lacks deeper mechanistic analysis.

p9s6j9oq4g.one_liner: Decomposes visuomotor policy activations with a sparse autoencoder to detect execution anomalies and attribute failures to named concepts.
p9s6j9oq4g.problem: Observing external robot behavior during manipulation failures reveals little about which internal visuomotor policy representations caused the error.
p9s6j9oq4g.method: MIND trains a sparse autoencoder on internal activations of a visuomotor policy, grounds individual latent features against robot state, motion, surroundings, and closed-loop steering effects, and learns normal versus failure-bound feature dynamics across executions. At runtime, it monitors deviations in these temporal feature patterns and attributes flagged failures to the highest-contributing named features.
p9s6j9oq4g.key_idea: Decompose visuomotor policy activations via a sparse autoencoder into state-grounded concepts and monitor deviations in their temporal execution statistics for unified failure detection and diagnosis.
p9s6j9oq4g.evidence: Evaluated on failure detection, concept naming precision, closed-loop feature steering, and root-cause diagnosis in simulated and physical robot manipulation tasks.
p9s6j9oq4g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying runtime failure detection and human-interpretable root-cause diagnosis through the same named sparse autoencoder features and closed-loop steering is practically informative.
p9s6j9oq4g.main_concern: Reviewers point out that concept naming relies on a predefined concept vocabulary unable to diagnose unanticipated out-of-vocabulary failure modes, alongside incremental design over prior VLA SAE and linear-probe methods.

cj0slSTSMP.one_liner: Projects multidimensional hidden tensors into compact Tucker cores to perform subquadratic self-attention and linear projections.
cj0slSTSMP.problem: Standard self-attention incurs quadratic computational cost that limits scaling to long spatiotemporal sequences from multidimensional data.
cj0slSTSMP.method: Tucker Bottleneck Attention (TuBA) projects multidimensional hidden tensors via mode-wise factors into compact low-rank Tucker cores, executes multi-head self-attention and Q/K/V linear projections inside the core, and maps updates back to the ambient space. Its autoregressive variant combines bidirectional mixing within cores with block-causal attention across cores.
cj0slSTSMP.key_idea: Project multidimensional hidden states into low-rank Tucker cores, execute Q/K/V projections and attention on the core, and reconstruct ambient updates.
cj0slSTSMP.evidence: Evaluated on video prediction (including KittiCaltech) and global weather forecasting in both standard and autoregressive settings using shared transformer backbones.
cj0slSTSMP.claimed_gains: Compared with standard self-attention, TuBA reduces error and computation by up to 24.7% and 66.6% in video prediction and by 18.9% and 79.4% in weather forecasting with up to 4.84x speedups, while using 5-6x fewer FLOPs in autoregressive forecasting.
cj0slSTSMP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that performing both linear projections and attention inside a compressed Tucker core is clean, easy to integrate, and evaluated fairly under shared transformer backbones.
cj0slSTSMP.main_concern: Reviewers question how much gain stems from low-rank Tucker structure versus generic latent bottlenecking (since full-rank TuBA already beats ViT) and note missing citation and comparison to TEAFormers.

PeYuOqj9Ov.one_liner: Evolves external LLM-agent procedural skills by contrasting incremental skill revision with full skill reconstruction via pairwise preference recombination.
PeYuOqj9Ov.problem: Continual evolution of external procedural skills in frozen-parameter LLM agents is highly sensitive to initial skill quality, often causing persistent bias or negative learning gains.
PeYuOqj9Ov.method: From shared interaction experiences, Skill-CoE generates two candidate updates—revising the current skill and reconstructing a skill from scratch—and compares their task executions against the current skill as a reference. Using a pairwise preference objective, it recombines complementary procedures from both candidates before validation-gated acceptance.
PeYuOqj9Ov.key_idea: Generate both revised and reconstructed skill candidates from new agent experiences, compare their executions against the current skill via pairwise preference, and recombine complementary procedures.
PeYuOqj9Ov.evidence: Continual agent learning experiments across diverse initial-skill difficulty groups (Easy, Medium, Hard) and multiple LLM backbones (per reviews).
PeYuOqj9Ov.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing initialization sensitivity in non-parametric skill evolution is well motivated and that contrasting revision with reconstruction stabilizes continual gains across starting skills.
PeYuOqj9Ov.main_concern: Generating, executing, iteratively recombining, and validation-gating multiple skill candidates per batch introduces substantial unquantified rollout and LLM-call overhead relative to baselines.

Mr7Agljwss.one_liner: Reallocates GRPO rollout groups across coding harnesses to optimize taskwise co-success with marginal joint credit and localized schema penalties.
Mr7Agljwss.problem: Mixed-harness RL for coding agents maximizes average reward rather than taskwise co-success, leaving agents failing or emitting foreign tool schemas on the same task under different harnesses.
Mr7Agljwss.method: JH-GRPO splits each task's fixed rollout group across native coding harnesses without extra rollouts, optimizing a Joint Harness Coverage Utility via trajectory-specific Marginal Joint Advantage. It pairs this credit assignment with harness-conditional constraints that localize penalties to invalid and foreign-schema tool-call spans.
Mr7Agljwss.key_idea: Partition each task's fixed GRPO rollout group across coding harnesses and assign marginal higher-order co-success credit alongside span-localized penalties for invalid or foreign-schema tool calls.
Mr7Agljwss.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B across four coding harnesses and four software-engineering benchmarks under matched compute using Pass@1 and Joint Harness Reliability (JHR).
Mr7Agljwss.claimed_gains: Improves macro Pass@1 from 48.8% to 53.7%, JHR@4 from 24.6% to 35.8%, worst-harness Pass@1 by 6.6 percentage points, and unseen-harness Pass@1 by 3.5 percentage points while reducing foreign-schema violations by 46.4%.
Mr7Agljwss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing taskwise cross-harness co-success rather than mean Pass@1 addresses an important deployment reliability gap in coding agents with strong matched-compute gains.
Mr7Agljwss.main_concern: Ablations do not clearly separate Marginal Joint Advantage from simpler counterfactual or difference-reward reweighting, nor isolate span-localized adaptive tool penalties from trajectory-wide fixed penalties.

e5rlO61XDB.one_liner: Replaces nested PINN reverse-mode autodiff with dual-number plus finite-difference derivatives and initializes long-horizon windows via parameter-trajectory regression.
e5rlO61XDB.problem: Physics-informed neural networks incur slow, memory-intensive nested backward passes for higher-order PDE derivatives and frequently collapse to trivial solutions over long time horizons.
e5rlO61XDB.method: Regressive Dual-PINN (RD-PINN) computes exact first-order derivatives with dual numbers and second-order derivatives via finite differences (Dual-FD) to avoid nested reverse-mode differentiation. Across sequential time windows, regressive initialization predicts each new window's starting parameters by regressing over parameter trajectories from earlier windows.
e5rlO61XDB.key_idea: Compute PINN PDE residuals using exact dual-number first derivatives plus one finite difference, and initialize successive time-window models by regressing prior windows' parameters.
e5rlO61XDB.evidence: Evaluated across seven PDE problems (including five extended-horizon unsteady PDEs), 10 PINN architectures, and 24 paired 2D speedup and peak-memory comparisons.
e5rlO61XDB.claimed_gains: Across 24 paired 2D comparisons, Dual-FD achieves a 2.42× median speedup (9.68× maximum) and lowers peak memory in 21 of 22 comparisons, while sustaining long-horizon accuracy across five unsteady PDEs.
e5rlO61XDB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Dual-FD provides consistent 2D training speedups and memory reductions while window-marching RD-PINN preserves physical dynamics over extended time horizons.
e5rlO61XDB.main_concern: Reviewers find combining dual numbers, finite differences, and parameter extrapolation methodologically incremental, noting missing comparisons against established fast-derivative PINNs (DOF, CAN-PINN, STDE) and simple warm-start weight copying.

7XwfLhMTul.one_liner: Guides sequential molecular lead edits from a frozen chemical language model using multi-objective Metropolis-Hastings sampling at inference time.
7XwfLhMTul.problem: RL post-training for multi-objective molecular lead optimization requires costly task-specific datasets, whereas zero-shot generation from pretrained chemical language models under-explores valid scaffold-preserving edits.
7XwfLhMTul.method: ReMedI uses a pretrained molecular language model as a sequential edit proposer conditioned on the current molecule and target objectives, accepting or rejecting edits via Metropolis-Hastings refinement balancing property improvement, preservation, and lead similarity. Search trajectories generated at inference time can also be distilled back into the model.
7XwfLhMTul.key_idea: Propose sequential molecular edits with a frozen chemical language model and filter transitions via Metropolis-Hastings under a joint property-improvement, preservation, and similarity objective.
7XwfLhMTul.evidence: Evaluated across three chemical language model backbones on the C-MuMOInstruct and SMDD multi-objective lead-optimization benchmarks, including search-trace distillation.
7XwfLhMTul.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing LLM edit proposals with explicit multi-objective Metropolis-Hastings acceptance is flexible and practical for scaffold-constrained lead optimization across backbones.
7XwfLhMTul.main_concern: Experiments compare mainly against C-MORAL while omitting established MCMC and iterative molecular optimization baselines (such as MARS, GEGL, and GP-MoLFormer-Sim) and without equalizing oracle/proposal budgets.

3kjAj38q4J.one_liner: Executes sequential narrow full-depth subnetworks conditioned on earlier stages to learn complementary features for early-exit inference.
3kjAj38q4J.problem: Attaching early-exit classifiers along a single shared backbone restricts early predictors to shallow features and creates interference between immediate classification and downstream representations.
3kjAj38q4J.method: Instead of exiting at intermediate layers of one network, the framework organizes adaptive inference as a sequence of complete, narrow full-depth subnetworks applied to the input image. Later subnetworks condition on representations already computed by earlier subnetworks so they learn complementary features.
3kjAj38q4J.key_idea: Decouple early exits from shallow prefixes by running sequential narrow full-depth subnetworks where each later subnetwork conditions on earlier subnetworks' representations.
3kjAj38q4J.evidence: Evaluated with stage-wise CNNs on ImageNet classification alongside GPU and Raspberry Pi 4 CPU latency measurements (per reviews).
3kjAj38q4J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coherent architectural principle separating sequential early-exit execution from shared-prefix depth constraints and note strong low-FLOPs accuracy.
3kjAj38q4J.main_concern: Executing k full-depth subnetworks sequentially increases critical-path depth and degrades parallel GPU latency, while evaluations are restricted to stage-wise CNNs on ImageNet classification.

sKnrd8SViL.one_liner: Derives bias-free polyhedral conic decision geometry from scale invariance and optimizes representations with a von Mises-Fisher Bhattacharyya error bound.
sKnrd8SViL.problem: It is unclear what exact invariance and readout conditions yield convex conic class decision regions and how to optimize hyperspherical class separation under scarce labels.
sKnrd8SViL.method: The authors prove that positive-scaling invariance combined with an invariant affine Bayes readout produces bias-free representations and polyhedral convex decision cones, while separability and positive angular margin ensure pointed support containment. Under a shared-concentration von Mises-Fisher model with equal priors, they train representations by minimizing a closed-form pairwise Bhattacharyya overlap error bound.
sKnrd8SViL.key_idea: Pair bias-free positively homogeneous networks from scale-invariant affine Bayes readouts with a closed-form pairwise von Mises-Fisher Bhattacharyya error-bound loss.
sKnrd8SViL.evidence: Theoretical characterizations of conic decision regions and supports, plus a five-seed, 30-condition factorial study on 15%-labeled CIFAR-100 measuring accuracy, shifted calibration, and density-based OOD detection.
sKnrd8SViL.claimed_gains: On CIFAR-100 with 15% labels, reaches 71.2% accuracy—beating homogeneous cosine cross-entropy by 4.2 percentage points (paired 95% CI [4.05, 4.35])—with 100% gain agreement and a finite-sample geometric predictor achieving cross-validated R² = 0.71 across 30 conditions.
sKnrd8SViL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear, carefully scoped theoretical analysis distinguishing scale-invariant decision cones, convexity, and class-support containment.
sKnrd8SViL.main_concern: Controlled experiments compare primarily against cosine cross-entropy rather than matched vMF-likelihood, angular-margin, or supervised-contrastive losses, and the practical motivation for gain invariance in standard classification is questioned.

DXGNmcuxJf.one_liner: Training-free three-stage mediation separating emotional assessment, response drafting, and safety review to reduce alarmist medical LLM responses.
DXGNmcuxJf.problem: Standard safety behavior in conversational LLMs frequently produces disproportionately alarmist or catastrophizing language on health-related and emotionally sensitive queries.
DXGNmcuxJf.method: Using paired two-turn scenarios across six languages rated by native speakers, clinicians, and validated lexical/semantic metrics, the authors separate clinically justified emergency referrals from unsupported catastrophizing. They introduce CALM (Context-Aware Layered Mediation), a training-free pipeline chaining emotional assessment, calm response drafting, and clinical safety review.
DXGNmcuxJf.key_idea: Mediate sensitive health responses through training-free emotional assessment, calm drafting, and safety-review stages to curb disproportionate threat framing while preserving justified emergency referrals.
DXGNmcuxJf.evidence: Evaluated across six languages and seven LLMs on paired two-turn health scenarios using native-speaker judgments, clinician urgency assessments, and automated lexical/semantic metrics.
DXGNmcuxJf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing warranted clinical urgency from unnecessary alarmism across six languages with human and clinician evaluations addresses an important real-world medical-LLM issue.
DXGNmcuxJf.main_concern: Reviewers note missing source-data filtering and human-study details alongside a mismatch between the main text's claimed clinical-urgency preservation checks and the reassurance-focused prompt templates in the appendix.

65JrbZxYCU.one_liner: Retimes teacher queries and decouples noise to make velocity bootstrapping unbiased in flow-based distributional critics.
65JrbZxYCU.problem: Same-time affine velocity bootstrapping cannot simultaneously preserve Gaussian initial noise and provide an unbiased residual-free Bellman target on straight paths.
65JrbZxYCU.method: ReBF queries the teacher critic at a dynamically shifted earlier flow time to align student and teacher trajectories. Fresh decoupled noise completes a conditionally unbiased target that preserves the Bellman fixed point.
65JrbZxYCU.key_idea: Shift the teacher’s flow clock to align intermediate trajectories and combine that retiming with fresh noise for unbiased velocity targets.
65JrbZxYCU.evidence: The paper proves conditional unbiasedness, Bellman fixed-point preservation, and Wasserstein contraction, with controlled analyses and offline, long-horizon, and risk-sensitive control evaluations.
65JrbZxYCU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the mechanism is analyzed carefully, the unbiasedness guarantee is useful, and controlled experiments connect retiming and noise choices to observable behavior.
65JrbZxYCU.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether retiming and noise decoupling constitute a substantial advance over PCBF and whether they explain the downstream control results.

kVgf2cVN5b.one_liner: Separates adversarial-intervention gating from input-specific answer-margin steering to recover pre-attack vision-language responses.
kVgf2cVN5b.problem: Adversarial image perturbations alter vision-language model answers, while activation-based detection directions alone do not reliably recover pre-attack behavior.
kVgf2cVN5b.method: AM-GARD uses a learned gate to decide whether to intervene and input-specific answer-margin updates to determine how to correct the answer. Controlled analyses compare attack-status, detector, recovery, and answer-margin directions under matched interventions.
kVgf2cVN5b.key_idea: Decouple intervention selection from correction by gating activation steering separately from input-specific movements across answer margins.
kVgf2cVN5b.evidence: Experiments span multiple large vision-language models, tasks, and answer formats, with analyses of recovery, pre-attack response preservation, intervention breadth, and answer boundaries.
kVgf2cVN5b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing attack detection from answer correction is insightful and that broad experiments show recovery gains while largely preserving pre-attack responses.
kVgf2cVN5b.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization across models, attacks, and multi-token generation, citing inconsistent recovery and reliance on calibration data and first-token margins.

dVwUGifGZ7.one_liner: Reranks and verifies weak-text segmentation candidates using confuser-aware local evidence and semantic-visual consistency checks.
dVwUGifGZ7.problem: Category-name prompts cannot reliably distinguish visually similar target and confuser objects when semantic similarity is treated as sufficient evidence.
dVwUGifGZ7.method: CPDG compares target and confuser categories to induce discriminative cues, aggregates local evidence within candidate regions, and reranks them. SCV combines semantic and visual evidence to verify or reject the top candidate.
dVwUGifGZ7.key_idea: Discover category-discriminative local evidence for candidate reranking, then reject hypotheses whose semantic and visual evidence is insufficient.
dVwUGifGZ7.evidence: Experiments on EndoVis17 and EndoVis18 evaluate weak-text fine-grained segmentation, target selection, confuser errors, and verification.
dVwUGifGZ7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that category-only surgical-video segmentation is practically relevant and that diagnostic selection and verification metrics help separate the two components’ roles.
dVwUGifGZ7.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the comparison protocol unclear or incomplete, citing potentially inconsistent weak-text settings and missing recent segmentation baselines.

PtrubdFt3x.one_liner: Calibrates synthetic-data complexity relative to the target learner and mixes difficulty levels for vision-language generalization.
PtrubdFt3x.problem: Synthetic-data design lacks principled control of training-example complexity and its effect on out-of-distribution generalization.
PtrubdFt3x.method: The authors isolate complexity using matched VQA post-training subsets, then introduce CoRAL Synthesis to compose synthetic data using learner-relative Easy, Medium, and Hard levels. The study also assesses whether existing complexity measures guide curation.
PtrubdFt3x.key_idea: Define example complexity against the target learner and explicitly control the Easy-Medium-Hard composition of synthetic training data.
PtrubdFt3x.evidence: Hundreds of controlled VQA post-training settings use matched distinct subsets to isolate complexity from data scale, quality, and diversity across multiple complexity levels.
PtrubdFt3x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learner-relative complexity is a valuable data-centric question and praise the controlled, extensive experiments and sample-efficient synthesis results.
PtrubdFt3x.main_concern: Reviewers most often state that the full-system comparisons do not isolate complexity calibration from filtering and diversification, leaving the main mechanism’s contribution unclear.

VK0dzej8BI.one_liner: Replaces static KL-loss anchoring with gated, trajectory-adaptive reference rewards at individual diffusion denoising steps.
VK0dzej8BI.problem: Static KL-as-loss regularization indirectly constrains harmful diffusion actions, resists reward optimization, and fixes the exploration-anchoring trade-off.
VK0dzej8BI.method: The method converts reference anchoring into step-level rewards derived from prediction discrepancies and adaptive trajectory gates. It is evaluated as a plug-in for GRPO-style diffusion reinforcement learning rather than as a static loss penalty.
VK0dzej8BI.key_idea: Turn reference-model disagreement into gated, step-dependent rewards that adapt anchoring strength within each diffusion trajectory.
VK0dzej8BI.evidence: Experiments compare reward- and loss-level anchoring on MixGRPO and FlowGRPO across multiple diffusion architectures, benchmarks, reward functions, and exploration-noise levels.
VK0dzej8BI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the experiments are extensive and consistently show improvements across architectures, rewards, and metrics, including a useful high-noise stress test.
VK0dzej8BI.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the central update insufficiently specified, especially how shaped rewards enter timestep advantages and how discrepancies and gates are normalized or detached.

lDnWMr44x3.one_liner: Models disease evolution in longitudinal chest X-rays as geodesic trajectories on a product-sphere manifold for LLM report generation.
lDnWMr44x3.problem: Longitudinal radiology report generators focus on static differences between exams rather than explicitly modeling how persistent diseases evolve.
lDnWMr44x3.method: EvoRG aligns prior and current exam features using shared disease prototypes and Sinkhorn optimal transport to reduce spatial misalignment. It parameterizes transitions as continuous geodesics on a visual-semantic product-sphere manifold, fusing midpoint and tangent descriptors via distance-modulated product-of-experts for an LLM.
lDnWMr44x3.key_idea: Aligns longitudinal disease prototypes via optimal transport and parameterizes interval transitions as product-sphere geodesics to condition LLM report generation.
lDnWMr44x3.evidence: Evaluated on Longitudinal-MIMIC with N-gram, CheXbert, Temporal F1, and Euclidean-versus-spherical ablations.
lDnWMr44x3.claimed_gains: On Longitudinal-MIMIC, EvoRG achieves relative improvements of 12.5% in CIDEr and 9.6% over the strongest baseline.
lDnWMr44x3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the focus on modeling disease evolution rather than static differences and the coherent optimal-transport and spherical-geodesic formulation.
lDnWMr44x3.main_concern: Reviewers note evaluation is limited to pairwise chest X-rays on one dataset without radiologist validation, and question whether time-agnostic geodesics reflect true disease dynamics.

jNvUbFifzw.one_liner: Attenuates new LoRA updates along directions captured in a rank-bounded history of merged past task residuals.
jNvUbFifzw.problem: Sequential LoRA fine-tuning suffers from catastrophic forgetting without storing replay data or growing an adapter bank.
jNvUbFifzw.method: RG-LoRA compresses each merged task's executed weight residual via QR/SVD into a fixed-rank history of dominant input and output directions and strengths. During subsequent tasks, this residual geometry softly attenuates new LoRA updates along strongly represented past directions while still allowing reuse.
jNvUbFifzw.key_idea: Maintains a rank-bounded QR/SVD summary of past merged weight residuals to softly attenuate new LoRA updates along previously used directions.
jNvUbFifzw.evidence: Three-seed experiments on continual classification and instruction-generation benchmarks using T5-Large, Llama-2-7B-Chat, and Llama-3.2-3B.
jNvUbFifzw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value computing geometry directly from executed residuals into a bounded state and reporting multi-seed results.
jNvUbFifzw.main_concern: Reviewers criticize comparing newly trained RG-LoRA runs (with custom gradient-aligned initialization and hyperparameters) against published baseline numbers rather than controlled implementations.

GlYtP0RJ3b.one_liner: Schedules full Diffusion Transformer steps adaptively using Newton-divided-difference error proxies for cached feature forecasting.
GlYtP0RJ3b.problem: Feature-forecasting methods accelerate Diffusion Transformers using fixed computation schedules, ignoring that forecast accuracy varies across denoising steps.
GlYtP0RJ3b.method: ARCS schedules full network evaluations dynamically whenever an online approximation-risk proxy exceeds a threshold. To support the resulting irregular anchor spacing, it formulates Taylor feature forecasting with Newton divided differences and derives lightweight non-uniform error proxies from cached history.
GlYtP0RJ3b.key_idea: Replaces fixed caching intervals with adaptive full-step scheduling triggered by Newton-divided-difference error proxies over irregularly spaced anchors.
GlYtP0RJ3b.evidence: Evaluated on image and video Diffusion Transformers (DiT, FLUX, Hunyuan) against fixed-interval Taylor forecasting with latency and FLOPs measurements.
GlYtP0RJ3b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note clear quality gains under aggressive acceleration budgets and appreciate the training-free online scheduling signal.
GlYtP0RJ3b.main_concern: Reviewers identify mathematical flaws in the derivative-error proxy, limited novelty over TaylorSeer, and higher latency or unclear FLOP-budget accounting versus baselines.

OMnzG9O0FE.one_liner: Traces timestamp pathways in video MLLMs and reuses intermediate visual states via learned cross-layer interventions.
OMnzG9O0FE.problem: How video MLLMs form start and end timestamps during generative temporal grounding is poorly understood, leaving intermediate visual cues underused.
OMnzG9O0FE.method: Boundary Flow Tracing uses route interventions and representation probing to locate visual-to-prompt and prompt-to-boundary pathways across depths. Motivated by recoverable cues in intermediate layers, Temporal Revisit (BTR and prediction-conditioned HTR) injects intermediate visual states back into later layers of a frozen backbone.
OMnzG9O0FE.key_idea: Probes layerwise timestamp formation and learns lightweight interventions that route intermediate visual representations back into later backbone layers.
OMnzG9O0FE.evidence: Probing and grounding experiments on TimeLens-SFT, Qwen3-VL, InternVL2.5, and MiMo-VL across QVHighlights, Charades, and ActivityNet.
OMnzG9O0FE.claimed_gains: On TimeLens-SFT, Broad Temporal Revisit improves mIoU by 3.92, 2.85, and 2.19 percentage points on QVHighlights-TimeLens, Charades-TimeLens, and ActivityNet-TimeLens.
OMnzG9O0FE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate investigating internal boundary formation in video MLLMs and translating probing findings into a concrete frozen-backbone intervention.
OMnzG9O0FE.main_concern: Reviewers note small gains on stronger post-GRPO models, limited explanatory power of the probes for BTR's variable gains, and confounded prompt-blocking interventions.

gxBz9KqoD7.one_liner: Calibrates monocular depth priors by estimating a continuous response-coordinate parameter from sparse metric observations.
gxBz9KqoD7.problem: Aligning monocular depth priors to sparse metric measurements with fixed affine coordinates (depth, log-depth, or disparity) leaves systematic calibration errors.
gxBz9KqoD7.method: Adaptive Response Geometry treats the response coordinate as an image-level unknown within a continuous family unifying depth, log-depth, and disparity. It estimates three global calibration parameters in metric space using a derived response-gradient relation, followed by hard-Dirichlet residual reconstruction.
gxBz9KqoD7.key_idea: Optimizes a continuous response-coordinate exponent alongside affine scale in metric space before applying hard-Dirichlet residual depth completion.
gxBz9KqoD7.evidence: Evaluated across multiple datasets and monocular priors under deliberately incomplete regular-grid observations against PriorDA, LDCM, and Any2Full.
gxBz9KqoD7.claimed_gains: Under deliberately incomplete metric observations, the pipeline achieves macro AbsRel 0.0301 and macro NMed 14.04 degrees, improving over PriorDA, LDCM, and Any2Full.
gxBz9KqoD7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the compact three-parameter continuous response formulation and clear separation between global calibration and local residual refinement.
gxBz9KqoD7.main_concern: Reviewers note methodological overlap with prior spline/two-stage calibration and OASIS-DC, missing noisy/irregular LiDAR/SfM patterns, and confounded metric-objective baselines.

dp41aKRpH2.one_liner: Identifies narrative lock-in in long-horizon agents and proposes an external evidence-tracking supervisor to revise task state.
dp41aKRpH2.problem: Long-horizon agents often anchor later plans and tool calls on an early wrong interpretation, resisting correction even as counterevidence arrives.
dp41aKRpH2.method: The authors analyze 6,035 agent trajectories with a five-dimension rubric to characterize Narrative Lock-in (N-lock) and test six correction strategies on 728 matched cases. They also propose Nexus, a lightweight external overseer that tracks preserved evidence to flag conflicts and guide task-state revision.
dp41aKRpH2.key_idea: Formalizes trajectory-level Narrative Lock-in via a five-dimension rubric and deploys an external evidence-preserving supervisor (Nexus) to force task-state revision.
dp41aKRpH2.evidence: Analyzes 6,035 trajectories across four benchmarks and five models, plus intervention studies on 728 matched cases.
dp41aKRpH2.claimed_gains: Across 6,035 trajectories, N-lock trajectories score lower in 34 of 42 matched groups (mean completion 0.207 vs. 0.623 for non-N-lock), and across six correction strategies on 728 cases strict recovery ranges from 10.7% to 36.4%.
dp41aKRpH2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the five-dimension characterization of persistent erroneous interpretations across benchmarks systematic and informative.
dp41aKRpH2.main_concern: Reviewers note that Nexus alleviation experiments are rushed without baselines or cost analysis, and that recovery evaluation mixes official benchmark scores with unvalidated LLM judgments.

9eYGpwzIHM.one_liner: Learns latent continuous-time Markov chains without trajectory simulation by matching amortized time marginals via dual rate tilting.
9eYGpwzIHM.problem: Learning latent continuous-time Markov chains from noisy observations in large state spaces requires expensive trajectory simulation during inference.
9eYGpwzIHM.method: CTMC Matching directly parameterizes the variational posterior's time marginals with an amortized neural network and recovers the KL-optimal transition rates as an exponential tilt of prior rates by solving a concave dual problem. For structured systems like interacting particle systems, it decomposes optimization into local neighborhood problems without enumerating the joint state space.
9eYGpwzIHM.key_idea: Parameterizes posterior time marginals directly and recovers KL-optimal transition rates via an exponential tilt solving a concave dual problem without trajectory simulation.
9eYGpwzIHM.evidence: Backed by an exactness theorem at true smoothing marginals and experiments on chemical reaction networks and 64x64 and 128x128 wildfire grids.
9eYGpwzIHM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CTMC Matching is a mathematically rigorous, principled simulation-free variational inference framework for CTMCs.
9eYGpwzIHM.main_concern: Reviewers point out the missing end-to-end runtime and memory comparisons against simulation-based or exact baselines, mixed empirical results, and lack of quantitative posterior error bounds.

78ICEmdojg.one_liner: Runs a factorial study of identifier naming, surface vs. core syntax, and explicit relations in Lean proof states.
78ICEmdojg.problem: Machine theorem proving research focuses on models and search while leaving how proof-state surface representations affect learnability underexplored.
78ICEmdojg.method: The ICR framework defines proof-state representations along three binary axes—identifiers (I), core vs. conventional syntax (C), and explicit relations (R)—and trains small encoder-decoder models from scratch across all eight combinations.
78ICEmdojg.key_idea: Decomposes Lean proof-state representations into identifier preservation, surface versus core syntax, and explicit relation links in a controlled eight-cell factorial design.
78ICEmdojg.evidence: Factorial experiments training small and medium encoder-decoder models from scratch on Mathlib and miniF2F with kernel-verified proof search.
78ICEmdojg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled eight-cell factorial design with fixed data, tokenizer, initialization, optimization, and mechanically verified proof evaluation.
78ICEmdojg.main_concern: Reviewers note that switching between surface and core syntax simultaneously alters sequence length, types, qualified names, and output alignment, so the causal factor behind the gap is not isolated.

EViO2ILjzr.one_liner: Wraps a video world model in an agentic harness whose tools, skills, and code co-evolve via execution feedback.
EViO2ILjzr.problem: Existing multimodal reasoners invoke video world models through fixed pipelines for a single imagination type rather than adapting visual imagination to diverse tasks.
EViO2ILjzr.method: CoWorld Reasoner exposes multiple video world model operations as tools guided by skills for a frozen VLM, and uses VLM-VWM Harness Co-Evolution to revise tools, skills, and execution code from feedback.
EViO2ILjzr.key_idea: Pairs a multi-operation video world model tool harness with iterative co-evolution of tools, skills, and execution code using execution feedback.
EViO2ILjzr.evidence: Evaluations across seven spatial, temporal, causal, and perceptual reasoning benchmarks including held-out transfer sets SAT, SpatiaLab, and ERQA.
EViO2ILjzr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the flexible selective use of visual imagination operations across tasks and the evaluation on held-out benchmarks.
EViO2ILjzr.main_concern: Reviewers point out that baselines lack VWM access, making it unclear how much gain comes from co-evolution versus the multi-stage workflow or video tool, and note small gains on several benchmarks.

uKJIH6ib4w.one_liner: Analyzes pairwise LLM judge panel balance and proposes paired unanimity stopping to preserve reference decisions with fewer calls.
uKJIH6ib4w.problem: Adaptive early-stopping rules for repeated pairwise LLM judging can preserve expected scores while flipping many individual verdict decisions.
uKJIH6ib4w.method: The authors analyze random versus exact order-balanced 4-call panels and propose Paired Unanimity Stopping, which stops early only when order-balanced judgment pairs agree.
uKJIH6ib4w.key_idea: Stop repeated pairwise LLM judging early only after an order-balanced pair of calls reaches unanimity, avoiding tie-breaking flips.
uKJIH6ib4w.evidence: Theoretical propositions for 4-call panels and experiments across multiple LLM judges and benchmarks (e.g., JudgeBench) evaluate call counts and reference agreement.
uKJIH6ib4w.claimed_gains: With four seeds, random display orders capture 75% of the expected score gain of exact balance, while Paired Unanimity Stopping reduces reference decision changes by 0.98 to 18.97 percentage points across 17 configurations.
uKJIH6ib4w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical distinction between preserving expected benchmark scores and preserving individual verdicts.
uKJIH6ib4w.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty since the 4-call stopping rule is equivalent to existing ESC and Adaptive-Consistency variants, and uses more calls than non-strict stopping.

v4bOJQnRfX.one_liner: Diagnoses transcript bias in omni models and fine-tunes them on same-transcript vocal-expression counterfactual pairs.
v4bOJQnRfX.problem: Multimodal omni models often ignore how utterances are spoken and rely solely on transcripts, even when vocal expression flips the correct translation.
v4bOJQnRfX.method: The authors evaluate controlled translation selection with silence controls and introduce Paralinguistic Counterfactual Training (PCT), applying LoRA SFT on balanced same-transcript audio pairs with opposite labels and quality preferences.
v4bOJQnRfX.key_idea: Fine-tune omni models with LoRA on balanced same-transcript audio pairs whose opposite labels depend on vocal expression, combined with candidate-order augmentation.
v4bOJQnRfX.evidence: Evaluations test Qwen2.5-Omni-3B/7B, four other omni models, silence controls, and transfer to general audio benchmarks.
v4bOJQnRfX.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and 7B, PCT increases paired correctness from 2.65% to 49.29% and from 8.17% to 50.71%, respectively.
v4bOJQnRfX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled diagnostic showing omni models ignore prosody and the evaluation of cross-modal preservation.
v4bOJQnRfX.main_concern: Reviewers point out that PCT is standard LoRA SFT on ContraProST's own training split without a matched-budget non-counterfactual baseline, and OOD gains are small.

yVQfaLCCp2.one_liner: Applies query-conditioned 2D convolutions over a span lattice before structured posterior decoding and prototype-based potential refinement for video moment retrieval.
yVQfaLCCp2.problem: Transferring boundary-based structured posterior decoding to multi-moment video retrieval degrades because visual evidence is distributed across span interiors with indistinct boundaries.
yVQfaLCCp2.method: The authors apply query-conditioned local 2D convolutions on a 2D span lattice to aggregate neighboring and interior semantics, compute exact segment marginals via structured posterior decoding, and iteratively refine potentials using a posterior-weighted moment prototype.
yVQfaLCCp2.key_idea: Contextualizes a 2D span lattice with query-conditioned convolutions and iteratively refines exact segment posterior potentials via a posterior-weighted prototype.
yVQfaLCCp2.evidence: Evaluations on QV-M2, QVHighlights, and Charades-STA across CLIP+SlowFast and InternVideo2-6B features.
yVQfaLCCp2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling both local span-lattice context and global structured competition is well-motivated for multi-moment video retrieval.
yVQfaLCCp2.main_concern: Three-seed average G-mAP on QV-M2 slightly trails FlashMMR despite higher best-seed scores, and key controls, hyperparameter selection splits, and efficiency metrics are underspecified.

7MjYspnB9H.one_liner: Models and measures endogenous fault contagion in multi-agent LLM debates and contains it with a message provenance gate.
7MjYspnB9H.problem: Classical Byzantine fault tolerance assumes a fixed set of faulty agents, whereas LLM agents can become faulty simply by reading peer protocol messages.
7MjYspnB9H.method: The paper defines per-hop infection rate, payload replication rate, and inter-replica correlation, deriving majority-tolerance thresholds under endogenous contagion. To contain instruction-channel hijacks such as forged coordinator notices, it introduces a provenance gate that filters peer messages.
7MjYspnB9H.key_idea: Quantifies per-hop infection, payload replication, and replica correlation in multi-agent LLM protocols and blocks forged-authority contagion with a provenance gate.
7MjYspnB9H.evidence: Measured across 11 models from seven families on 1,300 questions and tested in 5-, 9-, and 15-agent debates, plus provenance-gate evaluations.
7MjYspnB9H.claimed_gains: A forged coordinator notice flips 97% of agents (up to 100% in TL;DR), cross-round contagion requires beta > 0.16 for five agents, and the provenance gate restores debate accuracy to 72-87% (from review).
7MjYspnB9H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly frames endogenous fault contagion and separates instruction-channel from evidence-channel attacks and answer flip from payload replication.
7MjYspnB9H.main_concern: Reviewers note thin theoretical novelty, missing trust-boundary prompt baselines in main debates, and limited evidence against adaptive gate-bypass attacks.

BYNMjQh8Y8.one_liner: Proves a post-hoc conditional safety bound on vulnerability increase for uncorrelated multiplayer subgame resolving.
BYNMjQh8Y8.problem: Unlike two-player zero-sum games, multiplayer subgame resolving with three or more independent players lacks theoretical guarantees against increasing exploitability.
BYNMjQh8Y8.method: The authors derive a post-hoc conditional safety theorem bounding the resolved profile's best-response gap increase over the blueprint by four terms: subgame activation, resolver solve error, opponents' subgame margin deficits, and a structural distance to constant-sum polymatrix games.
