BYNMjQh8Y8.key_idea: Bounds the multiplayer best-response gap increase after subgame resolving via activation, solve error, opponent margin deficits, and structural tax.
BYNMjQh8Y8.evidence: Formal mathematical proofs, tight worst-case constructions, and evaluations on 162 three-player Leduc poker instances.
BYNMjQh8Y8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical gap in multiplayer subgame resolving is real and the proofs and four-term decomposition are mathematically sound.
BYNMjQh8Y8.main_concern: Reviewers note the guarantee is only conditional and post-hoc, the empirical evaluation is limited to small Leduc instances without showing practical exploitability reduction, and writing clarity suffers.

An2xeekp6B.one_liner: Audits LLM zero-sum matrix-game solving with exploitability certificates, showing chat templates erase most named-game advantages and small-game training transfers.
An2xeekp6B.problem: Whether LLMs solve zero-sum matrix games from payoff structure or prompt memorization, and whether small-game training transfers to larger games.
An2xeekp6B.method: The paper scores tool-free LLM strategy pairs using an exploitability certificate without equilibrium labels, audits raw versus chat-template prompting on named games, trains on 2x2-3x3 games via SFT and residual-reward GRPO, and calibrates dominated-action padding controls.
An2xeekp6B.key_idea: Uses label-free exploitability certificates and matched chat-template controls to separate prompt artifacts from size-transferable zero-sum equilibrium solving.
An2xeekp6B.evidence: Tested Qwen3.5-9B (and Qwen3-8B in interface checks) on 10 named base games (12,600 observations), unseen 5x5 games, and padded 12x12 controls.
An2xeekp6B.claimed_gains: Correct-label advantage drops from 24.6 points (raw) to 1.6 points (chat template); on 5x5 games, best-of-four success reaches 61% (SFT, 33% pass@1) and 37% (GRPO) vs. 16% base.
An2xeekp6B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the transparent experimental protocol, released records, and label-free exploitability scoring.
An2xeekp6B.main_concern: Experiments are restricted to two small Qwen models on a narrow tractable task, and the GRPO recipe bundles multiple changes without isolating what drives its gains.

A56MFewqEP.one_liner: Passing linked-verse meaning through generated images increases semantic pivots and lexical density but does not establish better creativity.
A56MFewqEP.problem: LLMs show mixed divergent creativity in poetry, and the effect of visually recoding intermediate meaning remains unclear.
A56MFewqEP.method: Gemini and Qwen models extend and pivot seed verses in a linked-verse task. A text condition carries prior verse text directly, while a visual condition replaces that link with generated images.
A56MFewqEP.key_idea: Visual recoding forces each new verse to recover meaning from an image rather than directly reading the preceding verse text.
A56MFewqEP.evidence: The factorial study compares two LLM families using lexical, embedding, dictionary, LLM-judge, and translated human-corpus measures.
A56MFewqEP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the linked-verse design is interesting and that the multi-level lexical, semantic, and qualitative analyses are useful.
A56MFewqEP.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that divergence proxies do not establish creativity and that asymmetric models and instructions confound the modality comparison.

nUp4bKbt7K.one_liner: Dynamical mean-field equations track policy-dependent attention learning across supervised-to-GRPO staging and matched-budget interleaving.
nUp4bKbt7K.problem: The training-dynamics consequences of ordering supervised learning and verifier-guided reinforcement learning remain poorly understood under repeated finite-corpus use.
nUp4bKbt7K.method: The paper studies a solvable attention model in which MSE trains keys and values while GRPO updates keys from binary verifier rewards. DMFT reduces high-dimensional training to a self-consistent channel with policy-dependent action histories and derives noise sensitivities.
nUp4bKbt7K.key_idea: A history-score term propagates earlier parameter changes through later sampled GRPO actions, capturing on-policy feedback in finite-corpus training dynamics.
nUp4bKbt7K.evidence: Theory and synthetic experiments compare MSE-to-GRPO staging with exact-count random interleaving under matched supervision and verifier budgets and predict local crossover locations.
nUp4bKbt7K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that policy-dependent action histories and controlled training-order comparisons give the tractable model technical value.
nUp4bKbt7K.main_concern: Reviewers most often warn that unequal tasks, frozen values during GRPO, and the simplified attention model confound ordering effects and limit practical relevance.

93khAI4hyF.one_liner: TwinCheck filters harmful self-evolving agent memory updates by replaying readout-matched twin alternatives and comparing outcomes in both orders.
93khAI4hyF.problem: Self-evolving agent admission verifiers can approve harmful memories or skills that look identical to safe updates on all verifier readout signals.
93khAI4hyF.method: TwinCheck constructs an alternative update matching every signal seen by the native verifier without safety labels, replays both candidate and twin from the same state, and compares their behaviors in both presentation orders to decide admission.
93khAI4hyF.key_idea: Generates a native-readout-equivalent alternative update, replays both from the same state, and averages order-swapped comparative safety judgments before admitting memory updates.
93khAI4hyF.evidence: Evaluated on paired-update sets from AI Safety Gridworlds and tau^2-Bench across eight open-weight and proprietary verifiers and a ten-generation self-update loop.
93khAI4hyF.claimed_gains: Raises mean harmful-update detection AUC from 0.748 to 0.945 on controlled traces and from 0.695 to 0.835 on tool-use conversations, reducing degraded trajectories in a ten-generation loop from 30.39% to 0.43%.
93khAI4hyF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying verifier readout blind spots in self-evolving agents is important and that the research questions and multi-verifier experiments are well-structured.
93khAI4hyF.main_concern: Key tool-use detection tests pair candidates with a contract-safe reference rather than fully automatic alternatives, and the necessity of specific design choices over simpler safety filters is under-justified.

9UxdyJ69ph.one_liner: MAIGPO bridges the centralized-guider to decentralized-learner gap in MARL via information-bottleneck extraction and bidirectional mutual-information alignment.
9UxdyJ69ph.problem: Guided policy optimization in MARL (MAGPO) aligns only actions and fails to align decision-relevant information between centralized guiders and partially observable decentralized learners.
9UxdyJ69ph.method: Multi-Agent Information-Guided Policy Optimization (MAIGPO) uses a variational information bottleneck (VIB) to extract decision-relevant representations and InfoNCE mutual-information maximization for bidirectional alignment between guider and learner.
9UxdyJ69ph.key_idea: Combines variational information bottleneck compression with bidirectional InfoNCE mutual-information alignment between centralized guider and decentralized learner representations.
9UxdyJ69ph.evidence: Information-theoretic derivation plus experiments across 23 tasks on standard MARL benchmark suites (including MPE/SMAX) and component ablations.
9UxdyJ69ph.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the clear motivation for extending MAGPO with representation alignment and appreciate the broad 23-task empirical evaluation.
9UxdyJ69ph.main_concern: Novelty over MAGPO is incremental (combining standard VIB and InfoNCE), theoretical assumptions about capturing exact decision-relevant information are unverified, and per-task seed counts are unclear.

olMpdPRF1F.one_liner: SRCL reduces streaming LLM continual-learning interference by gating working-memory updates on gradient cosine consistency and projecting orthogonally into long-term memory.
olMpdPRF1F.problem: Continuous parameter updates in streaming LLMs cause representational smearing and interference across sequential formal reasoning domains.
olMpdPRF1F.method: Self-Referential Continual Learning (SRCL) maintains a transient working-memory adapter, estimates EMA cosine similarity between successive updates, and—only when exceeding a discrete threshold—projects the update into long-term memory via orthogonal rank expansion while decaying rejected updates.
olMpdPRF1F.key_idea: Gates consolidation from a transient working-memory adapter using EMA update cosine consistency and stores accepted updates via orthogonal rank expansion in long-term memory.
olMpdPRF1F.evidence: PCA parameter-trajectory analysis over 50 sequential steps and evaluations on sequential math (Lean theorem proving) and code-generation streams across multiple model scales.
olMpdPRF1F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean separation of when to consolidate (consistency gate) and where to store (orthogonal projection), backed by mechanistic ablations.
olMpdPRF1F.main_concern: Baselines use smaller fixed adapter capacity than SRCL's growing long-term memory, and working-memory state handling at evaluation time is described inconsistently.

D8P8uZcOvU.one_liner: Unifies heterogeneous temporal graph regimes in one architecture combining observed topology with temporal correlation-based message passing for zero-shot transfer.
D8P8uZcOvU.problem: Temporal graph models are typically dataset-specific because spatiotemporal graphs, interaction networks, and fully dynamic graphs have incompatible observation formats.
D8P8uZcOvU.method: The authors propose a unified temporal graph architecture (TRACE) that maps diverse temporal graph regimes into a shared representation space and combines observed topology with a temporal correlation-based message-passing operator (via associative Gram multiplication) for zero-shot transfer.
D8P8uZcOvU.key_idea: Maps static-topology, interaction, and fully dynamic graphs into a shared space and combines observed-graph and temporal-correlation message passing.
D8P8uZcOvU.evidence: Pre-training and zero-shot transfer experiments across three temporal graph domains against inductive graph baselines and time-series foundation models.
D8P8uZcOvU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clean unified interface for heterogeneous temporal graphs and the promising within-domain zero-shot transfer results with compact models.
D8P8uZcOvU.main_concern: Models are trained separately per domain (not one cross-domain foundation model as claimed), ablations do not retrain from scratch, and graph-aware traffic-transfer baselines are omitted.

jAdZT9Oi6d.one_liner: Formulates AdamW as a finite-horizon input–state–output system and linearizes parameter-moment dynamics to model delayed minibatch loss effects.
jAdZT9Oi6d.problem: Minibatch gradients affect future training losses beyond the immediate step because AdamW persists gradient information in its first- and second-moment states.
jAdZT9Oi6d.method: The authors model AdamW as a finite-horizon input–state–output (ISO) system over parameters and both optimizer moments, linearize the joint dynamics into a signed response operator, and derive an exact multistep error decomposition with first-order accuracy bounds.
jAdZT9Oi6d.key_idea: Linearizes AdamW's joint parameter and first/second-moment state dynamics into a finite-horizon signed response operator predicting delayed minibatch loss effects.
jAdZT9Oi6d.evidence: Theoretical multistep error bounds plus paired-trajectory perturbation experiments on quadratic models (H=32), CIFAR-10 CNNs/MLPs (H=12), and Pythia language models (H=8).
jAdZT9Oi6d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the paired-trajectory experimental design isolating delayed optimizer-moment effects and documenting linear-approximation horizons across model classes.
jAdZT9Oi6d.main_concern: Mathematical novelty beyond prior joint parameter-moment AdamW sensitivity derivations (Deng et al., 2026) is unclear, and language-model experiments show limited advantage over one-step baselines.

mqqVH2X8m2.one_liner: Encodes disentangled continuous hand and object latents and predicts them with a masked autoregressive transformer conditioning a flow-matching head.
mqqVH2X8m2.problem: Text-to-hand-object-interaction diffusion models typically generate fixed-length atomic motions, while discrete autoregressive approaches lose contact-sensitive motion detail.
mqqVH2X8m2.method: MAD-HOI encodes articulated object, left-hand, and right-hand motions into separate continuous latent streams to preserve stream-wise control. A masked autoregressive transformer predicts context features that condition a flow-matching head, enabling atomic and composite generation, completion, infilling, and End-of-Motion prediction under one training objective.
mqqVH2X8m2.key_idea: Combines disentangled continuous hand-object latent streams with a masked autoregressive transformer and flow-matching head to support variable-length generation, infilling, and termination.
mqqVH2X8m2.evidence: Evaluated on text-to-HOI generation, composite sequences, completion, infilling, handedness control, and unseen object/action splits.
mqqVH2X8m2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying variable-length generation, completion, infilling, composite motions, and termination in a disentangled continuous HOI framework is practically useful.
mqqVH2X8m2.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over prior continuous masked autoregressive diffusion and disentangled HOI models (e.g., MARDM, HOIGPT, HO-Flow) and weak generalization to unseen objects and actions.

kmkzrpMSPv.one_liner: Scores SFT tokens online by aligning forward-pass last-hidden-state gradients with held-out task directions plus cached excess loss.
kmkzrpMSPv.problem: Loss-based token selectors for LLM SFT ignore downstream task alignment, while full gradient-based token influence estimation is too expensive to run online.
kmkzrpMSPv.method: The authors introduce GRAIN, which approximates token-level gradient influence using closed-form last-hidden-state gradients computed directly from the forward pass. Each token is scored by gated alignment with task gradient directions estimated from a small held-out set combined with an excess-loss term from cached base-model losses, avoiding extra backward passes or a live reference model.
kmkzrpMSPv.key_idea: Approximate task-aware token influence online by aligning forward-pass last-hidden-state gradients with held-out task directions and combining with cached base-model excess loss.
kmkzrpMSPv.evidence: Conditional first-order influence theory (Proposition 1) and SFT experiments on LLaMA-3.2-3B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B with component ablations and runtime measurements.
kmkzrpMSPv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the closed-form forward-pass last-layer gradient approximation practical and clean, and appreciate testing across three LLM backbones with runtime reporting.
kmkzrpMSPv.main_concern: Reviewers cite modest single-seed average gains (0.41-1.24 points) alongside a 29% end-to-end runtime increase over full-token SFT, unablated 15% full-token warmup, and held-out directions drawn from evaluated benchmark families.

NAAO0nVmiC.one_liner: Characterizes LLM instruction-following difficulty via boundary slack, solution concentration, and conditional perplexity beyond constraint counts.
NAAO0nVmiC.problem: Evaluating instruction following by constraint count obscures wide variation in the difficulty of individual constraints and their multi-constraint interactions.
NAAO0nVmiC.method: The authors formulate instruction following as model-conditioned constraint satisfaction and measure individual and pairwise constraint difficulty via three properties: boundary slack, concentration among sampled successful outputs, and conditional perplexity. They evaluate correlation with compliance on disjoint streams, test prompt interventions targeting these properties, and examine infeasible and fuzzified extensions.
NAAO0nVmiC.key_idea: Quantify instruction-constraint difficulty using model-conditioned boundary slack, successful-solution concentration, and conditional perplexity rather than raw constraint counts.
NAAO0nVmiC.evidence: Disjoint-stream correlation analyses, leave-one-model-out transfer, pairwise interaction studies, and controlled prompt interventions across three LLMs up to 26B parameters.
NAAO0nVmiC.claimed_gains: All three difficulty properties correlate with compliance at mean |rho| approx 0.55; prompt interventions raise compliance by ~6.5 percentage points; coupling reduces constituent compliance by up to 15 points; fixed-count follow rates differ by >50 points across difficulty strata; infeasibility recognition and fuzzified properties rise by ~70.7% across difficulty settings.
NAAO0nVmiC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate moving beyond constraint counts, the disjoint-stream methodology avoiding shared-sample bias, and the sharp compliance variation observed at fixed constraint counts.
NAAO0nVmiC.main_concern: Reviewers point out that boundary slack restricts the framework to countable numeric constraints (excluding tone or persona), experiments cover only pairwise constraints and models <=26B, and the metrics lack theoretical justification.

QzAdsHLXcH.one_liner: Analyzes off-policy versus on-policy multi-teacher distillation via forward-KL arithmetic mixtures and reverse-KL geometric aggregates.
QzAdsHLXcH.problem: Why on-policy distillation reduces forgetting relative to SFT yet exhibits fragility in autoregressive settings is theoretically poorly understood.
QzAdsHLXcH.method: The authors formalize sequential multi-teacher distillation under forward KL (yielding a weighted arithmetic mixture) and reverse KL (yielding a normalized weighted geometric aggregate). They design tabular and function-approximation algorithms with logarithmic regret bounds and analyze token-level conditionals under uninformative teachers, misleading teachers, and long horizons.
QzAdsHLXcH.key_idea: Contrast forward-KL arithmetic mixtures and reverse-KL geometric aggregates in autoregressive multi-teacher distillation to explain expert retention, sensitivity to low-probability errors, and long-horizon prefix bias.
QzAdsHLXcH.evidence: Theoretical regret bounds for tabular and function-approximation settings plus closed-form analytical constructions illustrating uninformative teachers, misleading teachers, and long-horizon continuation effects.
QzAdsHLXcH.claimed_gains: Establishes logarithmic regret bounds in the tabular setting for learning the forward-KL and reverse-KL multi-teacher aggregation targets.
QzAdsHLXcH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting SFT and OPD through forward versus reverse KL multi-teacher aggregation provides clear theoretical insight into both knowledge retention and failure modes.
QzAdsHLXcH.main_concern: Reviewers note the complete absence of actual student training experiments (all figures evaluate closed-form expressions) and an unverified gap between sequence-level reverse-KL optima and practical token-level gradient-based OPD.

9WRBIFPtv4.one_liner: Measures semantic false-positive concentration under equal-error-budget audits to show label coarsening relocates segmentation errors.
9WRBIFPtv4.problem: Overlap metrics like Dice and IoU hide which non-target structures receive false positives, masking how collapsing background subclasses changes error composition even at fixed Dice.
9WRBIFPtv4.method: The authors define semantic error relocation (SER) and Semantic False-Positive Concentration (SFPC), the fraction of target false positives landing on a specified hidden negative subclass. They introduce a validation-matched false-positive protocol and an exact equal-error-budget audit to compare coarse- and fine-labeled segmentation models at identical total error counts.
9WRBIFPtv4.key_idea: Audit coarse- versus fine-labeled segmentation models at matched total false-positive budgets using Semantic False-Positive Concentration to isolate pure error relocation onto hidden negative subclasses.
9WRBIFPtv4.evidence: Matched-FP and exact-budget empirical audits on medical image segmentation (MS3SEG) and natural-image segmentation (Cityscapes).
9WRBIFPtv4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical question is important, the matched-error protocol cleanly controls total FP confounds, and replication across MS3SEG and Cityscapes is well designed.
9WRBIFPtv4.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over prior background-subdivision work (e.g., BackSplit) and class-conditional FP analysis, unclear deployability since exact audits need ground-truth negative labels, and confounding between label granularity and loss functions.

KWZ64ghoKP.one_liner: Certifies appearance-induced surface bias in Gaussian splatting and decouples geometry ranking from appearance penalties via Score Separation.
KWZ64ghoKP.problem: Jointly optimizing geometry and finite-capacity appearance in Gaussian splatting causes the image-fitting objective to strictly prefer physically worse 3D surfaces.
KWZ64ghoKP.method: The authors prove and certify appearance-induced surface bias via primal and dual certificates, identifying a capacity route (unabsorbed appearance residual) and a penalty route (appearance regularization in geometry ranking). They propose Score Separation, which retains regularized appearance fitting while ranking geometry updates using a penalty-free or complexity-corrected score (DATA or GCV).
KWZ64ghoKP.key_idea: Rank candidate geometry updates in Gaussian splatting using a score that excludes the appearance regularization penalty while selecting the penalty weight from training images.
KWZ64ghoKP.evidence: Primal/dual certification across 23 reconstructed scenes (including 15 DTU scans, Tanks and Temples, Replica, 2DGS, PGSR, and GStex) plus controlled unseen-material experiments.
KWZ64ghoKP.claimed_gains: Freeing geometry under SH0 2DGS raises test PSNR by 2.2 dB while worsening surfaces on all 15 DTU scans; certificates detect bias in 19 of 23 scenes; the complexity-corrected score cuts error in half vs. joint fitting and lowers unseen-material error by 13.7% under fair tuning.
KWZ64ghoKP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing why higher image PSNR can accompany worse 3D geometry in Gaussian splatting is an important, well-analyzed problem.
KWZ64ghoKP.main_concern: Reviewers note inconsistent geometry gains from Score Separation across real scenes (GCV worsens error on all 7 tested DTU scenes), narrow SH0/160px main settings, and no guidance on choosing among PROFILE, DATA, and GCV without a 3D reference.

kQVC2vQvcx.one_liner: Applies statistical power analysis via minimum detectable difference to audit ranking resolution and reversal rates across 202 leaderboards.
kQVC2vQvcx.problem: Machine learning leaderboards present fine-grained linear rankings without uncertainty intervals, obscuring which reported performance gaps exceed benchmark resolution.
kQVC2vQvcx.method: The authors compute the minimum detectable difference (MDD)—the smallest true accuracy gap detectable at 80% power—to partition 202 leaderboards across eight families into greedy resolvable tiers. They test whether MDD-labeled unresolvable versus resolvable orderings predict rank reversals on held-out MMLU subjects and random item splits across seven additional boards.
kQVC2vQvcx.key_idea: Use minimum detectable difference from statistical power analysis to partition leaderboards into resolvable tiers and predict out-of-sample rank reversals.
kQVC2vQvcx.evidence: Empirical audit of 202 leaderboards across eight families, held-out rescoring on 52 MMLU subjects, and random-split replication across seven additional boards including coding and software engineering.
kQVC2vQvcx.claimed_gains: The median HELM board separates into 5 greedy tiers (8 for non-slice boards, 14 for families), and unresolvable orderings reverse in 21.5% of held-out MMLU cases versus 0.27% for resolvable orderings.
kQVC2vQvcx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large-scale empirical audit of leaderboard resolution and the held-out item validation demonstrating high reversal rates below the resolution threshold.
kQVC2vQvcx.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty over Card et al. (2020), note that MDD does not outperform a simpler sqrt(n)-scaled gap rule or paired bootstrap, and criticize dense, poorly organized presentation packed with unmotivated propositions.

fb7pJANxOj.one_liner: Benchmarks AI agents on selecting and pre-ranking LLM post-training data subsets before standardized fine-tuning evaluation.
fb7pJANxOj.problem: Whether frontier AI agents can reliably identify high-value training data and forecast post-training performance without running training or seeing evaluation tasks is untested.
fb7pJANxOj.method: The authors introduce DataSense-Bench, where agents inspect candidate trajectory pools (OpenThoughts-Agent and EnvScaler), run analysis code and forward passes, and output five ranked training subsets without training access. A small base LLM is then fine-tuned on each subset under a fixed protocol and evaluated on TBLite and BFCL for top-subset performance and ranking accuracy.
fb7pJANxOj.key_idea: Freeze agent-selected training subsets and their predicted performance rankings before running standardized fine-tuning to jointly test data selection and performance forecasting.
fb7pJANxOj.evidence: Three-run evaluations of multiple frontier AI agents on terminal problem solving (OpenThoughts-Agent to TBLite) and tool use (EnvScaler to BFCL).
fb7pJANxOj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clean separation between pre-training data selection/forecasting and standardized post-training evaluation, along with transparent per-group cost and recipe reporting.
fb7pJANxOj.main_concern: Reviewers point out that letting each agent construct its own ranked groups confounds forecasting accuracy with group construction, random baselines and fine-tuning use single seeds despite small gains (0.35-1.78 points), and the protocol closely mirrors DataComp/DataPerf.

LmZ3iOzC80.one_liner: Indexes archived recurrent key-value states using compact key-derived summaries and reads them via joint online-historical attention.
LmZ3iOzC80.problem: Recurrent state space models overwrite earlier context as states update, and even multi-state architectures struggle to address and retrieve specific historical information efficiently.
LmZ3iOzC80.method: The authors introduce Tayra, a recurrent memory architecture combining sparsely updated online memory with archived key-value state snapshots. Compact centroid-and-entropy indices derived directly from stored keys address relevant archived snapshots while preserving full internal keys and values for query-dependent reading through a joint online-and-historical attention interface.
LmZ3iOzC80.key_idea: Derive compact state-level addressing indices directly from archived recurrent keys so queries select historical snapshots without replacing their internal key-value contents during joint attention readout.
LmZ3iOzC80.evidence: 50B-token pretraining experiments comparing Tayra against Raven and a Raven-based MARCH adaptation across six needle-in-a-haystack tasks (4K-16K and 2x length), LongBench, and general language benchmarks.
LmZ3iOzC80.claimed_gains: Achieves a 43.4% relative improvement over Raven in mean accuracy on six 4K-16K needle-in-a-haystack tasks and improves average LongBench score by approximately 23% over a Raven-based MARCH adaptation.
LmZ3iOzC80.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate reusing stored recurrent keys for hierarchical addressing and note meaningful matched-budget gains over the Raven-based MARCH baseline on LongBench and complex NIAH.
LmZ3iOzC80.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited conceptual novelty beyond combining Raven, MARCH, and HiLS, missing latency/throughput/memory benchmarks, and ablations that confound historical indexing with readout fusion.

gzctl4DNJo.one_liner: Refines frozen MLLM visual states via progressive contextual cue replay using retrieval differences from a shared visual memory.
gzctl4DNJo.problem: Causal attention in image-first autoregressive MLLMs prevents visual tokens from receiving top-down feedback from subsequent task instructions, hurting training-free whole-image emotion recognition.
gzctl4DNJo.method: The authors propose Contextual Cue Replay (CCR), which at selected decoder depths evaluates an auxiliary block to produce contextualized visual states attending to the full image and a generic instruction. Both base and contextualized states query a shared memory of current visual representations, and their retrieval difference is written back as an incremental update to refine visual states without parameter updates.
gzctl4DNJo.key_idea: Query a shared visual-state memory with both base and instruction-contextualized states at intermediate decoder depths and write back their retrieval difference to refine frozen MLLM visual tokens.
gzctl4DNJo.evidence: Training-free emotion recognition experiments across three MLLM backbones (including LLaVA, VILA, and Qwen2.5-VL) and 15 backbone-setting pairs with component ablations against zero-shot and SEPM.
gzctl4DNJo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mechanism is clearly motivated, parameter-free, easy to transfer across emotion label sets, and yields consistent gains over zero-shot and SEPM across tested backbones.
gzctl4DNJo.main_concern: Reviewers highlight missing validation-split and hyperparameter-selection protocols (raising test-set tuning concerns), unreported split sizes and significance tests, outdated backbones, and omitted visual re-reading baselines.

J4Bt3A8fqi.one_liner: Mixes Gaussian-reweighted material-constituent latent routing with Transolver routing via a bounded gate for zero-shot PDE generalization.
J4Bt3A8fqi.problem: Neural PDE solvers struggle with zero-shot compositional generalization when physical material constituents seen separately during training appear together in a heterogeneous domain.
J4Bt3A8fqi.method: The authors introduce Conservative Compositional Routing for Material-Interface Guided Transolver (CCR-MIG), which forms per-constituent routing distributions over learned latent physical slices by Gaussian-kernel reweighting and normalization, combines them by local constituent influence, and blends the result with original Transolver routing via a learned bounded gate.
J4Bt3A8fqi.key_idea: Reweight Transolver's latent-slice routing per material constituent with permutation-invariant Gaussian kernels and blend it into original routing through a bounded gate.
J4Bt3A8fqi.evidence: Six-seed experiments on 2D elasticity and steady thermal conduction across rectangular, waisted, and perforated plates tested on 400 mixed-composition samples against Transolver variants.
J4Bt3A8fqi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree zero-shot heterogeneous material composition is a practical PDE problem and appreciate the clean feature-matched Transolver isolation and bounded-gating ablations.
J4Bt3A8fqi.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize statistically weak evidence (no main six-seed comparison survives Holm correction, adjusted p = 0.75, with averages skewed by single outlier runs) and narrow evaluation limited to simple 2D linear PDEs and Transolver baselines.

UvVcH7gP7m.one_liner: Decomposes auxiliary recommendation embeddings into target-associated SVD and null-space components with separate learned calibration gains.
UvVcH7gP7m.problem: Multi-behavior recommendation models struggle to extract complementary ranking evidence from auxiliary behaviors without distorting target-associated representations.
UvVcH7gP7m.method: The authors propose Target-referenced Null-space Calibration (TNC), a plug-in module that computes cross-covariance between paired auxiliary and target representations and extracts a target-associated subspace via truncated SVD. TNC preserves both the target-associated projection and its orthogonal null-space residual, learning separate calibration gains under target ranking supervision.
UvVcH7gP7m.key_idea: Split auxiliary behavior embeddings via cross-covariance truncated SVD into target-associated and orthogonal null-space components and learn separate ranking-supervised scaling gains for each.
UvVcH7gP7m.evidence: Joint training experiments inserting TNC into multiple multi-behavior recommendation backbones (including CRGCN, MBGCN, SpectraMB, and UIPL) across three real-world datasets with ablations.
UvVcH7gP7m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decoupled target-subspace and null-space calibration formulation intuitive and aligned with the distinction between target association and ranking value.
UvVcH7gP7m.main_concern: Reviewers point out that +TNC replaces native backbone fusion/scoring with mean fusion and inner products (confounding gains on CRGCN/MBGCN while yielding negligible or negative effects on SpectraMB/UIPL), lacks proof that orthogonal residuals carry complementary signal, and omits recent baselines.

recDs8ZqDA.one_liner: Decomposes any finite representation into a linear source-projection component and an orthogonal non-realizable remainder with a random null.
recDs8ZqDA.problem: Dimensionality reduction methods output lower-dimensional coordinates without quantifying how much of the representation is linearly realizable from the source versus irreducibly nonlinear.
recDs8ZqDA.method: The authors define the realizability decomposition via least squares and thin QR factorization, splitting a centered representation Z into a source-subspace projection and an orthogonal non-realizable remainder measured by normalized residual energy rho, calibrated against an analytic random-representation null.
recDs8ZqDA.key_idea: Orthogonally split a representation into its linear source-projection fit and non-realizable residual energy calibrated against an exact finite-sample random null.
recDs8ZqDA.evidence: Evaluated across nonlinear embeddings (such as t-SNE on image data) and deep layers with out-of-sample checks, seed variability, and random-representation nulls.
recDs8ZqDA.claimed_gains: On image data, the non-realizable remainder carries nearly all of a t-SNE layout's neighborhood quality while holding only 17% of its energy.
recDs8ZqDA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the careful calibration with an analytic random-representation null, explicit finite-sample caveats, and broad, consistent empirical measurements.
recDs8ZqDA.main_concern: Reviewers argue that the formal theory consists of elementary classical linear algebra (thin QR and multivariate regression R^2) restated as theorems, leaving theoretical novelty minimal.

3nM9KvVR6Q.one_liner: Measures label-free decision drift in continual LLM fine-tuning and regularizes stored teacher outputs via thresholded KL and margin losses.
3nM9KvVR6Q.problem: Accuracy alone hides catastrophic forgetting in continual LLM fine-tuning because newly repaired errors mask previously correct predictions that flip.
3nM9KvVR6Q.method: Tether tracks decision drift on stored real or synthetic input-output records without labels, derives an exact per-record forward-KL critical radius below which the recorded decision cannot flip, and introduces Tether-Margin and thresholded-KL (Tether-TKL) losses that are zero inside this safe region.
3nM9KvVR6Q.key_idea: Store teacher predictions on unlabeled records and regularize continual updates with losses zeroed inside the exact KL critical radius that preserves recorded decisions.
3nM9KvVR6Q.evidence: Theoretical critical-radius derivation plus experiments on 15-task O-LoRA sequences with T5-large and Llama-2-7B-chat against Replay and DER++.
3nM9KvVR6Q.claimed_gains: On 15-task O-LoRA sequences, Tether-KL matches DER++ final accuracy in the same training time while changing about half as many decisions without retaining labels.
3nM9KvVR6Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the label-free decision-drift metric is practically meaningful and that the closed-form forward-KL critical radius derivation is sharp and sound.
3nM9KvVR6Q.main_concern: Reviewers flag that the closest label-free baseline DER is omitted (comparing only against labelled DER++), Tether-KL outperforms the new Tether-TKL/Margin variants while taking longer to train, and experimental runs violate theoretical assumptions.

WqxYtZp7r1.one_liner: Separates candidate-set refinement from passage reading in agentic search via stateful lexical and set operations on an inverted index.
WqxYtZp7r1.problem: Agentic search tools return raw matching passages on every query, coupling candidate-set narrowing with heavy source-text exposure in the agent's context.
WqxYtZp7r1.method: IndexAct exposes an inverted-index interface where LLM agents build and combine persistent candidate sets via lexical filters and set operations, receiving reusable state handles and candidate counts while fetching full passages only on explicit request.
WqxYtZp7r1.key_idea: Provide persistent inverted-index candidate-set handles and count feedback so agents refine search states before selectively loading passage text.
WqxYtZp7r1.evidence: Evaluated training-free across five agentic search and multi-hop QA benchmarks (including BrowseComp-Plus, 2Wiki, and Bamboogle) using GPT-5.4nano.
WqxYtZp7r1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear motivation for decoupling candidate refinement from text inspection and the strong BrowseComp-Plus accuracy and context-size gains.
WqxYtZp7r1.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments use only one backbone (GPT-5.4nano) with single runs, several multi-hop QA gains amount to one question, and baseline/backend latency details are under-specified.
